## 致谢

<!--en-->
*Acknowledgments*

本书中列举的那些拙劣且狡诈的例子来源广泛，离不开诸多人的帮助。我通过美国统计协会发出呼吁后，一些专业统计学家——相信我，他们和任何人一样痛恨统计数据的滥用——从自己的收藏中寄来了相关素材。我想，这些人应该也不希望在此被提及姓名。我还在多本著作中找到了有价值的案例，主要包括：马丁·A·布鲁姆鲍和莱斯特·S·凯洛格所著的《商业统计学》；哈德利·坎特里尔所著的《民意测量》；威拉德·科普·布林顿所著的《图形展示》；弗雷德里克·E·克罗克斯顿和达德利·J·考登所著的《实用商业统计学》；乔治·辛普森和弗里茨·卡夫卡所著的《基础统计学》；以及海伦·M·沃克所著的《初级统计方法》。

<!--en-->
THE PRETTY little instances of bumbling and chicanery with which this book is peppered have been gathered widely and not without assistance. Following an appeal of mine through the American Statistical Association, a number of professional statisticians—who, believe me, deplore the misuse of statistics as heartily as anyone alive—sent me items from their own collections. These people, I guess, will be just as glad to remain nameless here. I found valuable specimens in a number of books too, primarily these: *Business Statistics*, by Martin A. Brumbaugh and Lester S. Kellogg; *Gauging Public Opinion*, by Hadley Cantril; *Graphic Presentation*, by Willard Cope Brinton; *Practical Business Statistics*, by Frederick E. Croxton and Dudley J. Cowden; *Basic Statistics*, by George Simpson and Fritz Kafka; and *Elementary Statistical Methods*, by Helen M. Walker.

# 引言

<!--en-->
*Introduction*

“这儿的犯罪活动可真不少啊，”我的岳父从爱荷华州搬到加利福尼亚州后不久说道。的确如此——至少在他读的报纸上是这样写的。那份报纸从不放过本地发生的任何犯罪事件，甚至对一起发生在爱荷华州的谋杀案的关注程度，超过了案发地区的主要日报。

<!--en-->
"THERE'S a mighty lot of crime around here," said my father-in-law a little while after he moved from Iowa to California. And so there was—in the newspaper he read. It is one that overlooks no crime in its own area and has been known to give more attention to an Iowa murder than was given by the principal daily in the region in which it took place.

我岳父的结论其实是一种非正式的统计推断。它基于一个严重有偏的样本。和许多更为复杂的统计数据一样，它也犯了“半依附谬误”：它假定报纸上关于犯罪的报道篇幅就能反映犯罪率的高低。

<!--en-->
My father-in-law's conclusion was statistical in an informal way. It was based on a sample, a remarkably biased one. Like many a more sophisticated statistic it was guilty of semiattachment: It assumed that newspaper space given to crime reporting is a measure of crime rate.

几个冬天前，十几位研究人员分别报告了关于抗组胺药的数据。结果显示，相当比例的感冒患者在服药后痊愈。至少在广告中，这引发了巨大轰动，进而催生了医药产品的热潮。这种热潮建立在永无止境的希望之上，也源于人们不愿透过统计数据去了解一个早已为人所知的事实。正如幽默作家而非医学权威的亨利·G·费尔森早就指出的那样：恰当的治疗能让感冒在七天内痊愈，但若不加以干预，感冒会持续一周之久。

<!--en-->
A few winters ago a dozen investigators independently reported figures on antihistamine pills. Each showed that a considerable percentage of colds cleared up after treatment. A great fuss ensued, at least in the advertisements, and a medical-product boom was on. It was based on an eternally springing hope and also on a curious refusal to look past the statistics to a fact that has been known for a long time. As Henry G. Felsen, a humorist and no medical authority, pointed out quite a while ago, proper treatment will cure a cold in seven days, but left to itself a cold will hang on for a week.

你读到和听到的很多内容都是如此。平均值、关联关系、趋势和图表并不总是表面上看起来的那样。它们背后可能隐藏着更多玄机，也可能其实没那么重要。

<!--en-->
So it is with much that you read and hear. Averages and relationships and trends and graphs are not always what they seem. There may be more in them than meets the eye, and there may be a good deal less.

统计学的“秘密语言”在注重事实的文化中极具吸引力，但它常被用来制造轰动效应、夸大其词、混淆视听或过度简化。在报告社会与经济趋势、商业状况、“民意”调查以及人口普查等海量数据时，统计方法和术语确实是必不可少的。但如果没有诚实且理解深刻的写作者，也没有能读懂其含义的读者，最终结果只能是毫无意义的废话。

<!--en-->
The secret language of statistics, so appealing in a fact-minded culture, isemployed to sensationalize, inflate, confuse, and oversimplify. Statistical methods and statistical terms are necessary in reporting the mass data of social and economic trends, business conditions, “opinion” polls, the census. But without writers who use the words with honesty and understanding and readers who know what they mean, the result can only be semantic nonsense.

在科普类文章中，被滥用的统计数据几乎要取代那种穿着白大褂、在昏暗实验室里无偿加班的英雄形象。就像“一点点粉末、一小罐颜料”一样，统计数据让许多重要事实“看起来并非真实面目”。精心包装的统计数据比希特勒的“弥天大谎”更厉害：它能误导人，却又无法归咎于你。

<!--en-->
In popular writing on scientific matters the abused statistic is almost crowding out the picture of the white-jacketed hero laboring overtime without time-and-a-half in an ill-lit laboratory. Like the “little dash of powder, little pot of paint,” statistics are making many an important fact “look like what she ain’t.” A well-wrapped statistic is better than Hitler’s “big lie”; it misleads, yet it cannot be pinned on you.

本书算是一份如何利用统计数据行骗的入门指南。它看起来或许很像骗子手册。或许我可以这样辩解：就像那位退休窃贼出版的回忆录实际上成了教授如何开锁和掩饰脚步声的课程一样——骗子们早已熟知这些伎俩；正直的人为了自卫必须学会它们。

<!--en-->
This book is a sort of primer in ways to use statistics to deceive. It may seem altogether too much like a manual for swindlers. Perhaps I can justify it in the manner of the retired burglar whose published reminiscences amounted to a graduate course in how to pick a lock and muffle a footfall: The crooks already know these tricks; honest men must learn them in self-defense.

# 第一章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 1*

## 内置偏置的样品

<!--en-->
*The Sample with the Built-in Bias*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2d78917609eafb1008b2a325796399c0.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=de57742c56f73275553a3f91f9023eaab75cc212dba615b578852d65a7f68d28)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2d78917609eafb1008b2a325796399c0.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=de57742c56f73275553a3f91f9023eaab75cc212dba615b578852d65a7f68d28)

《时代》杂志曾在一篇关于《纽约太阳报》文章的评论中写道：“2024届的普通耶鲁人，年均收入为25,111美元。”

<!--en-->
"THE AVERAGE Yaleman, Class of '24," *Time* magazine noted once, commenting on something in the New York Sun, "makes $25,111 a year."

嗯，这对他来说真是好事！

<!--en-->
Well, good for him!

但请稍等一分钟。这个惊人的数字意味着什么？它是否如表面所示，证明了如果你把儿子送去耶鲁大学，你和他晚年都不必再工作？

<!--en-->
But wait a minute. What does this impressive figure mean? Is it, as it appears to be, evidence that if you send your boy to Yale you won't have to work in your old age and neither will he?

乍一看，这个数据有两点格外引人注目。它出奇地精确。它的健康益处更是令人难以置信。

<!--en-->
Two things about the figure stand out at first suspicious glance. It is surprisingly precise. It is quite improbably salubrious.

任何偏远地区群体的平均收入被精确到美元的可能性微乎其微。除非收入完全来自工资，否则你也不太可能如此精确地知道去年自己的收入数额。而且，2.5万美元的收入往往并非全部来自工资；属于这一收入阶层的人很可能拥有分布广泛的投资。

<!--en-->
There is small likelihood that the average income of any far-flung group is ever going to be known down to the dollar. It is not particularly probable that you know your own income for last year so precisely as that unless it was allderived from salary. And $25,000 incomes are not often all salary; people in that bracket are likely to have well-scattered investments.

此外，这个令人称羡的平均值无疑是根据耶鲁大学的毕业生*声称*自己挣得的收入计算出来的。即便1924年纽黑文地区实行过诚信申报制度，我们也无法确定经过四分之一个世纪后，这些报告是否依然真实可靠。有些人被问及收入时会出于虚荣或乐观心理而夸大其词；另一些人则会刻意少报，尤其是在填报所得税申报表时；一旦这么做了，他们可能就不愿在其他文件上自相矛盾。谁知道税务局会查到什么程度呢？这两种倾向——吹嘘与少报——或许会相互抵消，但可能性不大。其中一种倾向很可能远比另一种强烈，而我们却无从知晓究竟是哪一种。

<!--en-->
Furthermore, this lovely average is undoubtedly calculated from the amounts the Yale men *said* they earned. Even if they had the honor system in New Haven in '24, we cannot be sure that it works so well after a quarter of a century that all these reports are honest ones. Some people when asked their incomes exaggerate out of vanity or optimism. Others minimize, especially, it is to be feared, on income-tax returns; and having done this may hesitate to contradict themselves on any other paper. Who knows what the revenuers may see? It is possible that these two tendencies, to boast and to understate, cancel each other out, but it is unlikely. One tendency may be far stronger than the other, and we do not know which one.

我们开始计算一个凭常识判断几乎无法反映真相的数字。现在，让我们找出造成最大误差的可能根源——这一根源竟能将某些男性的“平均收入”算作25,111美元，而他们的实际平均值很可能只有这个数字的一半左右。

<!--en-->
We have begun then to account for a figure that common sense tells us can hardly represent the truth. Now let us put our finger on the likely source of the biggest error, a source that can produce $25,111 as the “average income” of some men whose actual average may well be nearer half that amount.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/063db9c446d9fd1765204dad253ca2d1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=192ab424368c676c2d798ae4ed8ead7bc9de5db783af69f784a1e2647f6f4df2)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/063db9c446d9fd1765204dad253ca2d1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=192ab424368c676c2d798ae4ed8ead7bc9de5db783af69f784a1e2647f6f4df2)

这就是抽样程序，它构成了我们在各类主题中遇到的绝大部分统计数据的核心。其原理相当简单，尽管实际应用中的种种改进却衍生出了各种旁枝末节，其中一些甚至并不那么可靠。假设你有一桶豆子，有红色的也有白色的，要准确知道每种颜色的豆子各有多少，只有一种方法：逐一计数。不过，你也可以通过抓取一把豆子并数一数其中的红色豆子数量，来大致估算出红色豆子的比例——因为你认为整桶豆子中各颜色的比例是一致的。如果样本足够大且选取得当，对于大多数用途而言，它就能很好地代表整体情况。反之，这样的样本可能远不如凭直觉做出的猜测准确，除了徒有其表的科学精确感外别无长处。令人遗憾的事实是，我们读到或自认为知晓的许多结论，其实都源于这类存在偏差、样本量不足或两者兼有的样本。

<!--en-->
This is the sampling procedure, which is the heart of the greater part of the statistics you meet on all sorts of subjects. Its basis is simple enough, although its refinements in practice have led into all sorts of by-ways, some less than respectable. If you have a barrel of beans, some red and some white, there is only one way to find out exactly how many of each color you have: Count 'em. However, you can find out approximately how many are red in much easier fashion by pulling out a handful of beans and counting just those, figuring that the proportion will be the same all through the barrel. If your sample is large enough and selected properly, it will represent the whole well enough for most purposes. If it is not, it may be far less accurate than an intelligent guess and have nothing to recommend it but a spurious air of scientific precision. It is sad truth that conclusions from such samples, biased or too small or both, lie behind much of what we read or think we know.

关于耶鲁大学男生的报告是基于一个样本得出的。我们对此可以相当确定，因为常识告诉我们，没有人能够掌握该届1924年毕业生中所有在世成员的信息。二十五年后，肯定有很多人地址不详。

<!--en-->
The report on the Yale men comes from a sample. We can be pretty sure of that because reason tells us that no one can get hold of all the living membersof that class of '24. There are bound to be many whose addresses are unknown twenty-five years later.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/3ee28b69a64d67caed6ec5c9a7be9d21.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=ab5f5faa89bc3dc94c1828aebbba9689f7566eabd071169d528f707cf27d824f)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/3ee28b69a64d67caed6ec5c9a7be9d21.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=ab5f5faa89bc3dc94c1828aebbba9689f7566eabd071169d528f707cf27d824f)

而且，在那些地址已知的人中，许多人不会回复问卷，尤其是这种较为私人的问卷。对于某些类型的邮寄问卷而言，能有5%或10%的回复率就算相当高了。这份问卷的表现本应优于此，但绝不可能达到百分之百。

<!--en-->
And, of those whose addresses are known, many will not reply to a questionnaire, particularly a rather personal one. With some kinds of mail questionnaire, a five or ten per cent response is quite high. This one should have done better than that, but nothing like one hundred per cent.

因此我们发现，收入数据是基于一个样本得出的，该样本由所有地址已知且回答了问卷的班级成员组成。这是一个具有代表性的样本吗？也就是说，能否认为这一群体的收入与那些无法联系到或没有回复的人所组成的未纳入样本群体相当呢？

<!--en-->
So we find that the income figure is based on a sample composed of all class members whose addresses are known and who replied to the questionnaire. Is this a representative sample? That is, can this group be assumed to be equal in income to the unrepresented group, those who cannot be reached or who do not reply?

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9109bff711f5a42cdf01224e5e341653.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=50432f8b88a8188ed3fc382739fa19cdaf144d0ff1745a7400e456f22961546e)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9109bff711f5a42cdf01224e5e341653.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=50432f8b88a8188ed3fc382739fa19cdaf144d0ff1745a7400e456f22961546e)

那些在耶鲁校友录中被标记为“地址不详”的迷途羔羊究竟是谁呢？他们会是那些高收入者——华尔街人士、企业董事、制造业及公用事业高管吗？不；要获取富人的地址并不难。即便他们疏于与校友办公室保持联系，通过《美国名人录》及其他参考书籍仍能找到这个阶层中许多最富裕的成员。

<!--en-->
Who are the little lost sheep down in the Yale rolls as “address unknown”? Are they the big-income earners—the Wall Street men, the corporation directors, the manufacturing and utility executives? No; the addresses of the rich will not be hard to come by. Many of the most prosperous members of the class can be found through *Who's Who in America* and other reference volumes even if they have neglected to keep in touch with the alumni office.

可以合理推测，那些被遗忘的名字属于这样一群人：他们在获得耶鲁大学文学学士学位约二十五年后，仍未实现任何辉煌的成就。他们或是店员、机械师、流浪汉、失业的酒鬼，或是勉强糊口的作家和艺术家……需要六七个这样的人，其收入才能凑齐25,111美元。这些人并不常参加同学聚会，原因无非是他们负担不起路费。

<!--en-->
It is a good guess that the lost names are those of the men who, twenty-five years or so after becoming Yale bachelors of arts, have not fulfilled any shining promise. They are clerks, mechanics, tramps, unemployed alcoholics, barely surviving writers and artists ... people of whom it would take half a dozen or more to add up to an income of $25,111. These men do not so often register at class reunions, if only because they cannot afford the trip.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/6d47032027d9d6d538acfa61d633db8d.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4a18130195809eb90a67f45760c9b948740e0c32e1c24a42a47aabe767c62765)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/6d47032027d9d6d538acfa61d633db8d.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4a18130195809eb90a67f45760c9b948740e0c32e1c24a42a47aabe767c62765)

那些把问卷扔进最近垃圾桶的人是谁呢？我们对此无法完全确定，但至少可以合理推测：他们中的许多人收入微薄，根本不值得拿来炫耀。他们有点像那个在第一份工资单上发现一张便条的人——便条上建议他把薪资数额视为机密，不可用于办公室闲聊。“别担心，”他对老板说，“我和您一样为此感到羞愧。”

<!--en-->
Who are those who chucked the questionnaire into the nearest wastebasket? We cannot be so sure about these, but it is at least a fair guess that many of them are just not making enough money to brag about. They are a little like the fellow who found a note clipped to his first pay check suggesting that he consider the amount of his salary confidential and not material for the interchange of office confidences. “Don’t worry,” he told the boss. “I’m just as ashamed of it as you are.”

很明显，样本中遗漏了最有可能拉低平均值的两个群体。25,111美元这个数字的含义开始显现出来：如果它真的能代表什么的话，那也仅仅是代表那部分地址已知、且愿意站出来说明自己收入的2024届毕业生。即便如此，这也需要假设这些人说的是实话。

<!--en-->
It becomes pretty clear that the sample has omitted two groups most likely to depress the average. The $25,111 figure is beginning to explain itself. If it is a true figure for anything it is one merely for that special group of the class of ’24 whose addresses are known and who are willing to stand up and tell how much they earn. Even that requires an assumption that the gentlemen are telling the truth.

这样的假设绝不可轻率作出。从一种被称为市场调研的抽样研究中获得的经验表明，这种假设几乎根本无法成立。曾经进行过一项旨在调查杂志读者情况的逐户调查，其中的关键问题是：“您家阅读哪些杂志？”当结果被整理和分析后，发现很多人喜欢《哈珀斯》杂志，而阅读《真实故事》杂志的人则寥寥无几。当时出版商提供的数据显示，《真实故事》的发行量比《哈珀斯》多出数百万册之多，而《哈珀斯》的发行量仅为几十万册。或许我们问错了人，调查的设计者们自言自语道。但事实并非如此；这些问题是在全国各地各种社区中提出的。唯一合理的结论就是：许多受访者——即回答此类问题的人——并没有说实话。这项调查所揭示的不过是人们的势利心态罢了。

<!--en-->
Such an assumption is not to be made lightly. Experience from one breed of sampling study, that called market research, suggests that it can hardly ever be made at all. A house-to-house survey purporting to study magazine readership was once made in which a key question was: What magazines does your household read? When the results were tabulated and analyzed it appeared that a great many people loved *Harper’s* and not very many read *True Story*. Now there were publishers’ figures around at the time that showed very clearly that *True Story* had more millions of circulation than *Harper’s* had hundreds of thousands. Perhaps we asked the wrong kind of people, thedesigners of the survey said to themselves. But no, the questions had been asked in all sorts of neighborhoods all around the country. The only reasonable conclusion then was that a good many of the respondents, as people are called when they answer such questions, had not told the truth. About all the survey had uncovered was snobbery.

最终人们发现，如果你想了解某些人读了什么，询问他们是没有用的。你只需去他们家里，声称想买旧杂志，问问能买到些什么，就能了解到更多信息。然后你只需数一数那些《耶鲁评论》和《爱情小说》的数量即可。当然，即便这种可疑的手段也无法告诉你人们真正读了什么，只能说明他们接触过哪些读物。

<!--en-->
In the end it was found that if you wanted to know what certain people read it was no use asking them. You could learn a good deal more by going to their houses and saying you wanted to buy old magazines and what could be had? Then all you had to do was count the *Yale Reviews* and the *Love Romances*. Even that dubious device, of course, does not tell you what people read, only what they have been exposed to.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/6d4c4cd3cd39ab3cdb64a91016c1057c.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2139a3422f30cd69ec931d537edd980e032a04481bca9f657ddc3e3ba7faa561)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/6d4c4cd3cd39ab3cdb64a91016c1057c.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2139a3422f30cd69ec931d537edd980e032a04481bca9f657ddc3e3ba7faa561)

同样地，下次当你从阅读中得知“普通美国人”（如今关于他的传闻很多，其中大部分都难以置信）每天刷牙1.02次——这个数字是我凭空编造的，但也许和其他人的统计结果一样可靠——时，不妨问问自己：究竟是谁能查出这种数据呢？一个在无数广告中看到“不刷牙的人属于社交上的害群之马”这一说法的女性，会向陌生人承认自己并不经常刷牙吗？对于只想了解人们关于刷牙话题的说法的人来说，这个统计数据或许有意义；但它并不能真实反映牙刷接触门牙的频率。

<!--en-->
Similarly, the next time you learn from your reading that the average American (you hear a good deal about him these days, most of it faintly improbable) brushes his teeth 1.02 times a day—a figure I have just made up, but it may be as good as anyone else's—ask yourself a question. How can anyone have found out such a thing? Is a woman who has read in countless advertisements that nonbrushers are social offenders going to confess to a stranger that she does not brush her teeth regularly? The statistic may have meaning to one who wants to know only what people say about tooth-brushing but it does not tell a great deal about the frequency with which bristle is applied to incisor.

我们常被告知，河流无法高过其源头。不过，如果某处隐藏着泵站的话，它似乎就能做到这一点。同样真实的是：抽样研究的结果绝不会比其所依据的样本更好。当数据经过层层统计处理并被简化为带小数点的平均值时，其结果便开始呈现出一种令人信服的假象，而若仔细审视抽样过程，便会发现这种假象并不成立。

<!--en-->
A river cannot, we are told, rise above its source. Well, it can seem to if there is a pumping station concealed somewhere about. It is equally true that the result of a sampling study is no better than the sample it is based on. By the time the data have been filtered through layers of statistical manipulation and reduced to a decimal-pointed average, the result begins to take on an auraof conviction that a closer look at the sampling would deny.

早期发现癌症能挽救生命吗？也许吧。但用来证明这一点的常用数据，最多只能说它们并不能说明问题。康涅狄格州肿瘤登记处的记录可追溯至1935年，这些记录似乎显示从那一年到1941年间五年生存率有显著提高。实际上，这些记录始于1941年，更早的数据是通过回溯获得的。许多患者已经离开康涅狄格州，因此无法得知他们是否存活。据医学记者伦纳德·恩格尔称，由此产生的固有偏差“足以解释所宣称的生存率改善现象的绝大部分”。

<!--en-->
Does early discovery of cancer save lives? Probably. But of the figures commonly used to prove it the best that can be said is that they don't. These, the records of the Connecticut Tumor Registry, go back to 1935 and appear to show a substantial increase in the five-year survival rate from that year till 1941. Actually those records were begun in 1941, and everything earlier was obtained by tracing back. Many patients had left Connecticut, and whether they had lived or died could not be learned. According to the medical reporter Leonard Engel, the built-in bias thus created is “enough to account for nearly the whole of the claimed improvement in survival rate.”

一份基于抽样的报告要想具有较高价值，就必须使用具有代表性的样本——即已经消除了所有偏差来源的样本。而耶鲁大学的数据正是在这一点上显得毫无价值。同样，你在报纸和杂志上读到的许多内容也在此暴露出它们固有的无意义性。

<!--en-->
To be worth much, a report based on sampling must use a representative sample, which is one from which every source of bias has been removed. That is where our Yale figure shows its worthlessness. It is also where a great many of the things you can read in newspapers and magazines reveal their inherent lack of meaning.

一位精神病医生曾声称，几乎每个人都是神经质的。且不说这种用法会彻底破坏“神经质”一词的含义，我们不妨看看这位医生的样本究竟是什么。也就是说，他观察的是哪些人呢？原来，他是从自己的病人身上得出这一“精辟”结论的——而这些病人根本无法代表整个人群。如果一个人是正常的，这位精神病医生根本就不会见到他。

<!--en-->
A psychiatrist reported once that practically everybody is neurotic. Aside from the fact that such use destroys any meaning in the word “neurotic,” take a look at the man’s sample. That is, whom has the psychiatrist been observing? It turns out that he has reached this edifying conclusion from studying his patients, who are a long, long way from being a sample of the population. If a man were normal, our psychiatrist would never meet him.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/48912e2b56702201231df71cae195954.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=ad6691f768760a6d3c1a9aea4b06b1870bd7de50692581a1e699819afb545f21)

对读到的内容多审视一眼，你就能避免学到许多错误的信息。

<!--en-->
Give that kind of second look to the things you read, and you can avoid learning a whole lot of things that are not so.

同样值得记住的是：样本的可靠性既可能被明显的偏差源所破坏，也可能被隐蔽的偏差源所摧毁。也就是说，即便你找不到明显的偏差来源，只要存在偏差的可能性，就应对结果保持一定程度的怀疑——因为偏差总是存在的。1948年和1952年的总统选举足以证明这一点（如果还有人对此存疑的话）。

<!--en-->
It is worth keeping in mind also that the dependability of a sample can be destroyed just as easily by invisible sources of bias as by these visible ones. That is, even if you can't find a source of demonstrable bias, allow yourself some degree of skepticism about the results as long as there is a possibility of bias somewhere. There always is. The presidential elections in 1948 and 1952 were enough to prove that, if there were any doubt.

欲寻更多证据，可回溯到1936年《文学文摘》那场著名的惨败。那千万名电话用户及杂志订阅者向这家注定倒闭的杂志社保证：兰登将获得370张选举人票，罗斯福则得161张。这些人选自一份曾准确预测1932年选举结果的名单。既然这份名单已经过检验，怎还会有偏差呢？当然有偏差——大学论文及其他事后分析早已指出：1936年能负担得起电话和杂志订阅费的人并非选民的代表。从经济角度看，他们属于特殊群体；由于其中共和党选民比例偏高，该样本本身就存在偏差。最终该样本选出的是兰登，但选民们的想法却并非如此。

<!--en-->
For further evidence go back to 1936 and the *Literary Digest's* famed fiasco. The ten million telephone and *Digest* subscribers who assured the editors of the doomed magazine that it would be Landon 370, Roosevelt 161 came from the list that had accurately predicted the 1932 election. How could there be bias in a list already so tested? There was a bias, of course, as college theses and other post mortems found: People who could afford telephones and magazine subscriptions in 1936 were not a cross section of voters. Economically they were a special kind of people, a sample biased because it was loaded with what turned out to be Republican voters. The sample elected Landon, but the voters thought otherwise.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2597992ac680bbf2ee910235bf27cdab.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1327d93054e42801d3764c6f3484c5c83306e74210b10be872dd02e78e0c59e3)

最基本的样本类型被称为“随机样本”。它是从统计学家所称的“总体”（即样本所隶属的整体）中纯粹凭机会选取的。例如：从索引卡文件中每第十个名字抽取一个；从帽子里取出五十张纸条；在商业街上每第二十个人中选取一位进行访谈。（但请记住：最后这种样本并非世界人口、美国人口或旧金山人口的样本，而仅仅是当时在商业街上的人群样本。一位民意调查员称她是在火车站找人的，因为“火车站里什么人都有”。有人提醒她：比如小孩的母亲可能在那里被严重低估了。）

<!--en-->
The basic sample is the kind called “random.” It is selected by pure chance from the “universe,” a word by which the statistician means the whole of which the sample is a part. Every tenth name is pulled from a file of index cards. Fifty slips of paper are taken from a hatful. Every twentieth person met on Market Street is interviewed. (But remember that this last is not a sample of the population of the world, or of the United States, or of San Francisco, but only of the people on Market Street at the time. One interviewer for an opinion poll said that she got her people in a railroad station because “all kinds of people can be found in a station.” It had to be pointed out to her that mothers of small children, for instance, might be underrepresented there.)

随机样本的检验标准是：总体中的每一个个体是否有同等机会被选入样本？

<!--en-->
The test of the random sample is this: Does every name or thing in the whole group have an equal chance to be in the sample?

纯随机样本是唯一能凭借统计理论完全可信地加以分析的样本类型，但它有一个缺陷：获取它的成本极高、难度极大，以至于实际运用中往往因成本问题而被排除。在民意调查和市场研究等领域普遍采用的更经济的替代方法，叫做分层随机抽样。

<!--en-->
The purely random sample is the only kind that can be examined with entire confidence by means of statistical theory, but there is one thing wrong with it. It is so difficult and expensive to obtain for many uses that sheer cost eliminates it. A more economical substitute, which is almost universally used in such fields as opinion polling and market research, is called stratified random sampling.

要获得这种分层样本，需按已知比例将总体划分为若干组。麻烦也就由此开始：你对各组比例的了解可能并不准确。你会指示调查员确保与一定数量的非裔美国人、不同收入阶层的人交谈，还要访问指定数量的农民等等。同时，各组内40岁以上与40岁以下的人数必须相等。

<!--en-->
To get this stratified sample you divide your universe into several groups inproportion to their known prevalence. And right there your trouble can begin: Your information about their proportion may not be correct. You instruct your interviewers to see to it that they talk to so many blacks and such-and-such a percentage of people in each of several income brackets, to a specified number of farmers, and so on. All the while the group must be divided equally between persons over forty and under forty years of age.

听起来不错——但实际会怎样呢？关于种族问题，调查员大多能正确判断；但在收入方面，他们容易出错。至于农民——如何界定那些兼职务农又在城市工作的人呢？就连年龄问题也会带来麻烦，最简单的解决办法是只选择明显未满40岁或超过40岁的受访者。这样一来，样本就会因缺少30多岁和40岁出头的人群而产生偏差。总之，你无法两全其美。

<!--en-->
That sounds fine—but what happens? On the question of black or white the interviewer will judge correctly most of the time. On income he will make more mistakes. As to farmers—how do you classify a man who farms part time and works in the city too? Even the question of age can pose some problems which are most easily settled by choosing only respondents who obviously are well under or well over forty. In that case the sample will be biased by the virtual absence of the late-thirties and early-forties age groups. You can’t win.

除此之外，如何在分层内获得随机样本呢？最直观的做法是先从所有人名单中随机抽选：但这成本太高。于是你走上街头——结果样本便偏向那些不出门的人。白天挨家挨户访问——又会漏掉大多数上班族。改在晚上访谈——又忽略了看电影的人和夜店常客。

<!--en-->
On top of all this, how do you get a random sample within the stratification? The obvious thing is to start with a list of everybody and go after names chosen from it at random: but that is too expensive. So you go into the streets—and bias your sample against stay-at-homes. You go from door to door by day—and miss most of the employed people. You switch to evening interviews—and neglect the movie-goers and night-clubbers.

民意调查的运作归根结底是一场与偏差来源的持续斗争，所有信誉良好的调查机构都在时刻进行这场斗争。阅读报告的人必须记住：这场斗争永远不会取得最终胜利。任何诸如“67%的美国民众反对某事物”之类的结论，都应带着这样的疑问去解读：这67%究竟是指哪些美国人？

<!--en-->
The operation of a poll comes down in the end to a running battle against sources of bias, and this battle is conducted all the time by all the reputable polling organizations. What the reader of the reports must remember is that the battle is never won. No conclusion that “sixty-seven per cent of the American people are against” something or other should be read without the lingering question, Sixty-seven per cent of which American people?

阿尔弗雷德·C·金赛博士的“女性卷”也是如此。与所有基于抽样的调查一样，问题在于如何解读它（或其通俗摘要），而不至于误信那些未必属实的内容。其中至少涉及三个层次的抽样：金赛博士选取的人口样本（第一层）远非随机，代表性可能也有限；但与他之前该领域的研究相比，这些样本规模庞大，因此即便其数据未必完全准确，仍具有揭示性且重要。更重要的是要记住：任何问卷都只是可能提出的问题中的一个样本（第二层）；而受访者给出的答案，也不过是她对每个问题的态度和经历的一个样本（第三层）。

<!--en-->
So with Dr. Alfred C. Kinsey’s “female volume.” The problem, as with anything based on sampling, is how to read it (or a popular summary of it) without learning too much that is not necessarily so. There are at least three levels of sampling involved. Dr. Kinsey’s samples of the population (one level) are far from random ones and may not be particularly representative, but they are enormous samples by comparison with anything done in his field before and his figures must be accepted as revealing and important if not necessarily on the nose. It is possibly more important to remember that any questionnaire is only a sample (another level) of the possible questions and that the answer the lady gives is no more than a sample (third level) of her attitudes and experiences on each question.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/cc1c1f642566798a2baacd75e1a7d3e0.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a6fdc241a0187b6153cbeda0a6485d3edb1efda96da5137d52547d2e9ac1afe2)

访谈人员的构成方式可能会以有趣的方式影响调查结果。几年前战争期间，国家舆论研究中心派出了两组访谈员，向南方某城市中的500名黑人询问三个问题。一组由白人访谈员组成，另一组则由黑人访谈员组成。

<!--en-->
The kind of people who make up the interviewing staff can shade the result in an interesting fashion. Some years ago, during the war, the National Opinion Research Center sent out two staffs of interviewers to ask three questions of five hundred blacks in a Southern city. White interviewers made up one staff, blacks the other.

其中一个问题是：“如果日本人占领了美国，黑人在这里的待遇会变得更好还是更差？”黑人访谈员报告称，9%的受访者回答“更好”；而白人访谈员只发现2%的人这样回答。此外，黑人访谈员发现仅有25%的人认为黑人待遇会更差，白人访谈员则发现这一比例为45%。

<!--en-->
One question was, “Would blacks be treated better or worse here if the Japanese conquered the U.S.A.?” Black interviewers reported that nine per cent of those they asked said “better.” White interviewers found only two per cent of such responses. And while black interviewers found only twenty-five per cent who thought blacks would be treated worse, white interviewers turned up forty-five per cent.

当问题中将“日本人”替换为“纳粹”时，结果类似。

<!--en-->
When “Nazis” was substituted for “Japanese” in the question, the results were similar.

第三个问题旨在探究可能基于前两个问题所揭示的情感而产生的态度。“你认为优先击败轴心国更重要，还是让国内的民主制度运转得更好更重要？”根据黑人访谈员的记录，39%的人选择“击败轴心国”；而白人访谈员记录的比例则高达62%。

<!--en-->
The third question probed attitudes that might be based on feelings revealed by the first two. “Do you think it is more important to concentrate on beating the Axis, or to make democracy work better here at home?” “Beat Axis” was the reply of thirty-nine per cent, according to the black interviewers; of sixty-two per cent, according to the white.

这里便引入了未知因素造成的偏差。最有可能起作用的因素，是在解读民意调查结果时必须始终考虑的一种倾向——即人们倾向于给出讨人喜欢的答案。试想一下，在战时面对带有不忠意味的问题时，一个南方黑人会向白人说出听起来顺耳而非真实想法的话，这难道奇怪吗？另外，不同组的访谈员也可能选择了不同类型的人进行交谈。

<!--en-->
Here is bias introduced by unknown factors. It seems likely that the most effective factor was a tendency that must always be allowed for in reading poll results, a desire to give a pleasing answer. Would it be any wonder if, when answering a question with connotations of disloyalty in wartime, a Southern black would tell a white man what sounded good rather than what he actually believed? It is also possible that the different groups of interviewers chose different kinds of people to talk to.

无论如何，这些结果显然存在严重偏差，以至于毫无价值。你可以自行判断还有多少基于民意调查的结论同样存在偏差、同样毫无价值——只是没有途径能揭露它们罢了。

<!--en-->
In any case the results are obviously so biased as to be worthless. You can judge for yourself how many other poll-based conclusions are just as biased, just as worthless —but with no check available to show them up.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/4436f0607ab3865642996540521ecdfd.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5f70b89425bb419e8540a2074dd7a71f1c69f81759c8e31aaeaba3848f257981)

如果你怀疑民意调查普遍存在某种特定方向的偏差，即《文学文摘》式的错误方向，那么你就有相当充分的依据。这种偏差表现为：被调查者往往比其所代表的平均人群拥有更多金钱、更高教育水平、更多信息与敏锐度、更好的外貌、更循规蹈矩的行为方式，以及更固定的生活习惯。

<!--en-->
You have pretty fair evidence to go on if you suspect that polls in general are biased in one specific direction, the direction of the *Literary Digest* error. This bias is toward the person with more money, more education, more information and alertness, better appearance, more conventional behavior, and more settled habits than the average of the population he is chosen to represent.

你很容易理解造成这种现象的原因。假设你是一名被派往街角的访谈员，只需完成一次访谈。你看到两名似乎符合要求的男性：年龄超过四十岁，且居住在城市。一人衣着整洁、举止得体；另一人则衣衫肮脏、神情阴沉。由于有任务在身，你自然会选择看起来更合适的人交谈，而全国各地的同事也会做出类似决定。

<!--en-->
You can easily see what produces this. Let us say that you are aninterviewer assigned to a street corner, with one interview to get. You spot two men who seem to fit the category you must complete: over forty, and urban. One is in clean clothes, neat. The other is dirty and he looks surly. With a job to get done, you approach the more likely-looking fellow, and your colleagues all over the country are making similar decisions.

对民意调查最强烈的批评来自自由派或左翼圈子，他们普遍认为民意调查往往被操纵。这种观点背后的原因是：调查结果常常与那些非保守派人士的观点和愿望不符。他们指出，民意调查似乎总能选出共和党人，尽管随后选民的投票结果往往并非如此。

<!--en-->
Some of the strongest feeling against public-opinion polls is found in liberal or left-wing circles, where it is rather commonly believed that polls are generally rigged. Behind this view is the fact that poll results so often fail to square with the opinions and desires of those whose thinking is not in the conservative direction. Polls, they point out, seem to elect Republicans even when voters shortly thereafter do otherwise.

实际上，正如我们所见，民意调查并不一定要被人为操纵——即不必故意扭曲结果以制造虚假印象。样本本身在这种一致方向上的偏差就足以自动导致结果失真。

<!--en-->
Actually, as we have seen, it is not necessary that a poll be rigged—that is, that the results be deliberately twisted in order to create a false impression. The tendency of the sample to be biased in this consistent direction can rig it automatically.

# 第二章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 2*

## 精心挑选的平均值

<!--en-->
*The Well - Chosen Average*

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/bc3a83c016fe111bbb210d4f8af80ab5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=b01f6e98e7c6c1b22b9d71d42f434aba702cc929b0749c619a9b3854138b40f3)

我相信你并非势利之徒，而我当然也不从事房地产行业。但假设你是，我也是，而且你正在寻找一处位于我居住的加利福尼亚山谷附近道路旁的房产。

<!--en-->
You, I trust, are not a snob, and I certainly am not in the real-estate business. But let's say that you are and I am, and that you are looking for property to buy along a road that is not far from the California valley in which I live.

在打量了你一番后，我特意告诉你：这个社区的平均年收入约为15,000美元。或许这能激起你在此居住的兴趣；总之，你买下了那处房产，那个诱人的数字便铭刻在你心中。既然我们已约定暂时假定你是个有点势利的人，你很可能会在向朋友谈及住处时随口提起这个数字。

<!--en-->
Having sized you up, I take pains to tell you that the average income in this neighborhood is some $15,000 a year. Maybe that clinches your interest in living here; anyway, you buy and that handsome figure sticks in your mind. More than likely, since we have agreed that for the purposes of the moment you are a bit of a snob, you toss it in casually when telling your friends about where you live.

大约一年后我们再次相遇。作为某个纳税人委员会的成员，我正在发起请愿，要求降低税率、评估额或公交车费。我恳求大家理解：我们实在负担不起这些增加的费用——毕竟，该社区的平均年收入仅为3,500美元。也许你会支持我和委员会的主张——你不仅势利，还吝啬——但你听到那区区3,500美元的数字时，难免会感到惊讶。我现在是在撒谎，还是去年就在撒谎呢？

<!--en-->
A year or so later we meet again. As a member of some taxpayers' committee I am circulating a petition to keep the tax rate down or assessmentsdown or bus fare down. My plea is that we cannot afford the increase: After all, the average income in this neighborhood is only $3,500 a year. Perhaps you go along with me and my committee in this—you're not only a snob, you're stingy too—but you can't help being surprised to hear about that measly $3,500. Am I lying now, or was I lying last year?

无论何时你都无法指责我。这正是用统计数据来撒谎的精妙之处：这两个数字都是合法得出的合理平均值，它们代表相同的数据、相同的人群和相同的收入。然而显而易见的是，其中至少有一个数字具有极大的误导性，简直堪比赤裸裸的谎言。

<!--en-->
You can't pin it on me either time. That is the essential beauty of doing your lying with statistics. Both those figures are legitimate averages, legally arrived at. Both represent the same data, the same people, the same incomes. All the same it is obvious that at least one of them must be so misleading as to rival an out-and-out lie.

我的窍门在于每次使用不同类型的平均值，因为“平均值”一词的含义极为宽泛。这种伎俩常被那些想影响公众舆论或出售广告位的人所利用，有时出于无意，但往往别有用心。当你听说某数据是平均值时，除非能弄清它属于均值、中位数还是众数，否则你仍无法了解其全貌。

<!--en-->
My trick was to use a different kind of average each time, the word “average” having a very loose meaning. It is a trick commonly used, sometimes in innocence but often in guilt, by fellows wishing to influence public opinion or sell advertising space. When you are told that something is an average you still don't know very much about it unless you can find out which of the common kinds of average it is—mean, median, or mode.

我用来强调数字庞大的15,000美元其实是均值，即该社区所有家庭收入的算术平均数。它是通过将所有收入相加后再除以家庭数量得出的。较小的那个数字则是中位数，它表明一半家庭年收入超过3,500美元，另一半则低于此数。我本也可以使用众数，即一组数据中出现频率最高的数值。如果在该社区中，年收入为5,000美元的家庭数量最多，那么5,000美元就是众数收入。

<!--en-->
The $15,000 figure I used when I wanted a big one is a mean, the arithmetic average of the incomes of all the families in the neighborhood. You get it by adding up all the incomes and dividing by the number there are. The smaller figure is a median, and so it tells you that half the families in question have more than $3,500 a year and half have less. I might also have used the mode, which is the most frequently met-with figure in a series. If in this neighborhood there are more families with incomes of $5,000 a year than with any other amount, $5,000 a year is the modal income.

在这种情况下，正如收入数据通常呈现的特点一样，不加限定的“平均值”几乎毫无意义。加剧混乱的一个因素是：对于某些类型的信息而言，各种平均值彼此非常接近，以至于出于日常用途考虑，区分它们可能并不重要。

<!--en-->
In this case, as usually is true with income figures, an unqualified “average” is virtually meaningless. One factor that adds to the confusion is that with some kinds of information all the averages fall so close together that, for casual purposes, it may not be vital to distinguish among them.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/34e088fd5a999cbfc49f4ca594f53b42.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a16586d064d7bf560d9d04475cfd50449e99583cc0665173090198f8daa82cda)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/34e088fd5a999cbfc49f4ca594f53b42.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a16586d064d7bf560d9d04475cfd50449e99583cc0665173090198f8daa82cda)

如果你读到某群体的男性平均身高仅为五英尺，你就能大致了解这些人的身材情况。你无需追问该平均值是均值、中位数还是众数；结果都相差无几。（当然，如果你从事为这些男性生产工作服的行业，仅靠平均值提供的信息远远不够。这与数据的范围和偏差有关，我们将在下一章详细探讨。）

<!--en-->
If you read that the average height of the men of some group of people is only five feet, you get a fairly good idea of the stature of these people. You don't have to ask whether that average is a mean, median, or mode; it would come out about the same. (Of course, if you are in the business of manufacturing overalls for these men you would want more information than can be found in any average. This has to do with ranges and deviations, and well tackle that one in the next chapter.)

当处理诸如人类特征等遵循正态分布规律的数据时，不同平均值会彼此接近。若绘制曲线表示，会呈现出钟形，此时均值、中位数和众数重合于一点。

<!--en-->
The different averages come out close together when you deal with data, such as those having to do with many human characteristics, that have the grace to fall close to what is called the normal distribution. If you draw a curve to represent it you get something shaped like a bell, and mean, median, and mode fall at the same point.

因此，描述男性身高时，一种平均值与另一种同样适用；但描述他们的收入状况时则不然。如果你列出某个城市所有家庭的年收入，可能会发现收入范围从极低水平到约50,000美元不等，其中还会有少数极高收入者。超过95%的家庭收入低于10,000美元，这使得数据分布明显偏向左侧。其形状并非对称的钟形，而是呈偏态分布，类似儿童滑梯：梯子部分急剧上升到达顶点，滑行部分则缓缓下降。此时均值会与中位数相去甚远。由此可见，用某一年的“平均值”（均值）与另一年的“平均值”（中位数）进行比较，其有效性将大打折扣。

<!--en-->
Consequently one kind of average is as good as another for describing the heights of men, but for describing their pocketbooks it is not. If you should list the annual incomes of all the families in a given city you might find that they ranged from not much to perhaps $50,000 or so, and you might find a few very large ones. More than ninety-five per cent of the incomes would be under $10,000, putting them way over toward the left-hand side of the curve. Instead of being symmetrical, like a bell, it would be skewed. Its shape would be a little like that of a child's slide, the ladder rising sharply to a peak, the working part sloping gradually down. The mean would be quite a distance from the median. You can see what this would do to the validity of any comparison made between the "average" (mean) of one year and the "average" (median) of another.

在我向你出售房产的那个社区里，这两个平均值相差极大，因为收入分布严重偏斜。实际上，你的邻居大多是小农、在附近村庄打工的雇员，或是领取养老金的退休人员。但有三位居民是拥有百万资产的周末度假者，他们极大地拉高了总收入，从而也拉高了算术平均值。这一数值远远高于社区中绝大多数人的收入。实际上，这就出现了一种看似玩笑或比喻的情况：几乎每个人的收入都低于平均水平。

<!--en-->
In the neighborhood where I sold you some property the two averages are particularly far apart because the distribution is markedly skewed. It happens that most of your neighbors are small farmers or wage earners employed in a near-by village or elderly retired people on pensions. But three of the inhabitants are millionaire week-enders and these three boost the total income, and therefore the arithmetic average, enormously. They boost it to a figure that practically everybody in the neighborhood has a good deal less than. You have in reality the case that sounds like a joke or a figure of speech: Nearly everybody is below average.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/d1686ffb9630f3da1e33d1d44738eb9f.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7da96d894ffb8e937c886a56a4955f6fa0c601b1bcef53a7802d1028e9871242)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/d1686ffb9630f3da1e33d1d44738eb9f.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7da96d894ffb8e937c886a56a4955f6fa0c601b1bcef53a7802d1028e9871242)

这就是为什么当你看到企业高管或业主宣称其员工的平均工资为某一数值时，这个数字可能具有参考价值，也可能没有。如果这个平均值是中位数，你就能从中获得重要信息：一半员工收入高于该数值，另一半则低于它。但如果它是均值（相信我，如果未说明其性质的话很可能就是均值），那么你得到的可能只是老板本人4.5万美元的收入与一群低薪员工的工资的平均值而已。“年均工资5,700美元”这一数字背后，可能隐藏着2,000美元的员工薪资以及老板以高额薪水形式获取的利润。

<!--en-->
That's why when you read an announcement by a corporation executive or a business proprietor that the average pay of the people who work in his establishment is so much, the figure may mean something and it may not. If the average is a median, you can learn something significant from it: Half the employees make more than that; half make less. But if it is a mean (and believe me it may be that if its nature is unspecified) you may be getting nothing more revealing than the average of one $45,000 income—the proprietor's—and the salaries of a crew of underpaid workers. "Average annual pay of $5,700" may conceal both the $2,000 salaries and the owner's profits taken in the form of a whopping salary.

让我们更深入地看看这一点。对页展示了不同收入档次的人数分布情况。老板或许愿意用“平均工资5,700美元”这样的说法来描述情况——利用这种具有误导性的均值。然而，众数更能揭示真相：该行业最常见的年薪为2,000美元。和往常一样，中位数比任何其他单一数字都能更准确地反映实际情况：一半人年收入超过3,000美元，另一半则低于此数。

<!--en-->
Let's take a longer look at that one. The facing page shows how many people get how much. The boss might like to express the situation as "average wage $5,700"—using that deceptive mean. The mode, however, is more revealing: most common rate of pay in this business is $2,000 a year. As usual, the median tells more about the situation than any other single figure does; half the people get more than $3,000 and half get less.

某些公司报表如何将这一原理巧妙地运用为一种“颠倒黑白”的手段——情况越糟糕，数据看起来却越好，这一点可见一斑。让我们试着简单模拟一下。

<!--en-->
How neatly this can be worked into a whipsaw device in which the worse the story, the better it looks is illustrated in some company statements. Let's try our hand at one in a small way.

你是拥有一家小型制造企业的三位合伙人之一。

<!--en-->
You are one of the three partners who own a small manufacturing business.

现在是一年的尾声，业绩相当不错。你已向负责生产和运送椅子或其他产品的90名员工支付了198,000美元的工资。你与合伙人各自领取了11,000美元的薪水。你发现全年利润为45,000美元，需由你们三人平分。你将如何描述这一情况呢？为了便于理解，你选择用平均值来表示。由于所有员工从事类似工作且薪酬相近，使用均值还是中位数并无太大区别。最终结果如下：

<!--en-->
It is now the end of a very good year. You have paid out $198,000 to the ninety employees who do the work of making and shipping the chairs or whatever it is that you manufacture. You and your partners have paid yourselves $11,000 each in salaries. You find there are profits for the year of $45,000 to be divided equally among you. How are you going to describe this? To make it easy to understand, you put it in the form of averages. Since all the employees are doing about the same kind of work for similar pay, it won't make much difference whether you use a mean or a median. This is what you come out with:

员工平均工资 .................... 2,200美元

<!--en-->
Average wage of employees .................... $ 2,200

业主的平均薪水及利润 ............ 26,000美元

<!--en-->
Average salary and profit of owners ............ 26,000

这看起来很糟糕，对吧？让我们换一种方式来表达。

<!--en-->
That looks terrible, doesn't it? Let's try it another way.

模式（最常见的情况）：从利润中提取3万美元，作为奖金分给三位合伙人。这次在计算平均工资时，要把你自己和合伙人也包含在内。务必使用平均值。

<!--en-->
MODE (occurs most frequently)
Take $30,000 of the profits and distribute it among the three partners as bonuses. And this time when you average up the wages, include yourself and your partners. And be sure to use a mean.

<table><tr><td>平均工资或薪金</td><td>$ 2,806.45</td></tr><tr><td>所有者的平均利润</td><td>5,000.00</td></tr></table>

<!--en-->
<table><tr><td>Average wage or salary</td><td>$ 2,806.45</td></tr><tr><td>Average profit of owners</td><td>5,000.00</td></tr></table>

啊，这样看起来好多了。虽然不如你原本能呈现的效果那么完美，但也足够好了。用于支付工资和利润的资金中，只有不到6%被分配到了利润项，如果你愿意的话，还可以进一步展示这一点。总之，你现在有了可以公布、张贴在公告栏上或用于谈判的数据。

<!--en-->
Ah. That looks better. Not as good as you could make it look, but good enough. Less than six per cent of the money available for wages and profits has gone into profits, and you can go further and show that too if you like. Anyway, you've got figures now that you can publish, post on a bulletin board, or use in bargaining.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/0eb710400d24f1a8b9320c4f71c2a219.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=446e8e34f57fa41ab5be4f7b5294924757ea4c24af51e18886ea251a7f5722b8)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/0eb710400d24f1a8b9320c4f71c2a219.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=446e8e34f57fa41ab5be4f7b5294924757ea4c24af51e18886ea251a7f5722b8)

这个例子相当粗糙，因为被简化了，但它跟那些打着会计旗号行骗的行为相比根本算不了什么。对于一家结构复杂的公司来说，从初级打字员到拿着数十万美元奖金的总裁，各种层级的人员都能通过这种方式掩盖真相。

<!--en-->
This is pretty crude because the example is simplified, but it is nothing to what has been done in the name of accounting. Given a complex corporation with hierarchies of employees ranging all the way from beginning typist to president with a several-hundred-thousand-dollar bonus, all sorts of things can be covered up in this manner.

所以当你看到某个平均工资数字时，首先要问：这是针对什么的平均值？包含了哪些人？美国钢铁公司曾称，其员工在1940年至1948年间的周平均收入增长了107%。确实如此——但如果你注意到1940年的数据中包含大量兼职人员，这种惊人的增长势头就会大打折扣。如果你一年做半职工作，下一年做全职工作，你的收入会翻倍，但这根本无法反映你的实际工资水平。

<!--en-->
So when you see an average-pay figure, first ask: Average of what? Who's included? The United States Steel Corporation once said that its employees average weekly earnings went up 107 per cent between 1940 and 1948. So they did—but some of the punch goes out of the magnificent increase when you note that the 1940 figure includes a much larger number of partially employed people. If you work half-time one year and full-time the next, your earnings will double, but that doesn't indicate anything at all about your wage rate.

你可能在报纸上读到过，1949年美国普通家庭的收入为3,100美元。除非你了解这里所说的“家庭”具体指什么，以及这是哪种类型的平均值，否则不应过分看重这个数字。（还有，谁说的？他凭什么知道？这个数字有多准确？）

<!--en-->
You may have read in the paper that the income of the average American family was $3,100 in 1949. You should not try to make too much out of thatfigure unless you also know what “family” has been used to mean, as well as what kind of average this is. (And who says so and how he knows and how accurate the figure is.)

这个数字恰好来自人口普查局。如果你有该局的报告，就能轻松找到所需的其他信息：这是一个中位数；“家庭”指的是“两个或两个以上有亲属关系且共同生活的人”。（如果把独居者也算进去，中位数就会降至2,700美元，差别很大。）通过查阅表格你还会发现，这一数字是基于一个样本量足够大的调查得出的；二十次中有十九次，四舍五入前的估计值3,107美元会在±59美元的误差范围内准确无误。

<!--en-->
This one happens to have come from the Bureau of the Census. If you have the Bureau’s report you’ll have no trouble finding the rest of the information you need right there: This is a median; “family” signifies “two or more persons related to each other and living together.” (If persons living alone are included in the group the median slips to $2,700, which is quite different.) You will also learn if you read back into the tables that the figure is based on a sample of such size that there are nineteen chances out of twenty that the estimate—$3,107 before it was rounded—is correct within a margin of $59 plus or minus.

这种概率和误差范围加起来便构成了相当可靠的估计。人口普查局既有足够的技术能力，也有充足的资金来确保其抽样调查达到较高的精确度。想必他们并无特别的偏袒之心。不过，并非你看到的所有数字都诞生于如此理想的条件之下，也并非所有数字都附带说明其精确程度的信息。我们将在下一章详细探讨这个问题。

<!--en-->
That probability and that margin add up to a pretty good estimate. The Census people have both skill enough and money enough to bring their sampling studies down to a fair degree of precision. Presumably they have no particular axes to grind. Not all the figures you see are born under such happy circumstances, nor are all of them accompanied by any information at all to show how precise or unprecise they may be. We’ll work that one over in the next chapter.

与此同时，你或许想对《时代》杂志中“出版商来信”栏目里的一些内容试试自己的怀疑精神。文中提到新订阅者的“中位年龄为34岁，家庭年均收入为7,270美元”。而此前对老订户的调查显示，他们的“中位年龄为41岁……平均收入为9,535美元……”自然而然会有人问：既然两次调查都给出了年龄的中位数，为何收入的平均值却未被明确说明？难道是因为使用了更大的均值，从而在广告商面前显得读者群体更富裕吗？

<!--en-->
Meanwhile you may want to try your skepticism on some items from “A Letter from the Publisher” in *Time* magazine. Of new subscribers it said, “Their median age is 34 years and their average family income is $7,270 a year.” An earlier survey of “old TIMErs” had found that their “median age was 41 years.... Average income was $9,535....” The natural question is why, when median is given for ages both times, the kind of average for incomes is carefully unspecified. Could it be that the mean was used instead because it is bigger, thus seeming to dangle a richer readership before advertisers?

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/690ee1bb800fb5072234b7ffe3536cd1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5434734f20a798d86e4a8219fbd0156716d7f035875f9d8066a50d3dbcca1800)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/690ee1bb800fb5072234b7ffe3536cd1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5434734f20a798d86e4a8219fbd0156716d7f035875f9d8066a50d3dbcca1800)

你还可以试着对第一章开头提到的1924年耶鲁大学所谓的繁荣景象，分析一下它究竟属于哪种类型的平均值。

<!--en-->
You might also try a game of what-kind-of-average-are-you on the alleged prosperity of the 1924 Yales reported at the beginning of Chapter 1.

# 第三章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 3*

## 那些不存在的微小数字

<!--en-->
*The Little Figures That Are Not There*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/1fd255ab08354520649404ff9b792d5c.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7edca87b81795cc982d13ca279262a8df239add190515e983806118658b72705)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/1fd255ab08354520649404ff9b792d5c.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7edca87b81795cc982d13ca279262a8df239add190515e983806118658b72705)

章节

<!--en-->
CHAPTER

大字标题宣称：使用Doakes牙膏后，蛀牙数量减少了23%。你当然希望自己也能少受23%的牙痛困扰，于是继续读下去。你会发现，这些结果来自一家令人放心的“独立”实验室，且数据还经过了注册会计师的认证。你还想要什么呢？

<!--en-->
USERS report 23% fewer cavities with Doakes' tooth paste, the big type says. You could do with twenty-three per cent fewer aches so you read on. These results, you find, come from a reassuringly "independent" laboratory, and the account is certified by a certified public accountant. What more do you want?

然而，如果你不是特别容易轻信或过于乐观的话，就会凭经验想起：一种牙膏很少会比其他牙膏好多少。那么Doakes公司怎能得出这样的结果呢？他们能靠撒谎蒙混过关吗，而且还是用这么大的字体印刷？其实不必如此。有更简单也更有效的方法。

<!--en-->
Yet if you are not outstandingly gullible or optimistic, you will recall from experience that one tooth paste is seldom much better than any other. Then how can the Doakes people report such results? Can they get away with telling lies, and in such big type at that? No, and they don't have to. There are easier ways and more effective ones.

这里最大的“玩笑”在于样本量不足——从统计学角度看确实如此；但对多克斯而言，这个样本量刚好合适。细读文中小字说明你会发现，那组测试用户仅有区区十几人。（不得不承认，多克斯还算仁慈，给了你一个公平的机会。有些广告商甚至会隐瞒这一信息，让即便是精通统计的人也只能猜测其中究竟有何猫腻。不过就这类研究而言，他选取的十几人样本也算不上糟糕。几年前，一种名为“科尼什博士牙膏”的产品上市，宣称能“显著改善龋齿问题”。其原理是该牙膏含有尿素，实验室研究认为尿素对此具有疗效。但问题在于，相关实验仅处于初步阶段，且研究对象仅有六人而已。】

<!--en-->
The principal joker in this one is the inadequate sample —statistically inadequate, that is; for Doakes' purpose it is just right. That test group of users, you discover by reading the small type, consisted of just a dozen persons. (You have to hand it to Doakes, at that, for giving you a sporting chance. Some advertisers would omit this information and leave even the statistically sophisticated only a guess as to what species of chicanery was afoot. His sample of a dozen isn't so bad either, as these things go. Something called Dr. Cornish's Tooth Powder came onto the market a few years ago with a claim to have shown "considerable success in correction of ... dental caries." The idea was that the powder contained urea, which laboratory work was supposed to have demonstrated to be valuable for the purpose. Thepointlessness of this was that the experimental work had been purely preliminary and had been done on precisely six cases.)

言归正传，多克斯是如何轻松获得无需虚假宣传且数据经过认证的头条新闻呢？只需让一小群人记录六个月内的蛀牙数量，然后改用多克斯推荐的产品即可。结果无非三种：蛀牙明显增多、明显减少，或数量基本不变。如果出现前两种情况，多克斯公司就会把数据藏起来，重新再试。迟早有一天，由于偶然因素，某个测试组会显示出足以登上头条甚至开展整轮广告宣传的巨大改善效果。无论他们使用的是多克斯的产品、小苏打，还是原来的牙膏，情况都会如此。

<!--en-->
But let's get back to how easy it is for Doakes to get a headline without a falsehood in it and everything certified at that. Let any small group of persons keep count of cavities for six months, then switch to Doakes'. One of three things is bound to happen: distinctly more cavities, distinctly fewer, or about the same number. If the first or last of these possibilities occurs, Doakes & Company files the figures (well out of sight somewhere) and tries again. Sooner or later, by the operation of chance, a test group is going to show a big improvement worthy of a headline and perhaps a whole advertising campaign. This will happen whether they adopt Doakes' or baking soda or just keep on using their same old dentifrice.

使用小样本的重要性在于：大样本产生的偶然差异往往很小，不足以值得大肆宣扬。宣称只有2%的改善效果，显然无法卖出多少牙膏。

<!--en-->
The importance of using a small group is this: With a large group any difference produced by chance is likely to be a small one and unworthy of big type. A two-per-cent-improvement claim is not going to sell much tooth paste.

只要案例数量足够少，纯粹靠运气就能得出毫无意义的结论——这一点你只需花点小钱就能亲自验证。不妨试试抛硬币：它出现正面的概率是多少？当然是50%。这谁都知道。

<!--en-->
How results that are not indicative of anything can be produced by pure chance—given a small enough number of cases—is something you can test for yourself at small cost. Just start tossing a penny. How often will it come up heads? Half the time, of course. Everyone knows that.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28177a175a27a14bf61a307bb22c1ac1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7e4ba989f817cfcb26f0618704267ed6ac311103cb463edfc98cb574bf064bc8)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/28177a175a27a14bf61a307bb22c1ac1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7e4ba989f817cfcb26f0618704267ed6ac311103cb463edfc98cb574bf064bc8)

好吧，让我们来验证一下……我刚刚抛了十次硬币，有八次正面朝上，由此证明硬币正面朝上的概率是80%。按照牙膏广告里的说法，确实如此。现在你也来试试吧。你可能会得到五五开的结果，但很可能不会；你的结果很可能与我的一样，偏离五五开很远。不过如果你有耐心抛上一千次，几乎可以肯定你会得到接近一半正面的结果——也就是真正的概率值。只有当试验次数足够多时，平均值法则才能作为有效的描述或预测工具。

<!--en-->
Well, let's check that and see.... I have just tried ten tosses and got heads eight times, which proves that pennies come up heads eighty per cent of the time. Well, by tooth paste statistics they do. Now try it yourself. You may get a fifty-fifty result, but probably you won't; your result, like mine, stands a good chance of being quite a ways away from fifty-fifty. But if your patience holds out for a thousand tosses you are almost (though not quite) certain to come out with a result very close to half heads—a result, that is, which represents the real probability. Only when there is a substantial number of trials involved is the law of averages a useful description or prediction.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f76f0d0eec87c45f8a36aba6bfbb307b.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=eaa0b2736646c601539227dd87aef4d253f551f011d0bd32f6d075accb9c4ad0)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f76f0d0eec87c45f8a36aba6bfbb307b.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=eaa0b2736646c601539227dd87aef4d253f551f011d0bd32f6d075accb9c4ad0)

多少样本才算足够？这也是个棘手的问题。它取决于诸多因素，比如你所研究的群体规模有多大、多样性如何。有时，样本中的实际数量也并非表面看上去那么多。

<!--en-->
How many is enough? That's a tricky one too. It depends among other things on how large and how varied a population you are studying by sampling. And sometimes the number in the sample is not what it appears to be.

几年前一项脊髓灰质炎疫苗测试就体现了这一点。从医学研究角度看，这项实验规模相当庞大：某社区中有450名儿童接种了疫苗，另有680名未接种作为对照组。不久之后，该地区爆发了疫情。令人惊讶的是，接种疫苗的儿童中无人患上明显的脊髓灰质炎。

<!--en-->
A remarkable instance of this came out in connection with a test of a polio vaccine a few years ago. It appeared to be an impressively large-scale experiment as medical ones go: 450 children were vaccinated in a community and 680 were left unvaccinated, as controls. Shortly thereafter the community was visited by an epidemic. Not one of the vaccinated children contracted a recognizable case of polio.

对照组儿童同样无人患病。实验者在设计项目时忽视或未理解的一点就是麻痹型脊髓灰质炎的发病率极低。按常规比例推算，如此规模的群体中预计仅会出现两例病例，因此这项测试从一开始便注定毫无意义。要想得出有意义的结果，所需的儿童数量应是原来的十五到二十五倍之多。

<!--en-->
Neither did any of the controls. What the experimenters had overlooked or not understood in setting up their project was the low incidence of paralytic polio. At the usual rate, only two cases would have been expected in a group this size, and so the test was doomed from the start to have no meaning. Something like fifteen to twenty-five times this many children would have been needed to obtain an answer signifying anything.

许多轰动一时却转瞬即逝的医学发现都是如此诞生的。“趁还来得及，”一位医生说道，“赶紧采用新疗法吧。”

<!--en-->
Many a great, if fleeting, medical discovery has been launched similarly. "Make haste," as one physician put it, "to use a new remedy before it is too late."

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/1074ae83ad0197b43f4c2b6644eb8511.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4a2b42cb1300782654131f891bac3f4415c41728fc98904f3b46fea200807d04)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/1074ae83ad0197b43f4c2b6644eb8511.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4a2b42cb1300782654131f891bac3f4415c41728fc98904f3b46fea200807d04)

责任并不总在医学界。公众压力和仓促的新闻报道常常推动那些未经证实的治疗方法上市，尤其是在需求迫切且统计背景模糊的情况下。几年前的感冒疫苗以及近期的抗组胺药便是如此。这些不成功的“疗法”之所以受欢迎，很大程度上源于感冒本身的不确定性以及逻辑上的缺陷：感冒终究会自行痊愈。

<!--en-->
The guilt does not always lie with the medical profession alone. Public pressure and hasty journalism often launch a treatment that is unproved, particularly when the demand is great and the statistical background hazy. So it was with the cold vaccines that were popular some years back and the antihistamines more recently. A good deal of the popularity of these unsuccessful “cures” sprang from the unreliable nature of the ailment and from a defect of logic. Given time, a cold will cure itself.

如何才能避免被不具结论性的结果所误导呢？难道每个人都必须自己成为统计学家，亲自去研究原始数据吗？其实没那么糟糕；有一种易于理解的显著性检验方法。它只是用来说明某个测试数值代表真实结果而非偶然现象的可能性有多大。这个小小的数字往往被省略了——大概是认为普通读者无法理解吧；或者是因为有人别有用心，故意不让你看到它。

<!--en-->
How can you avoid being fooled by unconclusive results? Must every man be his own statistician and study the raw data for himself? It is not that bad; there is a test of significance that is easy to understand. It is simply a way of reporting how likely it is that a test figure represents a real result rather than something produced by chance. This is the little figure that is not there—on the assumption that you, the lay reader, wouldn’t understand it. Or that, where there’s an axe to grind, you would.

如果信息来源能同时提供显著性程度，你就能更清楚地了解实际情况。这种显著性程度最简单的形式就是概率表达：比如人口普查局会告诉你，他们的数据具有特定精确度的概率为二十分之十九。对于大多数用途而言，低于5%的显著性水平就足够了。对某些人来说，要求的水平是1%，这意味着某一明显差异或类似现象为真实的概率高达百分九十九。如此高的可能性有时会被描述为“几乎可以确定”。

<!--en-->
If the source of your information gives you also the degree of significance, you’ll have a better idea of where you stand. This degree of significance is most simply expressed as a probability, as when the Bureau of the Censustells you that there are nineteen chances out of twenty that their figures have a specified degree of precision. For most purposes nothing poorer than this five per cent level of significance is good enough. For some the demanded level is one per cent, which means that there are ninety-nine chances out of a hundred that an apparent difference, or what not, is real. Anything this likely is sometimes described as “practically certain.”

还有另一种被省略掉的小数字，它的缺失同样可能造成危害。它指的是事物范围或其偏离给定平均值的情况。通常，无论平均数是指均值还是中位数，无论是否明确说明，这种简化往往弊大于利。对某个主题一无所知，有时反而比知道错误的知识更健康；一知半解或许反而危险。

<!--en-->
There’s another kind of little figure that is not there, one whose absence can be just as damaging. It is the one that tells the range of things or their deviation from the average that is given. Often an average—whether mean or median, specified or unspecified—is such an oversimplification that it is worse than useless. Knowing nothing about a subject is frequently healthier than knowing what is not so, and a little learning may be a dangerous thing.

例如，近年来美国建造的住房中，有太多是为了适应统计意义上的平均家庭规模——3.6人。落实到现实中，这意味着三到四口之家，进而意味着需要两间卧室。

<!--en-->
Altogether too much of recent American housing, for instance, has been planned to fit the statistically average family of 3.6 persons. Translated into reality this means three or four persons, which, in turn, means two bedrooms.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/48f84092e38371f0e735d2ccfe89c662.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=fdb8f5969898b2ee43ab947db242fb987a5e7e0cfeaa264f30df5e2167a3a197)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/48f84092e38371f0e735d2ccfe89c662.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=fdb8f5969898b2ee43ab947db242fb987a5e7e0cfeaa264f30df5e2167a3a197)

尽管这个家庭规模被称为“平均”，但实际上它只占所有家庭的少数。“我们为普通家庭建造普通房屋，”建筑商们这样说，却忽视了那些规模更大或更小的家庭。结果，某些地区过度建设了两居室住宅，而较小或较大的户型则供应不足。于是，这一具有误导性且不完整的统计数据导致了高昂的代价。美国公共卫生协会对此指出：“当我们超越算术平均值，去看它所掩盖的实际范围时，会发现三口之家和四口之家仅占总家庭的45%；35%是一口或两口之家；20%的家庭人数超过四人。”

<!--en-->
And this size family, “average” though it is, actually makes up a minority of all families. “We build average houses for average families,” say the builders—and neglect the majority that are larger or smaller. Some areas, in consequence of this, have been overbuilt with two-bedroom houses, underbuilt in respect to smaller and larger units. So here is a statistic whose misleading incompleteness has had expensive consequences. Of it the American Public Health Association says: “When we look beyond the arithmetical average to the actual range which it misrepresents, we find that the three-person and four-person families make up only 45 per cent of the total. Thirty-five per cent are one-person and two-person; 20 per cent have more than four persons.”

面对看似精确且权威的3.6这个数字，常识竟显得无能为力。它似乎压倒了人们从观察中得出的常识：许多家庭规模较小，也有不少家庭规模较大。

<!--en-->
Common sense has somehow failed in the face of the convincingly precise and authoritative 3.6. It has somehow outweighed what everybody knows from observation: that many families are small and quite a few are large.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/5fc4758c49b74c1f98bbcea35878c4fb.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4e66e8665aac481a24a310d7614802bc0eaa0d375062a1dfe51ccb29c191a1d6)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/5fc4758c49b74c1f98bbcea35878c4fb.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4e66e8665aac481a24a310d7614802bc0eaa0d375062a1dfe51ccb29c191a1d6)

类似地，所谓“格塞尔发育标准”中缺失的那些小数字，也给父母带来了痛苦。就像许多人在周日增刊中读到的那样，某个月龄的孩子应该学会坐直，父母立刻就会联想到自己的孩子。如果孩子未能在指定年龄做到这一点，父母便会认定自己的孩子“发育迟缓”或“发育不正常”。由于有一半的孩子注定无法在指定时间坐直，因此许多父母因此感到不安。当然，从数学角度看，这种不安被另外50%的父母因发现孩子“超前”而感到的喜悦所抵消。但那些不安的父母试图强迫孩子符合标准、不再“落后”的努力，可能会带来危害。

<!--en-->
In somewhat the same fashion those little figures that are missing from what are called “Gesell’s norms” have produced pain in papas and mamas. Let a parent read, as many have done in such places as Sunday rotogravure sections, that “a child” learns to sit erect at the age of so many months and he thinks at once of his own child. Let his child fail to sit by the specified age and the parent must conclude that his offspring is “retarded” or “subnormal” or something equally invidious. Since half the children are bound to fail to sit by the time mentioned, a good many parents are made unhappy. Of course, speaking mathematically, this unhappiness is balanced by the joy of the other fifty per cent of parents in discovering that their children are “advanced.” But harm can come of the efforts of the unhappy parents to force their children to conform to the norms and thus be backward no longer.

这一切并不能归咎于阿诺德·格塞尔博士或其研究方法。问题出在研究人员经夸张或无知作者传递到读者手中的过程中，读者未能注意到那些在此过程中消失的数字。如果在“标准”或平均值旁加上范围说明，很多误解便可避免。父母看到自己的孩子处于正常范围内，就不会再为那些微不足道且毫无意义的差异而担忧。实际上，几乎没有人是完全正常的，正如抛一百枚硬币时，很少会出现恰好五十枚正面、五十枚反面的情况。

<!--en-->
All this does not reflect on Dr. Arnold Gesell or his methods. The fault is in the filtering-down process from the researcher through the sensational or ill-informed writer to the reader who fails to miss the figures that have disappeared in the process. A good deal of the misunderstanding can be avoided if to the “norm” or average is added an indication of the range. Parents seeing that their youngsters fall within the normal range will quit worrying about small and meaningless differences. Hardly anybody is exactly normal in any way, just as one hundred tossed pennies will rarely come up exactly fifty heads and fifty tails.

把“正常”与“理想”混为一谈，情况就更糟了。格塞尔博士只是陈述了一些观察到的现象；真正得出结论的是那些阅读相关书籍和文章的父母——他们认为走路晚一天或一个月的孩子就是低人一等。

<!--en-->
Confusing “normal” with “desirable” makes it all the worse. Dr. Gesell simply stated some observed facts; it was the parents who, in reading the books and articles, concluded that a child who walks late by a day or a month must be inferior.

对阿尔弗雷德·金赛博士那份广为人知（尽管鲜有人细读）的报告所提出的诸多愚蠢批评，源于人们将“正常”等同于“良好”、“正确”或“可取”。金赛博士被指责向年轻人灌输错误观念，尤其是将各种流行但未被认可性行为称为正常。但他只是说这些活动很常见——这正是“正常”的含义而已，他并未给予它们任何认可的标志。至于这些行为是否“不端”，并不在金赛博士认为属于自己的职责范围内。因此，他遇到了许多观察者都曾面临的难题：提及任何具有强烈情感色彩的话题时，若不迅速表明自己的立场，便会陷入危险境地。

<!--en-->
A good deal of the stupid criticism of Dr. Alfred Kinsey’s well-known (ifhardly well-read) report came from taking normal to be equivalent to good, right, desirable. Dr. Kinsey was accused of corrupting youth by giving them ideas and particularly by calling all sorts of popular but unapproved sexual practices normal. But he simply said that he had found these activities to be usual, which is what normal means, and he did not stamp them with any seal of approval. Whether they were naughty or not did not come within what Dr. Kinsey considered to be his province. So he ran up against something that has plagued many another observer: It is dangerous to mention any subject having high emotional content without hastily saying where you are for or agin it.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/dd85deaaa1e31dac96ccafb1a667d479.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=be87e51fd8c5b6304879c9021b705f425f7d557c8f097d4474c8c03e0a78f298)

那个并不存在的微小形象之所以具有欺骗性，是因为它的缺失往往不易被察觉。当然，这正是它成功的秘诀。对当今新闻业的批评者痛斥那种缺乏实地调查的传统作风，并严厉指责那些“坐在华盛顿办公室里的记者”——他们只会不加批判地照搬政府发布的材料。以《Fortnight》杂志中列出的“新工业发展”项目为例：“西屋公司研发出一种新型冷处理浴槽，可使钢铁硬度提高三倍。”这听起来确实是一项了不起的进展……

<!--en-->
The deceptive thing about the little figure that is not there is that its absence so often goes unnoticed. That, of course, is the secret of its success. Critics of journalism as practiced today have deplored the paucity of good old-fashioned leg work and spoken harshly of “Washington’s armchair correspondents,” who live by uncritically rewriting government handouts. For a sample of unenterprising journalism take this item from a list of “new industrial developments” in the news magazine *Fortnight*: “a new cold temper bath which triples the hardness of steel, from Westinghouse.”

现在，这听起来像是一项了不起的发明……直到你试图弄明白它的真正含义。结果它却像水银一样难以捉摸。这种新浴槽究竟只是让普通钢材的硬度变为原来的三倍？还是能制造出比以往任何钢材都要硬三倍的钢材？或者它到底有什么作用？显然，记者只是照搬了某些措辞，却并未探究其含义，而读者则被期望不加思考地接受这些信息，从而产生自己学到了什么的错觉。这让人不禁想起对课堂教学中的一种旧有定义：一种将教师课本中的内容直接转移到学生笔记本中、却无需经过双方大脑的过程。

<!--en-->
Now that sounds like quite a development ... until you try to put your finger on what it means. And then it becomes as elusive as a ball of quicksilver. Does the new bath make just any kind of steel three times as hard as it was before treatment? Or does it produce a steel three times as hard as any previous steel? Or what does it do? It appears that the reporter has passed along some words without inquiring what they mean, and you are expected to read them just as uncritically for the happy illusion they give you of having learned something. It is all too reminiscent of an old definition of the lecture method of classroom instruction: a process by which the contents of thetextbook of the instructor are transferred to the notebook of the student without passing through the heads of either party.

几分钟前，我在《时代》杂志上查找有关金赛博士的资料时，又发现了另一句经不起推敲的说法。它出现在1948年一家电力公司集团的广告中：“如今，超过四分之三的美国农场都能用上电力……”听起来不错，这些电力公司确实尽职尽责。当然，如果你故意挑剔的话，也可以将其改写为：“如今，近四分之一的美国农场仍无法使用电力。”不过真正的玄机在于“能用上”这个词——借助它，这些公司几乎可以随心所欲地表述。显然，这并不意味着所有农场真的通了电；否则广告中肯定会明说。他们只是“具备使用条件”——据我所知，这可能意味着电线只是经过他们的农场附近，或者距离他们十英里甚至一百英里之内。

<!--en-->
A few minutes ago, while looking up something about Dr. Kinsey in *Time*, I came upon another of those statements that collapse under a second look. It appeared in an advertisement by a group of electric companies in 1948. "Today, electric power is available to more than three-quarters of U. S. farms...." That sounds pretty good. Those power companies are really on the job. Of course, if you wanted to be ornery you could paraphrase it into "Almost one-quarter of U. S. farms do not have electric power available today." The real gimmick, however, is in that word "available," and by using it the companies have been able to say just about anything they please. Obviously this does not mean that all those farmers actually have power, or the advertisement surely would have said so. They merely have it "available"—and that, for all I know, could mean that the power lines go past their farms or merely within ten or a hundred miles of them.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f0c6c037f8e87f50de7f5628b6084971.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=885d1126ae536eda828f6647575d412f33189674207aba333807728d84357233)

让我引用一篇1952年发表于《Collier's》杂志上的文章标题：“你现在就能知道孩子将来能长多高。”文章旁边醒目地附有两张图表，一张针对男孩，一张针对女孩，显示孩子在每年龄阶段达到最终身高百分比的情况。“要确定孩子成年后的身高，”说明文字写道，“只需将当前测量值与图表对照即可。”

<!--en-->
Let me quote a title from an article published in *Collier's* in 1952: "You Can Tell *Now* HOW TALL YOUR CHILD WILL GROW." With the article is conspicuously displayed a pair of charts, one for boys and one for girls, showing what percentage of his ultimate height a child reaches at each year of age. "To determine your child's height at maturity," says a caption, "check present measurement against chart."

有趣的是，如果你继续阅读这篇文章，就会发现图表存在的致命缺陷：并非所有孩子的生长方式都相同。有些孩子起步缓慢但后来加速；有些则先快速生长，随后逐渐放缓；还有些孩子的生长过程相对平稳。如你所料，这张图表是基于大量测量数据得出的平均值。对于随机抽取的一百名青少年的总体平均身高而言，它或许足够准确，但家长关心的只是某个特定孩子的身高，而这样的图表对此几乎毫无用处。如果你想预测孩子将来能长多高，或许看看他的父母和祖父母更为靠谱。这种方法虽不像图表那样科学精确，但至少同样准确。

<!--en-->
The funny thing about this is that the article itself—if you read on—tells you what the fatal weakness in the chart is. Not all children grow in the same way. Some start slowly and then speed up; others shoot up quickly for a while, then level off slowly; for still others growth is a relatively steady process. The chart, as you might guess, is based on averages taken from a large number of measurements. For the total, or average, heights of a hundredyoungsters taken at random it is no doubt accurate enough, but a parent is interested in only one height at a time, a purpose for which such a chart is virtually worthless. If you wish to know how tall your child is going to be, you can probably make a better guess by taking a look at his parents and grandparents. That method isn't scientific and precise like the chart, but it is at least as accurate.

我觉得好笑的是，根据我十四岁参加高中军事训练时的记录，我的身高属于最小队列中的最后一名。按此推算，我最终应该只会长到五英尺八英寸左右。而实际上我身高五英尺十一英寸。人类身高预测出现三英寸的误差，实在算不上准确的猜测。

<!--en-->
I am amused to note that, taking my height as recorded when I enrolled in high-school military training at fourteen and ended up in the rear rank of the smallest squad. I should eventually have grown to a bare five feet eight. I am five feet eleven. A three-inch error in human height comes down to a poor grade of guess.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9d906642d9d78a0e49995eddf6b17144.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=c5395f365b4de05849a405f3af48133e87c3c899fb1104c5e7d30ea30a66ccf5)

我面前放着两盒葡萄坚果片的包装纸。它们属于略有不同的版本，从上面的宣传语就能看出：一盒上写着“Two-Gun Pete”，另一盒则宣称：“如果你想成为Hoppy那样的人……就必须像Hoppy一样进食！”两盒产品都配有图表来证明（“科学家*证实*这是真的！”）这些麦片“能在2分钟内为你提供能量！”其中一盒图表隐藏在密密麻麻的感叹号中，侧面标有数字；另一盒则没有标注数字。这也罢了，毕竟根本没人知道这些数字代表什么。两幅图表都显示了一条急剧上升的红线（“能量释放”），但一幅图显示吃完葡萄坚果片后1分钟就开始上升，另一幅则是2分钟后。而且其中一条线的上升速度大约是另一条的两倍，这似乎表明就连绘图者自己都认为这些图表毫无意义。

<!--en-->
Before me are wrappers from two boxes of Grape-Nuts Flakes. They are slightly different editions, as indicated by their testimonials: one cites Two-Gun Pete and the other says, "If you want to be like Hoppy ... you've got to eat like Hoppy!" Both offer charts to show ("Scientists *proved* it's true!") that these flakes "start giving you energy in 2 minutes!" In one case the chart hidden in these forests of exclamation points has numbers up the side; in the other case the numbers have been omitted. This is just as well, since there is no hint of what the numbers mean.
