Both show a steeply climbing red line ("energy release"), but one has it starting one minute after eating Grape-Nuts Flakes, the other two minutes later. One line climbs about twice as fast as the other, too, suggesting that even the draftsman didn't think these graphs meant anything.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/809836b4080e888adea6f1ac88ee5017.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1839dfd1212d4bb144190699c7267b48fa701a72d627b7c61b23a523936d87ac)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/809836b4080e888adea6f1ac88ee5017.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1839dfd1212d4bb144190699c7267b48fa701a72d627b7c61b23a523936d87ac)

当然，这种荒谬的内容只会出现在面向儿童或清晨疲惫的家长的产品上。没人会用这种毫无根据的统计垃圾去侮辱大商人的智商……或许吧？让我来给你讲讲《财富》杂志中用来宣传某广告公司的图表（希望我没把事情搞混）。该图表中的线条显示了该公司业务逐年强劲上升的趋势。图表上没有标注数字。凭同样的“诚实”原则，这张图表既可以表示业务翻倍或每年增长数百万美元的巨大发展，也可以表示一家停滞不前的公司每年仅增加一两美元的营业额。不过它确实构成了一幅引人注目的画面。

<!--en-->
Such foolishness could be found only on material meant for the eye of a juvenile or his morning-weary parent, of course. No one would insult a big businessman's intelligence with such statistical tripe... or would he? Let me tell you about a graph used to advertise an advertising agency (I hope this isn't getting confusing) in the rather special columns of *Fortune* magazine. The line on this graph showed the impressive upward trend of the agency's business year by year. There were no numbers. With equal honesty this chart could have represented a tremendous growth, with business doubling or increasing by millions of dollars a year, or the snail-like progress of a static concern adding only a dollar or two to its annual billings. It made a striking picture, though.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c2595ac8faf8d2b2ed053f1576b5c470.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=57cf9941cd42a411bc00d281bd407a4a735f737d563d58288f06ee0513144108)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c2595ac8faf8d2b2ed053f1576b5c470.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=57cf9941cd42a411bc00d281bd407a4a735f737d563d58288f06ee0513144108)

当那些关键数据缺失时，切勿轻信平均值、图表或趋势。否则你就像仅凭平均气温报告来选择露营地的人一样盲目。你可能会认为61华氏度是舒适的年度平均气温，从而在加利福尼亚州选择内陆沙漠或南海岸的圣尼古拉斯岛等地。但如果你忽略温度范围，就可能会遭遇严寒或酷热。圣尼古拉斯岛的温度范围是47到87华氏度，而内陆沙漠则是15到104华氏度。

<!--en-->
Place little faith in an average or a graph or a trend when those important figures are missing. Otherwise you are as blind as a man choosing a camp site from a report of mean temperature alone. You might take 61 degrees as a comfortable annual mean, giving you a choice in California between suchareas as the inland desert and San Nicolas Island off the south coast. But you can freeze or roast if you ignore the range. For San Nicolas it is 47 to 87 degrees but for the desert it is 15 to 104.

俄克拉荷马城过去六十年的平均气温也是60.2华氏度。但如下面的图表所示，这个看似宜人的数字背后隐藏着130华氏度的温差。*俄克拉荷马城的极端气温记录*

<!--en-->
Oklahoma City can claim a similar average temperature for the last sixty years: 60.2 degrees. But as you can see from the chart below, that cool and comfortable figure conceals a range of 130 degrees.
*Record Temperatures in Oklahoma City*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/5e4da8c7a5b6343bf7aab56972f0393d.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=364655b592194022fd35bcd96436da6acb07732a7f098e3d9dab43024206a35d)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/5e4da8c7a5b6343bf7aab56972f0393d.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=364655b592194022fd35bcd96436da6acb07732a7f098e3d9dab43024206a35d)

# 第四章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 4*

## 无事生非

<!--en-->
*Much Ado about Practically Nothing*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/06ad05b934a94ac99a7fb0ed8fc21c49.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=15a95fada644cab747c21d39e93c629d520d1c151970a10c609cd4ad2d8fc110)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/06ad05b934a94ac99a7fb0ed8fc21c49.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=15a95fada644cab747c21d39e93c629d520d1c151970a10c609cd4ad2d8fc110)

如果不介意的话，我们先给你虚构两个孩子：彼得和琳达（既然要取名，不如选些时髦的名字）。和许多学龄儿童一样，他们接受了智力测试。如今，各类智力测试已成为我们时代的“神秘图腾”之一，因此你可能得费点口舌才能得知测试结果；这些信息极为隐秘，往往被认为只有心理学家和教育工作者才能掌握，也许他们说得对。总之，你最终得知彼得的智商为98，琳达的智商为101。你当然知道，智商是以100为平均值或“正常值”来衡量的。

<!--en-->
IF YOU don't mind, we will begin by endowing you with two children. Peter and Linda (we might as well give them modish names while we're about it) have been given intelligence tests, as a great many children are in the course of their schooling. Now the mental test of any variety is one of the prime voodoo fetishes of our time, so you may have to argue a little to find out the results of the tests; this is information so esoteric that it is often held to be safe only in the hands of psychologists and educators, and they may be right at that. Anyway, you learn somehow that Peter's IQ is 98 and Linda's is 101. You know, of course, that the IQ is based on 100 as average or "normal."

啊哈，琳达是你的更聪明的孩子。她甚至高于平均水平。彼得低于平均水平，但咱们还是别纠结于这一点了。

<!--en-->
Aha. Linda is your brighter child. She is, furthermore, above average. Peter is below average, but let's not dwell on *that*.

诸如此类的结论纯属无稽之谈。

<!--en-->
Any such conclusions as these are sheer nonsense.

为了澄清事实，我们首先要指出：无论智力测试测量的是什么，它都与我们通常所说的智力并非同一回事。它忽略了领导力和创造性想象力等重要因素，也不考虑社会判断力、音乐或艺术天赋，更不用说勤奋和情绪稳定等性格特质了。此外，学校里最常进行的测试是那种快捷廉价的团体测试，这类测试很大程度上依赖于阅读能力；无论是否聪明，阅读能力差的人根本没有机会。

<!--en-->
Just to clear the air, let's note first of all that whatever an intelligence test measures it is not quite the same thing as we usually mean by intelligence. Itneglects such important things as leadership and creative imagination. It takes no account of social judgment or musical or artistic or other aptitudes, to say nothing of such personality matters as diligence and emotional balance. On top of that, the tests most often given in schools are the quick-and-cheap group kind that depend a good deal upon reading facility; bright or not, the poor reader hasn't a chance.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f212634557b23f1062e7103b0d6deb49.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=fc07bda5972b11c0112e62b37fa5fbf4e788d0d39e31d3e22afb2c1627fd88d9)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f212634557b23f1062e7103b0d6deb49.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=fc07bda5972b11c0112e62b37fa5fbf4e788d0d39e31d3e22afb2c1627fd88d9)

假设我们承认这一切，并同意将智商仅仅视为某种定义模糊的、处理抽象概念的能力的衡量标准。彼得和琳达接受的正是公认最优秀的测试——修订版斯坦福-比奈测验，该测验为个别测试，不要求特定的阅读能力。

<!--en-->
Let's say that we have recognized all that and agree to regard the IQ simply as a measure of some vaguely defined capacity to handle canned abstractions. And Peter and Linda have been given what is generally regarded as the best of the tests, the Revised Stanford-Binet, which is administered individually and doesn't call for any particular reading ability.

智商测试本质上是对智力的一次抽样。和所有抽样结果一样，智商也是一个带有统计误差的数值，这一误差反映了该数值的精确度和可靠性。

<!--en-->
Now what an IQ test purports to be is a sampling of the intellect. Like any other product of the sampling method, the IQ is a figure with a statistical error, which expresses the precision or reliability of that figure.

提出这些测试题的方式，就好比你在估算一块田地里玉米的质量时，随机摘取几穗玉米来观察。假设你摘了一百穗玉米并仔细查看，就能大致了解整块田地的状况。只要两块田地差异明显，这些信息就足以用来比较它们；但如果田地相似，你就可能需要观察更多玉米穗，并根据某种精确的质量标准逐一评分。

<!--en-->
Asking these test questions is something like what you might do in estimating the quality of the corn in a field by going about and pulling off an ear here and an ear there at random. By the time you had stripped down and looked at a hundred ears, say, you would have gained a pretty good idea of what the whole field was like. Your information would be exact enough for use in comparing this field with another field—provided the two fields were not very similar. If they were, you might have to look at many more ears, rating them all the while by some precise standard of quality.

你的样本能够多准确地代表整块田地，可以用数字来衡量：即可能误差和标准误差。

<!--en-->
How accurately your sample can be taken to represent the whole field is a measure that can be represented in figures: the probable error and the standard error.

假设你的任务是通过步测来测量许多田地的面积。你首先可能会通过多次步测所谓的一百码来检验测量系统的准确性。你可能会发现，平均而言你的误差为三码。也就是说，在一半的测试中，你的测量结果与实际一百码相差不超过三码；另一半测试中则偏差超过三码。

<!--en-->
Suppose that you had the task of measuring the size of a good many fields by pacing off the fence lines. The first thing you might do is check the accuracy of your measuring system by pacing off what you took to be a hundred yards, doing this a number of times. You might find that on the average you were off by three yards. That is, you came within three yards of hitting the exact one hundred in half your trials, and in the other half of them you missed by more than three yards.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/45ccbfe45497a16d2b589862b07ac0d2.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2b92e594a4d9ff0f0ac43a89666c9210c756a67d077a87676800db8fec35628a)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/45ccbfe45497a16d2b589862b07ac0d2.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2b92e594a4d9ff0f0ac43a89666c9210c756a67d077a87676800db8fec35628a)

因此，你的可能误差就是百分之一百中的三码，也就是百分之三。从此以后，通过步测得出的每一段一百码的围栏长度，都可以记录为$100 \pm 3$码。

<!--en-->
Your probable error then would be three yards in one hundred, or three per cent. From then on, each fence line that measured one hundred yards by your pacing might be recorded as $100 \pm 3$ yards.

（如今大多数统计学家更倾向于使用另一种类似但更方便的数学度量——标准误差。它涵盖了约三分之二的情况而非恰好一半，在数学处理上更为简便。出于我们的目的，可以继续使用可能误差，因为斯坦福-比奈测验中仍采用这一指标。）

<!--en-->
(Most statisticians now prefer to use another, but comparable, measurement called the standard error. It takes in about two-thirds of the cases instead of exactly half and is considerably handier in a mathematical way. For our purposes we can stick to the probable error, which is the one still used in connection with the Stanford-Binet.)

正如我们假设的步测情况一样，斯坦福-比奈智商测试的可能误差也被确定为百分之三。这与测试本身的好坏无关，只与其测量的一致性有关。因此，彼得的智商可表示为$98 \pm 3$，琳达的则为$101 \pm 3$。

<!--en-->
As with our hypothetical pacing, the probable error of the Stanford-Binet IQ has been found to be three per cent. This has nothing to do with how good the test is basically, only with how consistently it measures whatever it measures. So Peter's indicated IQ might be more fully expressed as $98 \pm 3$ and Linda's as $101 \pm 3$.

这意味着彼得的智商落在95到101之间的概率仅为二分之一；它高于或低于该范围的可能性相同。同样，琳达的智商在98到104之间的概率也不超过二分之一。由此可看出，彼得的智商有四分之一的几率实际上超过101，琳达的智商也有类似几率低于98。这样看来，彼得不仅不逊色于他人，反而高出至少三分。

<!--en-->
This says that there is no more than an even chance that Peter's IQ falls anywhere between 95 and 101; it is just as likely that it is above or below that figure. Similarly Linda's has no better than a fifty-fifty probability of being within the range of 98 to 104. From this you can quickly see that there is one chance in four that Peter's IQ is really above 101 and a similar chance that Linda's is below 98. Then Peter is not inferior but superior, and by a margin of anywhere from three points up.

归根结底，看待智商及其他许多抽样结果时，必须将其视为一个范围。“正常”值并非固定的100，而是诸如90到110这样的区间；将处于这一区间的儿童与处于更低或更高区间的儿童进行比较才有意义。但数值差异微小时的比较毫无意义。你必须始终牢记这种正负误差的存在，即使（或尤其当）它未被明确标出时。

<!--en-->
What this comes down to is that the only way to think about IQs and many other sampling results is in ranges. “Normal” is not 100, but the range of 90 to 110, say, and there would be some point in comparing a child in this range with a child in a lower or higher range. But comparisons between figures with small differences are meaningless. You must always keep that plus-or-minus in mind, even (or especially) when it is not stated.

忽视这些存在于所有抽样研究中的误差，导致了某些极其荒谬的行为。有些杂志编辑把读者调查数据奉为真理，主要是因为他们并不理解其含义。当某篇文章的男性读者比例被报告为40%，而另一篇仅为35%时，他们便要求刊登更多类似第一篇的文章。

<!--en-->
Ignoring these errors, which are implicit in all sampling studies, has led to some remarkably silly behavior. There are magazine editors to whom readership surveys are gospel, mainly because they do not understand them. With forty per cent male readership reported for one article and only thirty-five per cent for another, they demand more articles like the first.

35%与40%的读者比例差异对杂志而言或许重要，但调查结果的差异未必反映真实情况。由于成本限制，读者样本往往只有几百人，尤其是排除了根本不读该杂志的人之后。对于主要面向女性的杂志而言，样本中的男性数量可能极少。当这些人又被细分为“全部阅读”、“大部分阅读”、“部分阅读”或“未阅读”各类后，得出35%这一结论所依据的样本量可能微不足道。隐藏在看似精确的数字背后的可能误差可能极大，以至于依赖它的编辑简直是在抓救命稻草。

<!--en-->
The difference between thirty-five and forty per cent readership can be of importance to a magazine, but a survey difference may not be a real one. Costs often hold readership samples down to a few hundred persons, particularly after those who do not read the magazine at all have been eliminated. For a magazine that appeals primarily to women the number of men in the sample may be very small. By the time these have been divided among those who say they “read all,” “read most,” “read some,” or “didn’t read” the article in question, the thirty-five per cent conclusion may be based on only a handful. The probable error hidden behind the impressively presented figure may be so large that the editor who relies on it is grasping at a thin straw.

有时人们会对一种数学上真实但微不足道的差异大做文章。这违背了那句古老的谚语：“只有产生实际影响的差异才算差异。”一个典型的例子就是Old Gold香烟公司利用几乎无关紧要的差异所制造的喧嚣，并从中获利颇丰。

<!--en-->
Sometimes the big ado is made about a difference that is mathematically real and demonstrable but so tiny as to have no importance. This is in defiance of the fine old saying that a difference is a difference only if it makes a difference. A case in point is the hullabaloo over practically nothing that was raised so effectively, and so profitably, by the Old Gold cigarette people.

事情的开端颇为单纯：当时《读者文摘》的编辑虽自己抽烟，却对香烟持否定态度。该杂志委托实验室人员分析几种品牌香烟的烟雾成分，随后公布了结果，列出了各品牌烟雾中的尼古丁及其他物质含量。杂志得出的结论——并得到了详细数据的支持——是：所有品牌的烟雾成分几乎相同，抽哪种烟并无区别。

<!--en-->
It started innocently with the editor of the *Reader’s Digest*, who smokes cigarettes but takes a dim view of them all the same. His magazine went to work and had a battery of laboratory folk analyze the smoke from several brands of cigarettes. The magazine published the results, giving the nicotine and whatnot content of the smoke by brands. The conclusion stated by the magazine and borne out in its detailed figures was that all the brands were virtually identical and that it didn’t make any difference which one you smoked.

你或许会认为这对香烟制造商以及广告公司里负责构思新宣传语的人而言是个打击。这似乎会推翻所有关于“舒缓喉咙”或“对T区友好”的广告宣称。

<!--en-->
Now you might think this was a blow to cigarette manufacturers and to the fellows who think up the new copy angles in the advertising agencies. It would seem to explode all advertising claims about soothing throats and kindness to T-zones.

但有人发现了端倪：在那些成分含量几乎相同的列表中，有一种香烟的含量最低，那就是Old Gold牌香烟。于是电报纷飞，报纸上立刻登出了用最大字号印刷的重要广告。标题和文案仅仅声称：在这本权威全国性杂志测试的所有香烟中，Old Gold牌香烟烟雾中的有害物质含量最少。广告中刻意省略了所有数据，也绝口不提这种差异其实微乎其微。

<!--en-->
But somebody spotted something. In the lists of almost identical amounts of poisons, one cigarette had to be at the bottom, and the one was Old Gold. Out went the telegrams, and big advertisements appeared in newspapers at once in the biggest type at hand. The headlines and the copy simply said that of all cigarettes tested by this great national magazine Old Gold had the least of these undesirable things in its smoke. Excluded were all figures and any hint that the difference was negligible.

最终，Old Gold牌香烟的生产商被勒令停止这种误导性广告。但这已无关紧要；他们早已从这一噱头中榨取了全部利益。正如《纽约客》所言：广告人永远存在。

<!--en-->
In the end, the Old Gold people were ordered to “cease and desist” from such misleading advertising. That didn’t make any difference; the good had been milked from the idea long before. As the *New Yorker* says, there’ll always be an ad man.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/dfbaca6a81f1a45eff5e77f27cd9d150.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5a6578de820fac97f0266498a2ddf7c1de12f9733168f2b7c9fcc30b3c937592)

# 第五章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 5*

## 神奇图表

<!--en-->
*The Gee - Whiz Graph*

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/6ec422f2c39d352d52b980809d8303a3.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2eb0a3bcebc86902311d4e1ce5c843aa60c6ebf41de72378be5a7e36340629e5)

数字往往令人恐惧。汉普蒂·邓普蒂曾自信地向爱丽丝宣称自己能掌控所用词语的含义，但很少有人会将这种自信延伸到数字上。也许我们从小遭受的算术教育造成了某种心理创伤。

<!--en-->
THERE is terror in numbers. Humpty Dumpty's confidence in telling Alice that he was master of the words he used would not be extended by many people to numbers. Perhaps we suffer from a trauma induced by grade-school arithmetic.

无论原因如何，这对渴望被阅读的作者、指望文案能推销商品的广告人、希望书籍或杂志畅销的出版商而言都是个难题。当表格形式的数字被视为禁忌，而文字又无法有效传达信息时——这种情况屡见不鲜——只剩下一个办法：画图。

<!--en-->
Whatever the cause, it creates a real problem for the writer who yearns to be read, the advertising man who expects his copy to sell goods, the publisher who wants his books or magazines to be popular. When numbers in tabular form are taboo and words will not do the work well, as is often the case, there is one answer left: Draw a picture.

最简单的统计图表就是折线图。它非常适合展示趋势，而这正是几乎所有人都想展示、了解、察觉、感叹或预测的内容。比方说，让我们的图表展示一年内国民收入增长了百分之十的情况。

<!--en-->
About the simplest kind of statistical picture, or graph, is the line variety. It is very useful for showing trends, something practically everybody isinterested in showing or knowing about or spotting or deploring or forecasting. Well let our graph show how national income increased ten per cent in a year.

首先准备一张画有方格的纸。在底部标上月份名称，侧面标明数十亿美元的数值。标出数据点并连成线，你的图表就会如下所示：

<!--en-->
Begin with paper ruled into squares. Name the months along the bottom. Indicate billions of dollars up the side. Plot your points and draw your line, and your graph will look like this:

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/734e17ce6bd8fc2d5561464efc249097.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=69a2be6566662c3a788ff1b1810dd94b5a80b50617bd5e64801da83e79ffa692)

这样已经足够清晰：它展示了全年发生的情况，且按月呈现。任何人都能一目了然，因为整个图表比例协调，底部还有零基线可供对比。你看到的百分之十确实“看起来”像百分之十——这是一种显著但未必惊人的上升趋势。

<!--en-->
Now that's clear enough. It shows what happened during the year and it shows it month by month. He who runs may see and understand, because the whole graph is in proportion and there is a zero line at the bottom for comparison. Your ten per cent *looks* like ten per cent—an upward trend that is substantial but perhaps not overwhelming.

如果你只是想传递信息，这样便已足够。但倘若你想赢得争论、震撼读者、促使他们采取行动或推销产品呢？这样的图表就缺乏感染力。那就把底部切掉吧。

<!--en-->
That is very well if all you want to do is convey information. But suppose you wish to win an argument, shock a reader, move him into action, sell him something. For that, this chart lacks schmaltz. Chop off the bottom.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f140c71ae94a3d631be38c3d78a78f1b.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=f7262d167e10aff826cdac30f259cf08ea24063c975c20c63cd59ae2445de84c)

现在这样就更像样了。（你也省了纸张，要是有人挑剔你的误导性图表，正好可以拿这点来辩解。）数字和曲线并未改变，图表本身还是原来的那个。没有任何东西被篡改——除了它给人的印象。如今心急的读者看到的是一条在十二个月内攀升至纸张一半高度的国民收入线，只因图表的大部分已被删去。就像语法课上遇到的句子缺省成分一样，这种缺失被“默认理解”了。当然，眼睛无法“理解”不存在的东西，于是微小的上升在视觉上变成了巨大的飞跃。

<!--en-->
Now that's more like it. (You've saved paper too, something to point out if any carping fellow objects to your misleading graphics.) The figures are thesame and so is the curve. It is the same graph. Nothing has been falsified-except the impression that it gives. But what the hasty reader sees now is a national-income line that has climbed halfway up the paper in twelve months, all because most of the chart isn't there any more. Like the missing parts of speech in sentences that you met in grammar classes, it is "understood." Of course, the eye doesn't "understand" what isn't there, and a small rise has become, visually, a big one.

既然你已经练就了欺骗之术，何必止步于截短图表呢？还有一个更绝的技巧，其效果堪比十几个截短操作。它能让你那区区百分之十的增长显得比百分之百的增长还要惊人。只需改变纵坐标与横坐标的比例即可。并无规则禁止此举，而且这样确实能让图表更美观。你只需让侧面的每个刻度代表的金额仅为原来的十分之一。

<!--en-->
Now that you have practiced to deceive, why stop with truncating? You have a further trick available that's worth a dozen of that. It will make your modest rise of ten per cent look livelier than one hundred per cent is entitled to look. Simply change the proportion between the ordinate and the abscissa. There's no rule against it, and it does give your graph a prettier shape. All you have to do is let each mark up the side stand for only one-tenth as many dollars as before.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/fccfa85511a43ef47caba4614e35bad7.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dd37ac5aa1545dcec022881d79398de8ff9656e21d34c38693cf1c9294c37f60)

真是令人印象深刻，不是吗？任何看到它的人都能感受到国家脉搏中跳动的繁荣气息。这相当于把“国民收入增长了百分之十”改写成“……竟然飙升了惊人的百分之十”。不过这种方式的效果要强得多，因为它没有使用形容词或副词来破坏那种客观性的假象。没人能拿它来指责你。

<!--en-->
That is impressive, isn't it? Anyone looking at it can just feel prosperity throbbing in the arteries of the country. It is a subtler equivalent of editing "National income rose ten per cent" into "... climbed a whopping ten per cent." It is vastly more effective, however, because it contains no adjectives or adverbs to spoil the illusion of objectivity. There's nothing anyone can pin on you.

而且你并非孤例，至少算得上“体面”的同行。《新闻周刊》曾在1951年用这种方法展示“股市创下21年新高”，并将图表截断在80的位置。1952年，《时代》杂志上刊登的一则哥伦比亚燃气公司的广告也引用了“来自我们新年度报告的图表”。如果你细读上面的数字并加以分析，会发现十年间生活成本上升了约60%，而燃气价格却下降了4%。这本是一幅有利的画面，但对哥伦比亚燃气公司而言似乎还不够理想。他们把图表截断在90的位置（没有任何间隙或其他提示来提醒读者），于是你看到的画面就变成了：生活成本翻了三倍多，燃气价格却下降了三分之一！

<!--en-->
And you're in good, or at least respectable, company. *Newsweek* magazine used this method to show that "Stocks Hit a 21-Year High" in 1951, truncating the graph at the eighty mark. A Columbia Gas System advertisement in *Time* in 1952 reproduced a chart "from our new AnnualReport.” If you read the little numbers and analyzed them you found that during a ten-year period living costs went up about sixty per cent and the cost of gas dropped four per cent. This is a favorable picture, but it apparently was not favorable enough for Columbia Gas. They chopped off their chart at ninety per cent (with no gap or other indication to warn you) so that this was what your eye told you: Living costs have more than tripled, and gas has gone down one-third!

钢铁公司也曾采用类似具有误导性的图表手法，试图煽动公众反对涨薪。其实这种方法并不新鲜，其不当之处早已被揭露——而且不只是在统计学家的专业刊物中。1938年，《邓氏评论》的一位社论作者引用了一则倡导在华盛顿特区投放广告的广告中的图表，图表上方的标题恰如其分地表达了其论点：“政府雇员人数激增！”尽管背后的数据并未支持这一说法，但图表中的线条却顺着感叹号的方向延伸。实际显示的数据是从约19,500,000增加到20,200,000；然而红线却从图表底部直冲顶部，把不到4%的增长歪曲成超过400%的增长。该杂志同时给出了同一数据的真实图表版本——一条仅上升4%的诚实红线，配文为：“政府雇员人数保持稳定。”

<!--en-->
Steel companies have used similarly misleading graphic methods in attempts to line up public opinion against wage increases. Yet the method is far from new, and its impropriety was shown up long ago—not just in technical publications for statisticians either. An editorial writer in *Dun's Review* in 1938 reproduced a chart from an advertisement advocating advertising in Washington, D. C., the argument being nicely expressed in the headline over the chart: GOVERNMENT PAY ROLLS UP! The line in the graph went along with the exclamation point even though the figures behind it did not. What they showed was an increase from about $19,500,000 to $20,-200,000. But the red line shot from near the bottom of the graph clear to the top, making an increase of under four per cent look like more than 400. The magazine gave its own graphic version of the same figures alongside—an honest red line that rose just four per cent, under this caption: GOVERNMENT PAY ROLLS STABLE.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9098b8b0f12c40fc11d6c29a3778209a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=6219d06d6ec8f497f9072cbd135d44b511679e463460a9e259babc29f3674b5b)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9098b8b0f12c40fc11d6c29a3778209a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=6219d06d6ec8f497f9072cbd135d44b511679e463460a9e259babc29f3674b5b)

《科利尔杂志》在报纸广告中也采用了同样的手法处理柱状图。尤其要注意的是，图表的中间部分被截去了：*摘自1953年4月24日《科利尔杂志》的报纸广告*

<!--en-->
Collier's has used this same treatment with a bar chart in newspaper advertisements. Note especially that the middle of the chart has been cut out:*From an April 24, 1953, newspaper advertisement for COLLIER'S*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c6dda91075445441771b59a4eaa50693.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5cabb4cf41c676e04c943be69242abe3f659e1edb6036c55a1bde61850606b52)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c6dda91075445441771b59a4eaa50693.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5cabb4cf41c676e04c943be69242abe3f659e1edb6036c55a1bde61850606b52)

# 第六章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 6*

## 一维图像

<!--en-->
*The One-Dimensional Picture*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/78119eb51268fd3ab452e11d7817486a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=61fd0b772755038156738c9aa59c8fa3483ea24993ee55ce4f0a951d3501be6a)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/78119eb51268fd3ab452e11d7817486a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=61fd0b772755038156738c9aa59c8fa3483ea24993ee55ce4f0a951d3501be6a)

大约十年前，人们经常听到关于“小人物”的说法，实际上指的就是我们所有人。当这种说法听起来过于居高临下时，我们就变成了“普通人”。很快连这个称呼也被遗忘了，或许这样反而更好。但“小人物”依然存在——他就是图表中的那个形象。

<!--en-->
A DECADE or so ago you heard a good deal about the little people, meaning practically all of us. When this began to sound too condescending, we became the common man. Pretty soon that was forgotten too, which was probably just as well. But the little man is still with us. He is the character on the chart.

一种用一个小人代表一百万人、用一个钱袋或一堆硬币代表千元或亿元、用一头牛的轮廓表示明年牛肉供应量的图表，就是所谓的象形图。它是一种有用的工具，可惜它具备所谓的“视觉吸引力”。它也完全有能力成为狡猾、隐蔽且成功的谎言制造者。

<!--en-->
A chart on which a little man represents a million men, a moneybag or stack of coins a thousand or a billion dollars, an outline of a steer your beef supply for next year, is a pictorial graph. It is a useful device. It has what I am afraid is known as eye-appeal. And it is capable of becoming a fluent, devious, and successful liar.

象形图或 pictograph 的雏形就是普通的柱状图，这是一种简单而常用的比较多个数量的方法。柱状图同样也能用来欺骗人。如果柱状图的宽度和长度都随单一因素而变化，或者它们描绘的是难以比较体积的三维物体，那你就得警惕了。截断式柱状图与我们前文提到的截断式折线图一样，名声不佳且理应如此。柱状图常见于地理课本、企业报表和新闻杂志中，它那些具有视觉吸引力的“后代”也是如此。

<!--en-->
The daddy of the pictorial chart, or pictograph, is the ordinary bar chart, a simple and popular method of representing quantities when two or more are to be compared. A bar chart is capable of deceit too. Look with suspicion onany version in which the bars change their widths as well as their lengths while representing a single factor or in which they picture three-dimensional objects the volumes of which are not easy to compare. A truncated bar chart has, and deserves, exactly the same reputation as the truncated line graph we have been talking about. The habitat of the bar chart is the geography book, the corporation statement, and the news magazine. This is true also of its eye-appealing offspring.

假设我想比较两组数据——比如美国木匠的平均周薪与罗通迪亚国的数据，数值可能分别是60美元和30美元。我希望以此吸引你的注意，所以不满足于仅仅印出这些数字，于是我制作了一张柱状图。（顺便说一句，如果那60美元的数字与你去年夏天更换门廊栏杆时所支付的巨额费用不符，请记住：你的木匠每周的工作表现未必都像为你干活时那么出色。况且我并未说明所指的平均值是哪种类型，也未说明是如何得出的，所以你就算争论也无济于事。你看，如果不附带其他信息，利用最不可靠的统计数据来掩盖真相是多么容易吧？你大概猜到我是为了说明而编造了这个例子，但我敢打赌，如果我用的是59.83美元，你就不会这么想了。）

<!--en-->
Perhaps I wish to show a comparison of two figures—the average weekly wage of carpenters in the United States and Rotundia, let's say. The sums might be $60 and $30. I wish to catch your eye with this, so I am not satisfied merely to print the numbers. I make a bar chart. (By the way, if that $60 figure doesn't square with the huge sum you laid out when your porch needed a new railing last summer, remember that your carpenter may not have done as well every week as he did while working for you. And anyway I didn't say what kind of average I have in mind or how I arrived at it, so it isn't going to get you anywhere to quibble. You see how easy it is to hide behind the most disreputable statistic if you don't include any other information with it? You probably guessed I just made this one up for purposes of illustration, but I'll bet you wouldn't have if I'd used $59.83 instead.)

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/121b39f45fe0a38c86a10decad96c0cc.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2864ab57856a1ef11c714d44a5d7b74b9ffc8e7b07960f87304187c937586da3)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/121b39f45fe0a38c86a10decad96c0cc.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2864ab57856a1ef11c714d44a5d7b74b9ffc8e7b07960f87304187c937586da3)

就在那里，左侧标明了每周的美元金额。这是一幅清晰而真实的图表。金额翻倍时，在图表上的显示也确实会变大一倍。

<!--en-->
There it is, with dollars-per-week indicated up the left side. It is a clear and honest picture. Twice as much money is twice as big on the chart and looks it.

不过，这张图表缺乏视觉吸引力，不是吗？我可以用看起来更像钱而非柱状图的东西来轻松解决这个问题：钱袋。给那个可怜的罗坦迪亚人一个钱袋来代表他的微薄收入，给美国人两个钱袋来代表他的工资。或者给罗坦迪亚人三个钱袋，给美国人六个钱袋。无论如何，图表依然保持真实清晰，不会欺骗你匆忙的一瞥。这才是制作诚实图表的方式。

<!--en-->
The chart lacks that eye-appeal though, doesn't it? I can easily supply that by using something that looks more like money than a bar does: moneybags. One moneybag for the unfortunate Rotundian's pittance, two for the American's wage. Or three for the Rotundian, six for the American. Either way, the chart remains honest and clear, and it will not deceive your hasty glance. That is the way an honest pictograph is made.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/739bd0a0a8a09be9906793b86440d467.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=af839267d4408d5a2dad86c3ecfd7cadbe3901aedb46580df4a8b4d32628882f)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/739bd0a0a8a09be9906793b86440d467.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=af839267d4408d5a2dad86c3ecfd7cadbe3901aedb46580df4a8b4d32628882f)

如果我只是想传递信息的话，那样就足够了。但我想要更多。我想说美国工人比罗通迪亚人境况好得多；而且我越能夸大30与60之间的差距，对我的论点就越有利。说实话（当然，这正是我打算不去做的事），我希望你从中推断出某些东西，留下夸张的印象，但我不想被识破我的伎俩。有一种方法，它每天都被用来欺骗你。

<!--en-->
That would satisfy me if all I wanted was to communicate information. But I want more. I want to say that the American workingman is vastly better off than the Rotundian, and the more I can dramatize the difference between thirty and sixty the better it will be for my argument. To tell the truth (which, of course, is what I am planning not to do), I want you to infer something, to come away with an exaggerated impression, but I don't want to be caught at my tricks. There is a way, and it is one that is being used every day to fool you.

我只需画一个钱袋来代表罗通迪安人的30美元，然后再画一个高度为其两倍的钱袋来代表美国人的60美元。这样比例合适吧？

<!--en-->
I simply draw a moneybag to represent the Rotundian's thirty dollars, and then I draw another one twice as tall to represent the American's sixty. That's in proportion, isn't it?

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a358b5d6b224921be5a2c4396dc5d869.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=fc750b06bc86ba1354fb44304795d1049e34217a8c3ae441e2f6873a9650ccbc)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a358b5d6b224921be5a2c4396dc5d869.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=fc750b06bc86ba1354fb44304795d1049e34217a8c3ae441e2f6873a9650ccbc)

现在，*这*正是我想要营造的印象。如今美国人的工资远远超过了外国人。

<!--en-->
Now *that* gives the impression I'm after. The American's wage now dwarfs the foreigner's.

当然，问题在于此：由于第二个钱袋的高度是第一袋的两倍，其宽度也是两倍。因此它在页面上所占的面积不是两倍，而是四倍。数字上虽仍显示为二比一，但大多数时候占主导地位的视觉印象却显示比例为四比一，甚至更糟。由于这些图片描绘的是具有三维空间的物体，第二个钱袋的厚度也必定是第一袋的两倍。正如几何课本中所说，相似立体的体积与其任一对应维度的立方成正比。二乘二乘二等于八。如果一个钱袋能装30美元，那么体积为前者八倍的另一个钱袋所装的就不是60美元，而是240美元。

<!--en-->
The catch, of course, is this. Because the second bag is twice as high as the first, it is also twice as wide. It occupies not twice but four times as much area on the page. The numbers still say two to one, but the visual impression, which is the dominating one most of the time, says the ratio is four to one. Orworse. Since these are pictures of objects having in reality three dimensions, the second must also be twice as thick as the first. As your geometry book put it, the volumes of similar solids vary as the cube of any like dimension. Two times two times two is eight. If one moneybag holds $30, the other, having eight times the volume, must hold not $60 but $240.

而这正是我那张巧妙的小图表所传达的印象。虽然我说的是“两倍”，但它却给人留下了八比一这一压倒性比例的深刻印象。

<!--en-->
And that indeed is the impression my ingenious little chart gives. While saying “twice,” I have left the lasting impression of an overwhelming eight-to-one ratio.

你同样很难将任何犯罪意图归咎于我。我只是在做很多其他人都在做的事。《新闻周刊》杂志也这么做了——而且还是涉及大笔金钱的交易。

<!--en-->
You’ll have trouble pinning any criminal intent on me, too. I am only doing what a great many other people do. Newsweek magazine has done it—with moneybags at that.

美国钢铁协会做到了这一点，他们用两座高炉来展示。其意图在于说明20世纪30年代至40年间钢铁行业的生产能力是如何迅猛发展的，从而表明该行业完全有能力自行发展，无需政府干预。这一原则本身比其呈现方式更具价值。代表30年代新增一千万吨产能的高炉，其高度仅为40年代新增一千四百二十五万吨产能高炉的三分之二多一点。肉眼可见的是两座高炉，其中一座的体积几乎是另一座的三倍。说“将近一点五倍”却被听成“三倍”——这正是单一维度图像所能造成的效果。

<!--en-->
The American Iron and Steel Institute has done it, with a pair of blast furnaces. The idea was to show how the industry’s steelmaking capacity had boomed between the 1930s and the 1940s and so indicate that the industry was doing such a job on its own hook that any governmental interference was uncalled for. There is more merit in the principle than in the way it was presented. The blast furnace representing the ten-million-ton capacity added in the ‘30s was drawn just over two-thirds as tall as the one for the fourteen and a quarter million tons added in the ’40s. The eye saw two furnaces, one of them close to three times as big as the other. To say “almost one and one-half” and to be heard as “three—that’s what the one-dimensional picture can accomplish.”

这件由钢铁人创作的艺术品还有一些其他值得注意之处。不知为何，第二座熔炉在水平方向上膨胀得比邻近的熔炉更为严重；而那根象征熔融铁的黑色条状物，其长度竟达到了十年前的两倍半。原本只有50%的增长率，却被描绘成150%，从而营造出一种视觉上的错觉——除非我的计算尺和我的理解力已经跟不上这种夸张的表现手法——最终呈现出的比例竟然超过了1500%。数学在这里变成了幻想。

<!--en-->
This piece of art work by the steel people had some other points of interest. Somehow the second furnace had fattened out horizontally beyond the proportion of its neighbor, and a black bar, suggesting molten iron, had become two and one-half times as long as in the earlier decade. Here was a 50 per cent increase given, then drawn as 150 per cent to give a visual impression of—unless my slide rule and I are getting out of their depth — over 1500 per cent. Arithmetic becomes fantasy.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f390b7abf57a8c6394129ef7636116f2.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=36fb89d89e8d85ce8e7bc3502288a758b208504fcac125ff552d6d22ce13193f)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f390b7abf57a8c6394129ef7636116f2.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=36fb89d89e8d85ce8e7bc3502288a758b208504fcac125ff552d6d22ce13193f)

*经STEELWAYS许可改编。*

<!--en-->
*Adapted by courtesy of STEELWAYS.*

（实在不忍心提及：同一张光面四色页面上展示的截断折线图竟也算得上是中上水平的范例。由于图表下半部分被省略，曲线便夸大了人均炼钢产能的增长情况。这样既能节省纸张，又能让增长速率看起来翻倍。）

<!--en-->
(It is almost too unkind to mention that the same glossy four-color page offers a fair-to-prime specimen of the truncated line graph. A curve exaggerates the per-capita growth of steelmaking capacity by getting along with the lower half of its graph missing. This saves paper and doubles the rate of climb.)

其中一些可能只是粗制滥造的草图而已。但这有点像被少找了钱：当所有错误都对收银员有利时，你难免会心生疑虑。

<!--en-->
Some of this may be no more than sloppy draftsmanship. But it is rather like being short-changed: When all the mistakes are in the cashier's favor, you can't help wondering.

《新闻周刊》曾通过一张图表来展示“美国老年人日益长寿”的现象：图中出现两个男性形象，一个代表当今68.2岁的预期寿命，另一个则代表1879年至1888年间的34年预期寿命。这其实是个老掉牙的故事：其中一个形象的高度是另一个的两倍，因此其体积或重量也会是八倍之多。这张图片为了制造更吸引人的报道而夸大了事实，我将其称为一种黄色新闻手法。该期杂志中还包含了一张被截短处理的、故弄玄虚的折线图。

<!--en-->
*Newsweek* once showed how “U. S. Old Folks Grow Older” by means of a chart on which appeared two male figures, one representing the 68.2-year life expectancy of today, the other the 34-year life expectancy of 1879-1889. It was the same old story: One figure was twice as tall as the other and so would have had eight times the bulk or weight. This picture sensationalized facts in order to make a better story. I would call it a form of yellow journalism. The same issue of the magazine contained a truncated, or gee-whiz, line graph.

### 不断生长的奶牛

<!--en-->
*THE CRESCIVE COW*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f463c2ea45db5871f2b4e4bec922d252.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=b0cf5463787d471f2684e5a57fc3f99327bfface260c54337896859261a8c9d8)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f463c2ea45db5871f2b4e4bec922d252.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=b0cf5463787d471f2684e5a57fc3f99327bfface260c54337896859261a8c9d8)

在图表中改变物体大小还会带来另一种风险。数据显示，1860年美国有超过八百万头奶牛，而到1936年这一数字超过了两千五百万头。如果用两头奶牛来表示这种增长——其中一头的高度是另一头的三倍——就会如我们之前讨论的那样夸大其词。但对匆匆浏览页面的人来说，效果可能更奇怪：他很容易误以为现在的奶牛比过去更大。

<!--en-->
There is still another kind of danger in varying the size of objects in a chart. It seems that in 1860 there were something over eight million milk cows in the United States and by 1936 there were more than twenty-five million. Showing this increase by drawing two cows, one three times the height of the other, will exaggerate the impression in the manner we have been discussing. But the effect on the hasty scanner of the page may be even stranger: He may easily come away with the idea that cows are bigger now than they used to be.

#### 日益减少的犀牛

<!--en-->
*THE DIMINISHING RHINOCEROS*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/e2a4671e17e907300f81cd702d326a09.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=689409212e348265a545dbd202f19778a84ac71f7e57e30db78f0bef31cd4a59)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/e2a4671e17e907300f81cd702d326a09.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=689409212e348265a545dbd202f19778a84ac71f7e57e30db78f0bef31cd4a59)

把同样的欺骗手段套用到犀牛种群的遭遇上，结果就是如此。奥登·纳什曾将“rhinosterous”与“preposterous”押韵。这个词用来形容这种方法再贴切不过了。

<!--en-->
Apply the same deceptive technique to what has happened to the rhinoceros population and this is what you get. Ogden Nash once rhymed rhinosterous with preposterous. That's the word for the method too.

# 第七章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 7*

## 半依附型人物

<!--en-->
*The Semiattached Figure*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/0fd243c20ff8139ba74bcaf753e85036.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a7ff079801ccca651f3a61f784bfb24827f58fec87af3fe4fae9d7561f6950fe)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/0fd243c20ff8139ba74bcaf753e85036.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a7ff079801ccca651f3a61f784bfb24827f58fec87af3fe4fae9d7561f6950fe)

如果你无法证明你想证明的东西，那就展示别的事物，并假装它们是一回事。在统计数据与人类思维碰撞后产生的迷雾中，几乎没人会察觉其中的差别。“半附和式说法”是一种绝对能帮到你、让你受益匪浅的技巧——它向来如此。

<!--en-->
IF YOU can't prove what you want to prove, demonstrate something else and pretend that they are the same thing. In the daze that follows the collision of statistics with the human mind, hardly anybody will notice the difference. The semiattached figure is a device guaranteed to stand you in good stead. It always has.

你无法证明你的灵药能治愈感冒，但你可以刊登一份（用大字印刷的）经过认证的实验室报告，声称半盎司该药物能在11秒内杀死试管中的31,108个病菌。与此同时，务必确保该实验室信誉良好或拥有响亮的名头。将这份报告全文转载出来。再找一位身穿白大褂、类似医生的模特拍照，把他的照片附在旁边。

<!--en-->
You can't prove that your nostrum cures colds, but you can publish (in large type) a sworn laboratory report that half an ounce of the stuff killed 31,108 germs in a test tube in eleven seconds. While you are about it, make sure that the laboratory is reputable or has an impressive name. Reproduce the report in full. Photograph a doctor-type model in white clothes and put his picture alongside.

但千万别在你的叙述中提及那几个噱头。指出在试管中效果良好的消毒剂在人体喉咙中可能无效——尤其是在按照说明稀释后以避免灼伤喉咙组织时——这可不是你该做的事，对吧？别再通过列举你杀死了哪种病菌来混淆视听。谁知道究竟是什么导致了感冒呢？更何况它很可能根本就不是病菌呢？

<!--en-->
But don't mention the several gimmicks in your story. It is not up to you— is it?—to point out that an antiseptic that works well in a test tube may not perform in the human throat, especially after it has been diluted according to instructions to keep it from burning throat tissue. Don't confuse the issue by telling what kind of germ you killed. Who knows what germ causes colds,
particularly since it probably isn't a germ at all?

事实上，试管中的各种细菌与导致感冒的物质之间并无已知关联，但人们不会如此清晰地思考这个问题，尤其是在他们正不停地打喷嚏的时候。

<!--en-->
In fact, there is no known connection between assorted germs in a test tube and the whatever-it-is that produces colds, but people aren't going to reason that sharply, especially while sniffling.

也许那个太明显了，人们也开始察觉到了，尽管从广告页面上看不出来。不管怎样，这里有一个更隐蔽的版本。

<!--en-->
Maybe that one is too obvious, and people are beginning to catch on,
although it would not appear so from the advertising pages. Anyway, here is a trickier version.

假设在种族偏见日益严重的时期，你受雇去“证明”情况并非如此。这并非一项艰巨的任务。发起一次民意调查，或者更好的是，委托一家信誉良好的机构来代为调查。询问那些具有代表性的普通民众：他们认为黑人与白人获得工作的机会是否均等。每隔一段时间重复进行这项调查，以便能从中得出趋势并加以报告。

<!--en-->
Let us say that during a period in which race prejudice is growing you are employed to “prove” otherwise. It is not a difficult assignment. Set up a poll or, better yet, have the polling done for you by an organization of good reputation. Ask that usual cross section of the population if they think blacks have as good a chance as white people to get jobs. Repeat your polling at intervals so that you will have a trend to report.

普林斯顿大学公众舆论研究办公室曾对这个问题进行过一次测试。

<!--en-->
Princeton's Office of Public Opinion Research tested this question once.

调查结果揭示了一个有趣的现象：事情往往并非表面上看起来的那样，尤其是在民意调查中。每个被问及就业问题的人，还会被询问一些旨在判断其是否对黑人存在强烈偏见的问题。结果显示，偏见最严重的人最有可能对有关就业机会的问题回答“是”。（数据显示：大约三分之二对黑人持同情态度的人认为，黑人的就业机会不如白人；而约三分之二有偏见的人则表示，黑人获得的机遇与白人相当。）很明显，从这项调查中你很难了解到关于黑人就业状况的真实情况，不过或许能从中窥见一个人对种族问题的态度。

<!--en-->
What turned up is interesting evidence that things, especially in opinion polls,
are not always what they seem. Each person who was asked the question about jobs was also asked some questions designed to discover if he was strongly prejudiced against blacks. It turned out that people most strongly prejudiced were most likely to answer Yes to the question about job opportunities. (It worked out that about two-thirds of those who were sympathetic toward blacks did not think the black had as good a chance at a job as a white person did, and about two-thirds of those showing prejudice said that blacks were getting as good breaks as whites.) It was pretty evident that from this poll you would learn very little about employment conditions for blacks, although you might learn some interesting things about a man's racial attitudes.

由此可见，如果在调查期间偏见日益严重，你就会得到越来越多这样的回答：黑人与白人获得工作的机会是均等的。于是你公布调查结果：你的调查显示黑人正越来越受到公平对待。

<!--en-->
You can see, then, that if prejudice is mounting during your polling period you will get an increasing number of answers to the effect that blacks have as good a chance at jobs as whites. So you announce your results: Your poll shows that blacks are getting a fairer shake all the time.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/4cb701d68b127550fe4ba83e21d3e38f.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=590676534f9b0c81580b491cad48b682ce73095fb0c2a45b3e13f75bd694eacc)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/4cb701d68b127550fe4ba83e21d3e38f.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=590676534f9b0c81580b491cad48b682ce73095fb0c2a45b3e13f75bd694eacc)

通过巧妙运用半依附性数据，你取得了了不起的成就。情况越糟糕，你的统计结果就越能将其美化。

<!--en-->
You have achieved something remarkable by careful use of a semiattached figure. The worse things get, the better your poll makes them look.

再比如这个例子：“在一项针对众多知名医生的大样本调查中，有27%的人抽Throaties牌香烟——这一比例高于其他任何品牌。”当然，这个数字本身可能是虚假的，但那其实无关紧要。对于如此不相关的数字，唯一的回应就是“那又怎样？”尽管我们对医学界怀有应有的尊重，但医生们对烟草品牌的了解会比你更多吗？他们是否有内部信息可以帮助他们选出危害最小的香烟？显然没有，你的医生也会首先承认这一点。然而，那个“27%”的数字却偏偏让人觉得它意味深长。

<!--en-->
Or take this one: “27 per cent of a large sample of eminent physicians smoke Throaties—more than any other brand.” The figure itself may be phony, of course, in any of several ways, but that really doesn’t make any difference. The only answer to a figure so irrelevant is “So what?” With all proper respect toward the medical profession, do doctors know any more about tobacco brands than you do? Do they have any inside information that permits them to choose the least harmful among cigarettes? Of course they don’t, and your doctor would be the first to say so. Yet that “27 per cent” somehow manages to sound as if it meant something.

现在把比例下调1%，来看看榨汁机的情况。它被大肆宣传为一种“经实验室测试证明能多榨出26%果汁”的设备，并且还得到了《Good Housekeeping》杂志的背书。

<!--en-->
Now slip back one per cent and consider the case of the juice extractor. It was widely advertised as a device that “extracts 26 per cent more juice” as “proved by laboratory test” and “vouched for by Good Housekeeping Institute.”

听起来确实不错。如果能买到效率高出26%的榨汁机，何必买别的呢？不过先不说“实验室测试”（尤其是“独立实验室测试”）能证明一些多么离谱的事情，那个数字到底意味着什么？比什么多26%？最终查明，它仅仅表示这种榨汁机比老式手动榨汁器能多榨出那么多果汁而已。这与购买时所需的关键数据毫无关系；这种榨汁机可能是市场上最差的一种。除了数字精确得令人怀疑外，那26%的数据完全无关紧要。

<!--en-->
That sounds right good. If you can buy a juicer that is twenty-six per cent more effective, why buy any other kind? Well now, without going into the fact that “laboratory tests” (especially “independent laboratory tests”) have proved some of the darndest things, just what does that figure mean? Twenty-six per cent more than what? When it was finally pinned down it was found to mean only that this juicer got out that much more juice than an old-fashioned hand reamer could. It had absolutely nothing to do with the data you would want before purchasing; this juicer might be the poorest on the market. Besides being suspiciously precise, that twenty-six per cent figure is totally irrelevant.

如果你放任不管，用数字欺骗你的不只是广告商。《This Week》杂志发表的一篇关于驾驶安全的文章，无疑是出于为你好，文中告诉你如果“以每小时70英里的速度在公路上横冲直撞”，会发生什么。文章称，如果是早上七点，你存活的几率会是晚上七点的四倍。依据是：“下午7点发生的公路死亡事故是上午7点的四倍。”这话虽大致属实，但结论却站不住脚。傍晚死亡人数更多，仅仅是因为那时在公路上行驶的人更多。作为单独一名司机，你傍晚时可能面临更大危险，但数字本身并不能证明这一点。

<!--en-->
Advertisers aren’t the only people who will fool you with numbers if you let them. An article on driving safety, published by *This Week* magazine undoubtedly with your best interests at heart, told you what might happen to you if you went “hurtling down the highway at 70 miles an hour, careening from side to side.” You would have, the article said, four times as good a chance of staying alive if the time were seven in the morning than if it were seven at night. The evidence: “Four times more fatalities occur on thehighways at 7 P.M. than at 7 A.M.” Now that is approximately true, but the conclusion doesn’t follow. More people are killed in the evening than in the morning simply because more people are on the highways then to be killed. You, a single driver, may be in greater danger in the evening, but there is nothing in the figures to prove it either way.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b72c8e5a728bb6fe2ddc0bc814be96c5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=aa861fa252fd89f9d2fbac9964fc772dc9d1a0fb7a69033ee86472436e9f2228)

利用文章作者所用的那种荒谬逻辑，你甚至可以证明晴天比雾天更危险。因为晴天发生的事故更多，而晴天的时间也比雾天更长。不过，雾天驾驶可能确实更加危险。

<!--en-->
By the same kind of nonsense that the article writer used you can show that clear weather is more dangerous than foggy weather. More accidents occur in clear weather, because there is more clear weather than foggy weather. All the same, fog may be much more dangerous to drive in.

只要不注意数字之间的关联程度，你就可以利用事故统计数据把自己吓得要死，无论涉及哪种交通工具……

<!--en-->
You can use accident statistics to scare yourself to death in connection with any kind of transportation... if you fail to note how poorly attached the figures are.

去年因飞机事故死亡的人数比1910年更多。所以现代飞机更危险吗？胡说。只不过现在乘飞机的人多了几百倍罢了。

<!--en-->
More people were killed by airplanes last year than in 1910. Therefore modern planes are more dangerous? Nonsense. There are hundreds of times more people flying now, that’s all.

据报道，某一年因铁路事故导致的死亡人数为4,712人。这似乎成了远离火车、选择开车的充分理由。但当你深入探究这个数字的含义时，会发现它代表的意思截然不同。近一半的遇难者是那些在十字路口与火车相撞的汽车乘客；其余大部分则是铁路工人。在4,712人中，只有132人是火车乘客。而且即便这个数字本身也缺乏比较价值，除非它能与总客运里程的数据结合起来。

<!--en-->
It was reported that the number of deaths chargeable to steam railroads in one recent year was 4,712. That sounds like a good argument for staying off trains, perhaps for sticking to your automobile instead. But when you investigate to find what the figure is all about, you learn it means something quite different. Nearly half those victims were people whose automobiles collided with trains at crossings. The greater part of the rest were riding the rods. Only 132 out of the 4,712 were passengers on trains. And even that figure is worth little for purposes of comparison unless it is attached to information on total passenger miles.

如果你担心横跨全国旅行时的遇难风险，那么去询问去年火车、飞机或汽车哪类交通工具致死人数最多，并不会给你提供多少有用信息。你应该查询每百万客运里程的死亡人数比率。这样才能最接近地反映出你面临的最大风险所在。

<!--en-->
If you are worried about your chances of being killed on a coast-to-coast trip, you won’t get much relevant information by asking whether trains, planes, or cars killed the greatest number of people last year. Get the rate, by inquiring into the number of fatalities for each million passenger miles. Thatwill come closest to telling you where your greatest risk lies.

把某事物的数量统计出来后再以另一种方式呈现，这类做法还有很多种。通常的方法是选取两个发音相同但含义不同的词。作为一家正与工会激烈对抗的公司的人事经理，你会“开展调查”来了解有多少员工对工会不满。除非工会是一群由大天使领导的天使，否则你完全可以诚实地询问并记录下来，最终得出大部分员工确实有所抱怨的结论。随后你将信息整理成报告，称“绝大多数人——占78%——反对该工会”。你其实只是把一堆杂乱无章的抱怨和牢骚汇总起来，然后给它们起个听起来相似的新名称而已。你并未证明任何事情，但听起来却好像证明了什么，不是吗？

<!--en-->
There are many other forms of counting up something and then reporting it as something else. The general method is to pick two things that sound the same but are not. As personnel manager for a company that is scrapping with a union you “make a survey” of employees to find out how many have a complaint against the union. Unless the union is a band of angels with an archangel at their head you can ask and record with perfect honesty and come out with proof that the greater part of the men do have some complaint or other. You issue your information as a report that “a vast majority—78 per cent—are opposed to the union.” What you have done is to add up a bunch of undifferentiated complaints and tiny gripes and then call them something else that sounds like the same thing. You haven’t proved a thing, but it rather sounds as if you have, doesn’t it?

不过从某种角度来说，这也算公平。工会同样可以轻易地“证明”几乎所有工人都反对工厂的管理方式。

<!--en-->
It is fair enough, though, in a way. The union can just as readily “prove” that practically all the workers object to the way the plant is being run.

如果你想寻找这类“牵强附会的数据”，不妨看看公司的财务报表。留意那些看似数额过大因而被隐藏在其他名目下的利润。《联合汽车工人杂志》（*Ammunition*）对此类手段的描述如下：

<!--en-->
If you’d like to go on a hunt for semiattached figures, you might try running through corporation financial statements. Watch for profits that might look too big and so are concealed under another name. The United Automobile Workers’ magazine *Ammunition* describes the device this way:

报表显示，去年该公司获利3500万美元，仅占每美元销售额中的1.5美分。你可能会为该公司感到难过：厕所里的灯泡烧坏了，更换它就要花费30美分。就这样，相当于20美元销售额所产生的利润就没了。这真让人想少用点纸巾啊！

<!--en-->
The statement says, last year the company made $35 million in profits. Just one and a half cents out of every sales dollar. You feel sorry for the company. A bulb burns out in the latrine. To replace it, the company has to spend 30 cents. Just like that, there is the profit on 20 sales dollars. Makes a man want to go easy on the paper towels.

当然，实际情况是：公司所申报的利润其实只有实际利润的一半或三分之一。未被申报的部分被隐藏在折旧、特别折旧以及应急储备金之中。

<!--en-->
But, of course, the truth is, what the company reports as profits is only a half or a third of the profits. The part that isn’t reported is hidden in depreciation, and special depreciation, and in reserves for contingencies.

百分比的运用也同样充满趣味。最近九个月内，通用汽车公司报告的税后销售利润率仅为12.6%，这一数字看似并不起眼。但同一时期，通用汽车的投资利润率却达到了44.8%——这个数字听起来要么更糟，要么更好，完全取决于你想支持哪种论点。

<!--en-->
Equally gay fun is to be had with percentages. For a recent nine-month period General Motors was able to report a relatively modest profit (after taxes) of 12.6 per cent on sales. But for that same period GM’s profit on its investment came to 44.8 per cent, which sounds a good deal worse—or better, depending on what kind of argument you are trying to win.

同样，《哈珀斯杂志》（*Harper’s*）的一位读者在该刊的信件专栏中为A&P超市辩护，指出其销售净利率仅为1.1%。他问道：“难道有哪个美国公民会因为每年每投资1000美元就能赚回10多美元而被视为牟取暴利的奸商吗？”

<!--en-->
Similarly, a reader of *Harper’s* magazine came to the defense of the A & P stores in that magazine’s letters column by pointing to low net earnings of only 1.1 per cent on sales. He asked, “Would any American citizen fear public condemnation as a profiteer… for realizing a little over $10 for every $1,000invested during a year?”

乍一听，1.1%这个数字似乎小得令人担忧。与我们熟悉的联邦住房管理局抵押贷款、银行贷款等所涉及的4%至6%甚至更高的利率相比，这个数字显得微不足道。如果A&P放弃杂货业务，把资金存入银行靠利息生活，岂不是更好？

<!--en-->
Offhand this 1.1 per cent sounds almost distressingly small. Compare it with the four to six per cent or more interest that most of us are familiar with from FHA mortgages and bank loans and such. Wouldn’t the A & P be better off if it went out of the grocery business and put its capital into the bank and lived off interest?

问题在于：年度投资回报率与总销售额产生的收益并非一回事。另一位读者在后来一期的《哈珀斯杂志》中回应道：“如果我每天早上花99美分购进一件商品，下午以1美元的价格卖出，那么我的总销售额利润率仅为1%，但全年投入资金的回报率却高达365%。”

<!--en-->
The catch is that annual return on investment is not the same kettle of fish as earnings on total sales. As another reader replied in a later issue of *Harper’s*, “If I purchase an article every morning for 99 cents and sell it each afternoon for one dollar, I will make only 1 per cent on total sales, but 365 per cent on invested money during the year.”

表达同一个数字的方式往往有很多种。例如，你可以将其表述为销售利润率1%、投资回报率15%、1000万美元的利润、较1935–1939年平均值增长40%的利润，或是比去年减少60%的利润。关键在于选择最符合当前目的的表述方式，并指望读者不会察觉到它并不能准确反映实际情况。

<!--en-->
There are often many ways of expressing any figure. You can, for instance, express exactly the same fact by calling it a one per cent return on sales, a fifteen per cent return on investment, a ten-million-dollar profit, an increase in profits of forty per cent (compared with 1935-39 average), or a decrease of sixty per cent from last year. The method is to choose the one that sounds best for the purpose at hand and trust that few who read it will recognize how imperfectly it reflects the situation.

并非所有的牵强附会数据都是故意欺骗的产物。许多统计数据，包括对每个人都很重要的医疗数据，都会因源头上报不一致而被扭曲。关于堕胎、非婚生育和梅毒等敏感问题，相关数据往往存在惊人的矛盾。如果你查阅最新的流感和肺炎病例数据，可能会得出一个奇怪的结论：这些疾病几乎只集中在三个南部州，它们占了报告病例数的约80%。实际上，造成这一比例的原因是这三个州在其他州停止报告后仍要求继续上报。

<!--en-->
Not all semiattached figures are products of intentional deception. Many statistics, including medical ones that are pretty important to everybody, are distorted by inconsistent reporting at the source. There are startlingly contradictory figures on such delicate matters as abortions, illegitimate births, and syphilis. If you should look up the latest available figures on influenza and pneumonia, you might come to the strange conclusion that these ailments are practically confined to three southern states, which account for about eighty per cent of the reported cases. What actually explains this percentage is the fact that these three states required reporting of the ailments after other states had stopped doing so.

某些疟疾数据其实意义不大。1940年之前，美国南部每年有数十万例疟疾病例，如今却仅剩寥寥几例——这一在短短几年内发生的令人欣慰且看似重要的变化，实际上只是因为现在只有确诊的病例才会被记录为疟疾；而过去在美国南部，人们常把“疟疾”一词用作感冒或发冷的俗称。

<!--en-->
Some malaria figures mean as little. Where before 1940 there were hundreds of thousands of cases a year in the American South there are now only a handful, a salubrious and apparently important change that took place in just a few years. But all that has happened in actuality is that cases are now recorded only when proved to be malaria, where formerly the word was used in much of the South as a colloquialism for a cold or chill.

美西战争期间，海军中的死亡率为千分之九；同期纽约市的平民死亡率为千分之十六。后来，海军招募人员利用这些数字来证明：服役于海军比不服役更安全。假设这些数字准确无误（很可能确实如此），请稍停片刻，看看你能否发现为何它们——或者至少招募人员据此得出的结论——几乎毫无意义。

<!--en-->
The death rate in the Navy during the Spanish-American War was nine per thousand. For civilians in New York City during the same period it was sixteen per thousand. Navy recruiters later used these figures to show that it was safer to be in the Navy than out of it. Assume these figures to be accurate, as they probably are. Stop for a moment and see if you can spotwhat makes them, or at least the conclusion the recruiting people drew from them, virtually meaningless.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/4a260314970737c7bbc50a12d3404a8a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a8602c36596b440313cf39b8f616ed79f730acce8692341f127bad6c5840d127)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/4a260314970737c7bbc50a12d3404a8a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=a8602c36596b440313cf39b8f616ed79f730acce8692341f127bad6c5840d127)

这两组人群并不具备可比性。海军成员主要是健康状况良好的年轻人；而平民人口中则包括婴儿、老人和病人，无论身处何地，他们的死亡率都更高。这些数据根本无法证明符合海军标准的人员在海军中会比在外存活更久，也无法证明相反的情况。

<!--en-->
The groups are not comparable. The Navy is made up mainly of young men in known good health. A civilian population includes infants, the old, and the ill, all of whom have a higher death rate wherever they are. These figures do not at all prove that men meeting Navy standards will live longer in the Navy than out. They do not prove the contrary either.

你可能听说了这个令人沮丧的消息：1952年是医学史上脊髓灰质炎最严重的一年。这一结论基于看似无可挑剔的证据：当年报告的病例数前所未有地多。

<!--en-->
You may have heard the discouraging news that 1952 was the worst polio year in medical history. This conclusion was based on what might seem all the evidence anyone could ask for: There were far more cases reported in that year than ever before.

但专家深入剖析这些数据后，发现了一些较为乐观的现象。其一，1952年处于最易感染年龄段的儿童数量众多，即便发病率保持不变，病例数也注定会创下纪录；其二，人们对脊髓灰质炎的普遍关注促使医生更频繁地诊断和记录轻症病例；其三，经济激励因素也有所增加——脊髓灰质炎保险增多，国家小儿麻痹症基金会提供的援助也更丰富。所有这些因素都让人对“脊髓灰质炎达到新高峰”的说法产生怀疑，而死亡总数的情况也印证了这种怀疑。

<!--en-->
But when experts went back of these figures they found a few things that were more encouraging. One was that there were so many children at the most susceptible ages in 1952 that cases were bound to be at a record number if the rate remained level. Another was that a general consciousness of polio was leading to more frequent diagnosis and recording of mild cases. Finally, there was an increased financial incentive, there being more polio insurance and more aid available from the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis. All this threw considerable doubt on the notion that polio had reached a new high, and the total number of deaths confirmed the doubt.

一个有趣的事实是：死亡率或死亡人数往往比直接的发病数据更能反映某种疾病的流行程度——仅仅是因为关于死亡的报告与记录质量要高得多。在这个例子中，那个看似“半关联”的数据反而比表面上看似完全关联的数据更有参考价值。

<!--en-->
It is an interesting fact that the death rate or number of deaths often is a better measure of the incidence of an ailment than direct incidence figures—simply because the quality of reporting and record-keeping is so much higher on fatalities. In this instance, the obviously semiattached figure is better than the one that on the face of it seems fully attached.

在美国，这种“半关联”数据每四年就会迎来一次爆发式增长。这并非说明数据本身具有周期性，而仅仅意味着选举季到了。1948年10月共和党发布的竞选声明完全建立在看似相互关联实则不然的数字之上：

<!--en-->
In America the semiattached figure enjoys a big boom every fourth year. This indicates not that the figure is cyclical in nature, but only that campaign time has arrived. A campaign statement issued by the Republican party in October of 1948 is built entirely on figures that appear to be attached to each other but are not:

杜威于1942年当选州长时，某些地区的教师最低年薪仅为900美元。如今，纽约州的教师享有世界上最高的薪资。根据杜威州长的建议——该建议源自他任命的委员会的调查结果——立法机构于1947年从州财政盈余中拨款3200万美元，用于立即提高教师薪资。结果，纽约市教师的最低薪资达到了2,500美元至5,325美元不等。

<!--en-->
When Dewey was elected Governor in 1942, the minimum teacher's salary in some districts was as low as $900 a year. Today the school teachers in New York State enjoy the highest salaries in the world. Upon Governor Dewey's recommendation, based on the findings of a Committee he appointed, the Legislature in 1947 appropriated $32,000,000 out of a state surplus to provide an immediate increase in the salaries of school teachers. As a result the minimum salaries of teachers in New York City range from $2,500 to $5,325.

杜威先生或许确为教师的朋友，但这些数字并不能说明这一点。这是典型的“前后对比”手法，其中引入了许多未提及的因素并故意歪曲其本质。这里所谓的“之前”是900美元，而“之后”则是2,500美元至5,325美元，听起来确实是巨大改善。但实际上，那个小数额是该州某个农村地区的最低薪资，而大额数字仅指纽约市范围内的薪资范围。杜威州长任期内或许确有改善，也许并没有。

<!--en-->
It is entirely possible that Mr. Dewey has proved himself the teacher's friend, but these figures don't show it. It is the old before-and-after trick, with a number of un-mentioned factors introduced and made to appear what they are not. Here you have a "before" of $900 and an "after" of $2,500 to $5,325, which sounds like an improvement indeed. But the small figure is the lowest salary in any rural district of the state, and the big one is the range in New York City alone. There may have been an improvement under Governor Dewey, and there may not.

这份声明体现了一种统计学上的“前后对比”手法，这在杂志和广告中十分常见。人们会拍摄同一间客厅的两张照片，以展示刷漆所能带来的巨大改善效果。但在两次拍摄之间，新家具已被添置进去；有时“之前”的照片还是光线昏暗的黑白小图，而“之后”则是色彩鲜艳的大幅照片。又或者，一对照片展示的是女孩使用护发素后的变化——天哪，她确实看起来更好了。但仔细观察后会发现，大部分改变其实源于让她微笑以及给头发打背光的效果。与其说是护发素的功效，不如说是摄影师的功劳。

<!--en-->
This statement illustrates a statistical form of the before-and-after photograph that is a familiar stunt in magazines and advertising. A living room is photographed twice to show you what a vast improvement a coat of paint can make. But between the two exposures new furniture has been added, and sometimes the "before" picture is a tiny one in poorly lighted black-and-white and the "after" version is a big photograph in full color. Or a pair of pictures shows you what happened when a girl began to use a hair rinse. By golly, she does look better afterwards at that. But most of the change, you note on careful inspection, has been wrought by persuading her to smile and throwing a back light on her hair. More credit belongs to the photographer than to the rinse.

# 第八章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 8*

## 事后归因谬误再度上演

<!--en-->
*Post Hoc Rides Again*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/fde5c47f9f163bc4dac4caf96cc63c0e.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=614cc9f4bcad7333a1e211b696ebd9ab1ba3e8e6135a68b57f55996e28ce7dda)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/fde5c47f9f163bc4dac4caf96cc63c0e.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=614cc9f4bcad7333a1e211b696ebd9ab1ba3e8e6135a68b57f55996e28ce7dda)

有人曾费尽周折去研究吸烟者的大学生成绩是否低于不吸烟者。结果证实确实如此。这一发现让不少人欣喜不已，此后他们便大肆宣扬此事。看来，取得好成绩的途径在于戒烟；进而顺理成章地得出结论：吸烟会使人头脑迟钝。

<!--en-->
SOMEBODY once went to a good deal of trouble to find out if cigarette smokers make lower college grades than non-smokers. It turned out that they did. This pleased a good many people and they have been making much of it ever since. The road to good grades, it would appear, lies in giving up smoking; and, to carry the conclusion one reasonable step further, smoking makes dull minds.

我认为这项研究做得相当严谨：样本量足够大，选取过程诚实且细致，相关性也具备高度显著性，等等。

<!--en-->
This particular study was, I believe, properly done: sample big enough and honestly and carefully chosen, correlation having a high significance, and so on.

这种谬误由来已久，却极易在统计资料中浮现，并被一堆看似惊人的数字所掩盖。其逻辑就是：如果B紧随A之后发生，那么A便是B的原因。

<!--en-->
The fallacy is an ancient one which, however, has a powerful tendency to crop up in statistical material, where it is disguised by a welter of impressivefigures. It is the one that says that if B follows A, then A has caused B.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/e55fae09f499e1002538b297b1f1198e.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=e180c08160d7e08047a568609a40f9a98273afb994c0afdb86015d730ebf5e62)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/e55fae09f499e1002538b297b1f1198e.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=e180c08160d7e08047a568609a40f9a98273afb994c0afdb86015d730ebf5e62)

人们无端假定：既然吸烟与低分并存，那么吸烟导致了低分。难道不可能是反过来吗？或许低分促使学生转向烟草而非酒精。说到底，这种结论与另一种结论同样可信，且都有证据支持。但对宣传者而言，后者显然没那么令人满意。

<!--en-->
An unwarranted assumption is being made that since smoking and low grades go together, smoking causes low grades. Couldn't it just as well be the other way around? Perhaps low marks drive students not to drink but to tobacco. When it comes right down to it, this conclusion is about as likely as the other and just as well supported by the evidence. But it is not nearly so satisfactory to propagandists.

然而，更有可能的情况是：两者并非互相导致，而是均由某种第三方因素所致。会不会是那些不太认真对待学业、性格外向的人更可能吸烟呢？或者，有人曾发现外向性与低分之间存在相关性——这种关系似乎比成绩与智力之间的关系更紧密——这能否作为线索？也许外向者比内向者更易吸烟。关键在于：当存在多种合理解释时，你无权只挑选符合自己口味的那种并固执己见。但许多人恰恰如此。

<!--en-->
It seems a good deal more probable, however, that neither of these things has produced the other, but both are a product of some third factor. Can it be that the sociable sort of fellow who takes his books less than seriously is also likely to smoke more? Or is there a clue in the fact that somebody once established a correlation between extroversion and low grades—a closer relationship apparently than the one between grades and intelligence? Maybe extroverts smoke more than introverts. The point is that when there are many reasonable explanations you are hardly entitled to pick one that suits your taste and insist on it. But many people do.

为了避免陷入“事后归因”的谬误，从而避免相信许多并不属实之事，你必须对任何相关性陈述进行严格审查。那个看似能证明某事物因另一事物而产生的、精确得令人信服的数字，实际上可能属于多种类型之一。

<!--en-->
To avoid falling for the *post hoc* fallacy and thus wind up believing many things that are not so, you need to put any statement of relationship through a sharp inspection. The correlation, that convincingly precise figure that seems to prove that something is because of something, can actually be any of several types.

其中一种是由偶然性产生的相关性。你或许能凑出一组数字来证明某种不太可能的事情，但若再次尝试，下一组数字可能根本无法证明其存在。就像那家声称能减少蛀牙的牙膏制造商一样，他们只会丢弃不想要的结果，而大肆宣扬有利的数据。样本量越小，你就越容易找到任意两种特征或事件之间的显著相关性。

<!--en-->
One is the correlation produced by chance. You may be able to get together a set of figures to prove some unlikely thing in this way, but if you try again, your next set may not prove it at all. As with the manufacturer of the tooth paste that appeared to reduce decay, you simply throw away the results youdon't want and publish widely those you do. Given a small sample, you are likely to find some substantial correlation between any pair of characteristics or events that you can think of.

一种常见的共变现象是：关系确实存在，但无法确定哪个变量是原因、哪个是结果。在某些情况下，因果关系甚至可能随时间互换，或者两者同时互为因果。收入与股票持有量之间的相关性便属此类：你赚的钱越多，买的股票就越多；买的股票越多，收入也就越高；简单说成其中一方导致了另一方是不准确的。

<!--en-->
A common kind of co-variation is one in which the relationship is real but it is not possible to be sure which of the variables is the cause and which the effect. In some of these instances cause and effect may change places from time to time or indeed both may be cause and effect at the same time. A correlation between income and ownership of stocks might be of that kind. The more money you make, the more stock you buy, and the more stock you buy, the more income you get; it is not accurate to say simply that one has produced the other.

或许最棘手的是那种极为常见的情形：两个变量彼此并无实际影响，却仍存在真实的相关性。利用这一点进行歪曲的情况屡见不鲜。吸烟者成绩差便属于此类；还有太多医学统计数据在引用时未加说明：尽管相关性已被证实，但其因果性质仍只是推测而已。作为这种毫无意义或虚假相关却被视为真实统计事实的例子，有人兴高采烈地指出：马萨诸塞州长老会牧师的薪水与哈瓦那朗姆酒的价格之间存在密切关系。

<!--en-->
Perhaps the trickiest of them all is the very common instance in which neither of the variables has any effect at all on the other, yet there is a real correlation. A good deal of dirty work has been done with this one. The poor grades among cigarette smokers is in this category, as are all too many medical statistics that are quoted without the qualification that although the relationship has been shown to be real, the cause-and-effect nature of it is only a matter of speculation. As an instance of the nonsense or spurious correlation that is a real statistical fact, someone has gleefully pointed to this: There is a close relationship between the salaries of Presbyterian ministers in Massachusetts and the price of rum in Havana.

究竟哪个是原因、哪个是结果？换句话说，是牧师从朗姆酒贸易中获益，还是他们在支持它？好吧，这听起来荒谬至极。但要警惕其他应用“事后归因”逻辑的情况——它们只是更为隐蔽罢了。就牧师与朗姆酒而言，很容易看出两者数值的增长都是受第三方因素影响的：即几乎全世界范围内物价水平的历史性上涨。

<!--en-->
Which is the cause and which the effect? In other words, are the ministers benefiting from the rum trade or supporting it? All right. That's so farfetched that it is ridiculous at a glance. But watch out for other applications of post hoc logic that differ from this one only in being more subtle. In the case of the ministers and the rum it is easy to see that both figures are growing because of the influence of a third factor: the historic and world-wide rise in the price level of practically everything.

再来看看那些显示自杀率在6月达到顶峰的数据。难道自杀者会催生出“六月新娘”吗？或者，六月的婚礼会导致被抛弃者自杀？一个稍显可信（尽管同样未经证实）的解释是：那些整个冬天都靠“春天一切会变好”的想法来勉强忍受抑郁的人，到了六月发现情况依旧糟糕时便放弃了希望。

<!--en-->
And take the figures that show the suicide rate to be at its maximum in June. Do suicides produce June brides —or do June weddings precipitate suicides of the jilted? A somewhat more convincing (though equally unproved) explanation is that the fellow who licks his depression all through the winter with the thought that things will look rosier in the spring gives up when June comes and he still feels terrible.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2ef75c742edbace940e28f8ae60f5700.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=e20fa80bb58af9756f9d5f3ee9c0be5a9c7c44e2efd264d75fa390570cecae1a)

另一件需要注意的情况是：有人将相关性推断为在已有数据范围之外仍然成立。很容易证明，某个地区降雨越多，玉米就长得越高，甚至产量也越大。看来雨水真是恩赐。但持续性的强降雨却可能损害甚至毁掉庄稼。这种正相关关系只在一定限度内成立，过后便会迅速转为负相关——降雨超过一定量后，玉米产量反而会减少。

<!--en-->
Another thing to watch out for is a conclusion in which a correlation has been inferred to continue beyond the data with which it has been demonstrated. It is easy to show that the more it rains in an area, the taller the corn grows or even the greater the crop. Rain, it seems, is a blessing. But a season of very heavy rainfall may damage or even ruin the crop. The positive correlation holds up to a point and then quickly becomes a negative one. Above so-many inches, the more it rains the less corn you get.

我们稍后会仔细看看关于教育经济价值的证据。但眼下先假设已经证明：高中毕业生比辍学者赚得更多，大学每多读一年也能增加收入。不过要警惕那种“上学时间越长，赚钱就越多”的笼统结论。请注意，这一结论并未被证明适用于本科以上的阶段，很可能并不适用。拥有博士学位的人往往成为大学教师，因此并不属于高收入群体。

<!--en-->
We're going to pay a little attention to the evidence on the money value of education in a minute. But for now let's assume it has been proved that high-school graduates make more money than those who drop out, that each year of undergraduate work in college adds some more income. Watch out for the general conclusion that the more you go to school the more money you'll make. Note that this has not been shown to be true for the years beyond an undergraduate degree, and it may very well not apply to them either. People with Ph.D.s quite often become college teachers and so do not become members of the highest income groups.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2b9af30e98bad49cd089c3459bdfd44c.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=6cb758d74cefb1e4504e164a7c65987036064b636cd748875fc796f705b9f62b)

当然，相关性仅表示一种趋势，往往并非理想中的一对一关系。平均而言，高个子男孩比矮个子男孩体重更重，这就是正相关。但你很容易找到身高六英尺却比某些五英尺的人还轻的例子，因此相关系数小于1。负相关则意味着一个变量增加时另一个变量趋于减少。在物理学中，这表现为反比关系：离灯泡越远，书上的光线就越弱；距离增加，光强度便减小。这类物理关系往往能形成完美的相关性，但商业、社会学或医学中的数据很少如此规整。即便教育普遍能提高收入，也可能恰恰导致某个人财务上的破产。请记住：相关性可能是真实存在的，且基于真正的因果关系——但在具体个案中，它几乎毫无用处。

<!--en-->
A correlation of course shows a tendency which is not often the idealrelationship described as one-to-one. Tall boys weigh more than short boys on the average, so this is a positive correlation. But you can easily find a six-footer who weighs less than some five-footers, so the correlation is less than 1. A negative correlation is simply a statement that as one variable increases the other tends to decrease.
