In physics this becomes an inverse ratio: The further you get from a light bulb the less light there is on your book; as distance increases light intensity decreases. These physical relationships often have the kindness to produce perfect correlations, but figures from business or sociology or medicine seldom work out so neatly. Even if education generally increases incomes it may easily turn out to be the financial ruination of Joe over there. Keep in mind that a correlation may be real and based on real cause and effect—and still be almost worthless in determining action in any single case.

人们收集了大量数据来说明大学教育的美元价值，还出版了一堆小册子，向潜在学生宣传这些数字以及据此得出的结论。我并不反对这种意图。我自己也支持教育，尤其是包含基础统计学课程的教育。这些数字已相当明确地表明：上过大学的人比没上过大学的人赚得更多。当然例外情况不少，但总体趋势明显且清晰。

<!--en-->
Reams of pages of figures have been collected to show the value in dollars of a college education, and stacks of pamphlets have been published to bring these figures—and conclusions more or less based on them—to the attention of potential students. I am not quarreling with the intention. I am in favor of education myself, particularly if it includes a course in elementary statistics. Now these figures have pretty conclusively demonstrated that people who have gone to college make more money than people who have not. The exceptions are numerous, of course, but the tendency is strong and clear.

唯一的问题是，伴随这些数据和事实出现的却是一个毫无根据的结论。这正是典型的“事后归因谬误”。它声称这些数据说明：如果你（你的儿子或女儿）上了大学，赚的钱就会比选择其他生活方式的人更多。这一毫无根据的结论建立在同样站不住脚的假设之上：因为受过大学教育的人赚得多，所以是因为他们上了大学。事实上我们并不知道，这些人即便没上大学也可能赚得更多。有几点迹象强烈表明确实如此：大学招收的学生中，聪明人和富家子弟比例过高。聪明人即便没有大学知识也可能具备良好的赚钱能力；至于富人……显然，钱能生钱。无论是否上大学，富人的儿子很少属于低收入阶层。

<!--en-->
The only thing wrong is that along with the figures and facts goes a totally unwarranted conclusion. This is the post hoc fallacy at its best. It says that these figures show that if you (your son, your daughter) attend college you will probably earn more money than if you decide to spend the next four years in some other manner. This unwarranted conclusion has for its basis the equally unwarranted assumption that since college-trained folks make more money, they make it because they went to college. Actually we don't know but that these are the people who would have made more money even if they had not gone to college. There are a couple of things that indicate rather strongly that this is so. Colleges get a disproportionate number of two groups of kids: the bright and the rich. The bright might show good earning power without college knowledge. And as for the rich ones... well, money breeds money in several obvious ways. Few sons of rich men are found in low-income brackets whether they go to college or not.

下面这段文字摘自查问形式的文章，发表于发行量巨大的周日增刊《This Week》杂志上。或许你会和我一样觉得有趣：同一位作者曾写过一篇题为《大众观念：真还是假？》的文章。

<!--en-->
The following passage is taken from an article in question-and-answer form that appeared in *This Week* magazine, a Sunday supplement of enormous circulation. Maybe you will find it amusing, as I do, that the same writer once produced a piece called “Popular Notions: True or False?”

问：上大学对保持单身的概率有何影响？

<!--en-->
Q: What effect does going to college have on your chances of remaining unmarried?

答：如果你是女性，它会使你成为老处女的概率急剧上升；但如果你是男性，效果则恰恰相反——它会降低你保持单身的概率。

<!--en-->
A: If you're a woman, it skyrockets your chances of becoming an old maid. But if you're a man, it has the opposite effect — it minimizes your chances of staying a bachelor.

康奈尔大学对1,500名典型的中年大学毕业生进行了研究。其中，93%的男性已婚（相比之下，普通人群中这一比例为83%）。

<!--en-->
Cornell University made a study of 1,500 typical middle-aged college graduates. Of the men, 93 per cent were married (compared to 83 per cent for the general population).

但在中年女性毕业生中，只有65%的人已婚。在大学毕业生中，未婚女性的数量大约是普通女性群体中未婚女性数量的三倍。

<!--en-->
But of the middle-aged women graduates only 65 per cent were married. Spinsters were relatively three times as numerous among college graduates as among women of the general population.

17岁的苏西·布朗读到这段文字时会认为：如果她上大学，她找到伴侣的可能性会比不上大学时更低。文章就是这么说的，还附有来自权威来源的统计数据作为佐证。不过这些统计数据虽能支持文章观点，却并不能真正证实它；另外请注意，尽管统计数据来自康奈尔大学，但文中的结论并非该校得出——尽管心急的读者可能会误以为如此。

<!--en-->
When Susie Brown, age seventeen, reads this she learns that if she goes to college she will be less likely to get a man than if she doesn't. That is what the article says, and there are statistics from a reputable source to go with it. They go with it, but they don't back it up; and note also that while the statistics are Cornell's the conclusions are not, although a hasty reader may come away with the idea that they are.

这里又一次利用真实的相关性来支撑未经证实的因果关系。或许情况恰恰相反：即便这些女性没有上大学，她们也会保持未婚状态；甚至可能有更多人无法结婚。如果这些可能性并不比作者坚持的观点更站得住脚，那它们或许同样算是合理的结论——也就是说，都只是猜测而已。

<!--en-->
Here again a real correlation has been used to bolster up an unproved cause-and-effect relationship. Perhaps it all works the other way around and those women would have remained unmarried even if they had not gone to college. Possibly even more would have failed to marry. If these possibilities are no better than the one the writer insists upon, they are perhaps just as valid conclusions: that is, guesses.

事实上，有一项证据显示：倾向于终身未婚的特质可能导致一个人选择上大学。金赛博士似乎发现了性欲与教育之间的某种相关性，而这些特质或许在上大学前就已形成。这更让人怀疑“上大学会阻碍结婚”这一说法的可信度。

<!--en-->
Indeed there is one piece of evidence suggesting that a propensity for old-maidhood may lead to going to college. Dr. Kinsey seems to have found some correlation between sexuality and education, with traits perhaps being fixed at pre-college age. That makes it all the more questionable to say that going to college gets in the way of marrying.

给苏西·布朗的提示：事情未必如此。

<!--en-->
Note to Susie Brown: It ain't necessarily so.

曾有一篇医学文章惊恐地指出：饮用牛奶的人群中癌症发病率有所上升。似乎在新英格兰、明尼苏达州、威斯康星州以及瑞士等牛奶产量和消费量大的地区，癌症越来越常见；而在牛奶稀缺的锡兰，癌症则十分罕见。为进一步佐证这一观点，文章还指出：在一些牛奶消费量较低的南部州，癌症发病率较低。此外，文章还提到：喝奶的英国女性患某些类型癌症的几率是很少喝牛奶的日本女性的18倍。

<!--en-->
A medical article once pointed with great alarm to an increase in cancer among milk drinkers. Cancer, it seems, was becoming increasingly frequent in New England, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Switzerland, where a lot of milk is produced and consumed, while remaining rare in Ceylon, where milk is scarce. For further evidence it was pointed out that cancer was less frequent in some Southern states where less milk was consumed. Also, it was pointed out, milk-drinking English women get some kinds of cancer eighteen times as frequently as Japanese women who seldom drink milk.

稍加探究就能找到多种解释这些数据的原因，但单凭一个因素就足以揭穿其中的谬误。癌症主要是一种在中年或之后发作的疾病。瑞士以及前文提到的那些州有一个共同点：当地人口的平均寿命较长。研究开展时，英国女性的平均寿命比日本女性长12年。

<!--en-->
A little digging might uncover quite a number of ways to account for these figures, but one factor is enough by itself to show them up. Cancer is predominantly a disease that strikes in middle life or after. Switzerland and the states mentioned first are alike in having populations with relatively long spans of life. English women at the time the study was made were living an average of twelve years longer than Japanese women.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/446966ae6d5adad5604fc6d2209350e4.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=eabae7be524e643a1301b5f019b549f1716b1c05c24f6358b4d81490534c02b8)

海伦·M·沃克教授举了一个有趣的例子，来说明那种“只要两件事同时变化就认定存在因果关系”的愚蠢想法。在研究女性年龄与某些身体特征之间的关系时，可以先测量行走时双脚的夹角。你会发现，年纪较大的女性这一夹角往往更大。你可能会首先推测：这是不是因为女性随着年龄增长走路时脚会外撇，但马上就能看出这种想法很荒谬。所以看起来似乎是年龄增大导致双脚夹角变大，大多数女性随着年龄增长走路时脚会更往外撇。

<!--en-->
Professor Helen M. Walker has worked out an amusing illustration of the folly in assuming there must be cause and effect whenever two things vary together. In investigating the relationship between age and some physical characteristics of women, begin by measuring the angle of the feet in walking. You will find that the angle tends to be greater among older women. You might first consider whether this indicates that women grow older because they toe out, and you can see immediately that this is ridiculous. So it appears that age increases the angle between the feet, and most women must come to toe out more as they grow older.

任何此类结论很可能都是错误的，也毫无根据。只有通过对同一批女性——或类似的群体——进行长期跟踪研究，才能得出合理结论。这样才能排除此处真正的诱因：年长女性成长于那种教导年轻女士走路时要脚外撇的时代，而较年轻的那一组人则是在这种习惯被摒弃的年代学习正确姿势的。

<!--en-->
Any such conclusion is probably false and certainly unwarranted. You could only reach it legitimately by studying the same women—or possibly equivalent groups—over a period of time. That would eliminate the factor responsible here. Which is that the older women grew up at a time when a young lady was taught to toe out in walking, while the members of the younger group were learning posture in a day when that was discouraged.

当你发现有人——通常是利益相关方——对某种相关性大惊小怪时，首先要看看它是否属于这类由时代潮流或事件发展造成的相关性。在我们这个时代，很容易就能找出任意两组事物之间的正相关关系，比如：大学生人数、精神病院住院人数、香烟消费量、心脏病发病率、X光机使用量、假牙产量、加州教师的薪资、内华达州赌场的盈利额。把其中某一项说成是另一项的原因，显然十分荒谬。但这种现象每天都在发生。

<!--en-->
When you find somebody—usually an interested party—making a fussabout a correlation, look first of all to see if it is not one of this type, produced by the stream of events, the trend of the times. In our time it is easy to show a positive correlation between any pair of things like these: number of students in college, number of inmates in mental institutions, consumption of cigarettes, incidence of heart disease, use of X-ray machines, production of false teeth, salaries of California school teachers, profits of Nevada gambling halls. To call some one of these the cause of some other is manifestly silly. But it is done every day.

允许对统计数据进行处理，任由数字和小数点来模糊因果关系，这种做法与迷信并无二致。而且它往往更具误导性。这就像新赫布里底群岛的居民坚信体虱能带来健康一样。几个世纪的观察让他们发现：身体健康的人通常身上有虱子，而病人则往往没有虱子。这种观察本身准确可靠——多年来的非正式观察往往就是如此。但这些原始人由此得出的结论却值得商榷：虱子使人健康；每个人都应该有虱子。

<!--en-->
Permitting statistical treatment and the hypnotic presence of numbers and decimal points to befog causal relationships is little better than superstition. And it is often more seriously misleading. It is rather like the conviction among the people of the New Hebrides that body lice produce good health. Observation over the centuries had taught them that people in good health usually had lice and sick people very often did not. The observation itself was accurate and sound, as observations made informally over the years surprisingly often are. Not so much can be said for the conclusion to which these primitive people came from their evidence: Lice make a man healthy. Everybody should have them.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/54915514dcc3ea024b60fd1cecb02307.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=372886e29127da8a119e0c323efecf35535866c77a40a0a57f9a67eaafb48580)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/54915514dcc3ea024b60fd1cecb02307.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=372886e29127da8a119e0c323efecf35535866c77a40a0a57f9a67eaafb48580)

正如我们之前提到的，比这更薄弱的证据——经过统计处理后连常识都无法辨识其真相——却造就了诸多医学界的财富以及杂志上的医学文章，包括专业期刊在内。最终，更敏锐的观察者在新赫布里底群岛弄清了真相：实际上，那里几乎所有人大部分时间身上都有虱子。可以说，这是人类的正常状态。然而，一旦有人发烧（很可能是由虱子传播的），体温高到让虱子无法生存时，虱子便会离开。这样一来，因果关系就被彻底扭曲、颠倒且混杂在一起了。

<!--en-->
As we have already noted, scantier evidence than this—treated in the statistical mill until common sense could no longer penetrate to it—has made many a medical fortune and many a medical article in magazines, including professional ones. More sophisticated observers finally got things straightened out in the New Hebrides. As it turned out, almost everybody in those circles had lice most of the time. It was, you might say, the normal condition of man. When, however, anyone took a fever (quite possibly carried to him by those same lice) and his body became too hot for comfortable habitation, the lice left. There you have cause and effect altogetherconfusingly distorted, reversed, and intermingled.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/a6c5b826d845662190f077e2d7fb07ce.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1ee786d16de523923a904320109353ca478cf30c706732a688eeef736ec374f1)

<!--en-->

# 第九章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 9*

如何“统计化”处理数据

<!--en-->
How to Statisticulate

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/db87d285eb797d3471fe3e910ca6f95e.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1cc8fd1670cbbbf9a5f24271879a99b8587703c4143a7f439c83926c7219d7fa)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/db87d285eb797d3471fe3e910ca6f95e.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=1cc8fd1670cbbbf9a5f24271879a99b8587703c4143a7f439c83926c7219d7fa)

利用统计资料误导他人可称为统计操纵；简而言之（尽管这个词并不贴切），就是“统计化”处理。

<!--en-->
MISINFORMING people by the use of statistical material might be called statistical manipulation; in a word (though not a very good one), statisticulation.

本书的标题及部分内容似乎暗示所有此类操作都是出于故意欺骗的目的。美国统计协会某分会的主席曾因此指责我。他说，大多数情况下并非蓄意欺骗，而是无能所致。他的话或许不无道理¹，但我不确定哪种假设对统计学家来说较易接受。或许更重要的是要记住：统计数据的扭曲与操纵并不总是出自专业统计学家之手。统计学家精心整理的数据，到了推销员、公关专家、记者或广告文案撰写人手中，便可能被歪曲、夸大、过度简化或通过选择性呈现来篡改。

<!--en-->
The title of this book and some of the things in it might seem to imply that all such operations are the product of intent to deceive. The president of a chapter of the American Statistical Association once called me down for that. Not chicanery much of the time, said he, but incompetence. There may be something in what he says,¹ but I am not certain that one assumption will be less offensive to statisticians than the other. Possibly more important to keep in mind is that the distortion of statistical data and its manipulation to an end are not always the work of professional statisticians. What comes full of virtue from the statistician's desk may find itself twisted, exaggerated,oversimplified, and distorted-through-selection by salesman, public-relations expert, journalist, or advertising copywriter.

无论责任方是谁，都很难将其视为无心之失。杂志和报纸上的虚假图表常常通过夸张手法制造轰动效应，极少会淡化事实。以我的经验来看，代表企业界提出统计论据的人，很少会给予劳工或消费者比实际情况更好的待遇，往往反而更差。有哪一家工会曾雇用过如此无能的统计人员，以至于把劳工的立场说得比实际更弱呢？

<!--en-->
But whoever the guilty party may be in any instance, it is hard to grant him the status of blundering innocent. False charts in magazines and newspapers frequently sensationalize by exaggeration, rarely minimize anything. Those who present statistical arguments on behalf of industry are seldom found, in my experience, giving labor or the customer a better break than the facts call for, and often they give him a worse one. When has a union employed a statistical worker so incompetent that he made labor's case out weaker than it was?

只要这些错误是一面倒的，就很难将其归咎于疏忽或偶然。

<!--en-->
As long as the errors remain one-sided, it is not easy to attribute them to bungling or accident.

歪曲统计数据最狡猾的手段之一便是利用地图。地图引入了众多变量，足以掩盖事实并扭曲关系。我在此领域最“得意”的例子是《日益浓重的阴影》这张图。它不久前由波士顿第一国民银行发行，并被广泛转载——包括所谓的纳税人团体、报纸以及《新闻周刊》杂志。

<!--en-->
One of the trickiest ways to misrepresent statistical data is by means of a map. A map introduces a fine bag of variables in which facts can be concealed and relationships distorted. My favorite trophy in this field is "The Darkening Shadow." It was distributed not long ago by the First National Bank of Boston and reproduced very widely—by so-called taxpayers groups, newspapers, and *Newsweek* magazine.

这张地图显示了联邦政府目前拿走并花费的国民收入比例。它通过给密西西比河以西的各州（仅路易斯安那州、阿肯色州和密苏里州部分地区除外）着色，来表示联邦开支已相当于这些州居民的总收入。

<!--en-->
The map shows what portion of our national income is now being taken, and spent, by the federal government. It does this by shading the areas of the states west of the Mississippi (excepting only Louisiana, Arkansas, and part of Missouri) to indicate that federal spending has become equal to the total incomes of the people of those states.

欺骗之处在于选择了面积大但因人口稀少而收入相对较少的州。如果制图者同样“诚实”（也同样不诚实）地给纽约州或新英格兰地区着色，就会得出一个规模更小、效果更不惊人的“阴影”。使用相同的数据，他本可以给观者留下截然不同的印象。不过没人会费心去传播那样的地图——至少我没听说过有哪个有影响力的团体希望把公共开支描绘得比实际更少。

<!--en-->
The deception lies in choosing states having large areas but, because of sparse population, relatively small incomes. With equal honesty (and equal dishonesty) the map maker might have started shading in New York or New England and come out with a vastly smaller and less impressive shadow. Using the same data he would have produced quite a different impression in the mind of anyone who looked at his map. No one would have bothered to distribute that one, though. At least, I do not know of any powerful group that is interested in making public spending appear to be smaller than it is.

如果制图者的目的仅仅是传递信息，他本可以轻而易举地做到。他本可以选择一组中间状态的州，这些州的总面积与国家总面积的比例，正好与其总收入占国民收入的比例相匹配。

<!--en-->
If the objective of the map maker had been simply to convey information he could have done so quite easily. He could have chosen a group of in-between states whose total area bears the same relation to the area of the country that their total income does to the national income.

让这张地图成为一次尤为明目张胆的误导行为的原因是：这并非什么新的宣传伎俩，而是一种老掉牙、屡见不鲜的手段。早在过去，同一家银行就曾发布过该地图的不同版本，用以展示1929年和1937年的联邦开支情况；这些版本很快便被收录进威拉德·科普·布林顿所著的经典著作《图形展示》（Graphic Presentation）中，作为典型的反面教材。布林顿直言不讳地指出，这种方法“歪曲了事实”。但第一国民银行仍继续绘制此类地图，而《新闻周刊》以及其他本应更了解内情——或许也确实知情——的人，却继续不加警告、也不道歉地转载它们。

<!--en-->
The thing that makes this map a particularly flagrant effort to misguide is that it is not a new trick of propaganda. It is something of a classic, or chestnut. The same bank long ago published versions of this map to show federal expenditures in 1929 and 1937, and these shortly cropped up in astandard book, *Graphic Presentation*, by Willard Cope Brinton, as horrible examples. This method “distorts the facts,” said Brinton plainly. But the First National goes right on drawing its maps, and *Newsweek* and other people who should know better—and possibly do—go right on reproducing them with neither warning nor apology.

## 日益浓重的阴影

<!--en-->
*THE DARKENING SHADOW*

*(西式风格)*

<!--en-->
*(Western Style)*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/045669721c655d5e7a04eca617ede1e6.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=72f6d55420673601371074930f0d14f64e3ef5480928f62d342fcacd3f92a584)

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/045669721c655d5e7a04eca617ede1e6.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=72f6d55420673601371074930f0d14f64e3ef5480928f62d342fcacd3f92a584)

*(东方风格)*

<!--en-->
*(Eastern Style)*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b5fef48cf1ebb1619e8cf51d567eb733.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=7beaec34266d106255118ee6aa230a5d9698bb4caa74d299b6ddb73452023894)

<!--en-->

<!--en-->

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/9127ad21c22d68c2abeb85ad1f8e02a0.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=c561d2e45f9567f0099590b04724b340173a85a560d7720134d2d4467087d474)

美国家庭的平均收入是多少？正如我们之前提到的，根据美国人口普查局的数据，1949年“普通家庭的收入为3,100美元”。但如果你阅读了拉塞尔·塞奇基金会发布的关于“慈善捐赠”的报纸报道，就会发现同年这一数字竟达到了令人瞩目的5,004美元。你或许会为人们如此富裕而感到欣慰，但也可能对这个数字与自己的观察结果不符感到惊讶。也许你认识的是错误的一类人吧。

<!--en-->
What is the average income of American families? As we noted earlier, for 1949 the Bureau of the Census says that the “income of the average family was $3,100.” But if you read a newspaper story on “philanthropic giving” handed out by the Russell Sage Foundation you learned that, for the same year, it was a notable $5,004. Possibly you were pleased to learn that folks were doing so well, but you may also have been struck by how poorly that figure squared with your own observations. Possibly you know the wrong kind of people.

究竟为什么拉塞尔·塞奇基金会和人口普查局的数据会相差如此之大呢？人口普查局采用的是中位数，这当然无可厚非；但即便塞奇基金会使用的是平均数，这种差异也不应如此显著。原来，拉塞尔·塞奇基金会是通过制造一个只能被称之为“虚假家庭”的样本，才得出这种惊人的繁荣数据的。他们解释道（当被要求说明原因时），其方法是将美国人的个人总收入除以1.49亿，从而得出每人平均1,251美元的数字。“换算下来，”他们补充说，“四口之家的收入便达到了5,004美元。”

<!--en-->
Now how in the world can Russell Sage and the Bureau of the Census be so far apart? The Bureau is talking in medians, as of course it should be, but even if the Sage people are using a mean the difference should not be quite this great. The Russell Sage Foundation, it turns out, discovered this remarkable prosperity by producing what can only be described as a phony family. Their method, they explained (when asked for an explanation), was to divide the total personal income of the American people by 149,000,000 to get an average of $1,251 for each person. “Which,” they added, “becomes $5,004 in a family of four.”

## 如何每年赚22,500美元（税前）？

<!--en-->
How to Make $22,500 a year (gross)

1. 至少娶1位妻子并生育13个孩子。
2. 计算美国的人均收入。（答案：每年约1,500美元）
3. 乘以15。（答案：15 × $1,500 = $22,500）![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/8ec0e2525506b30be503d5ae3454d7a5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=3c22aec13c7b1b2e4c25a7ba56e08165fca2a53c97ef72a00025be8c14b1bd69) 这种奇怪的统计手法在两方面夸大了事实。它使用了被称为“均值”的平均数，而非更小且更具参考价值的“中位数”……这一点我们在前一章中已讨论过。此外，它还假定家庭收入与家庭规模成正比。我育有四个孩子，虽然我希望情况真是如此，但事实并非如此。四口之家绝不可能普遍比两口之家富裕两倍。为了公平起见，对Russell Sage的统计人员而言——他们理应被认为并无故意欺骗之意——应当指出他们主要关注的是描绘“给予”而非“获取”的情景。那个关于家庭收入的荒谬数字不过是副产品而已。但即便如此，它依然有效地散布了误导信息；它仍是为何不能轻信未经限定的平均数表述的典型例证。为了给最不可靠的统计数据披上虚假的精确外衣，不妨看看小数点的作用。询问一百位市民昨晚睡了多少小时，得出的总数可能是783.1小时。其实这类数据从一开始就不精确：大多数人会相差十五分钟甚至更久，而且无法保证这些误差会相互抵消。我们每个人都认识这样的人——他们会把五分钟的失眠记作半个不眠之夜。但继续算下去，然后宣称人们平均每晚睡眠7.831小时吧。你听起来就好像对自己所说的话了如指掌。倘若你只是简单地声称人们每晚睡7.8小时（或“将近8小时”），那便没什么值得大惊小怪的了；那样说听起来才像实话，不过是个粗略的估计罢了，并不比任何人的猜测更有参考价值。

<!--en-->
1. Acquire at least 1 (one) wife and 13 children.
2. Calculate the U.S. per capita income. (answer - $1,500 per year, approx.)
3. Multiply by 15. (ans. 15 x $1,500 = $22,500)
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/8ec0e2525506b30be503d5ae3454d7a5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=3c22aec13c7b1b2e4c25a7ba56e08165fca2a53c97ef72a00025be8c14b1bd69)
This odd piece of statistical manipulation exaggerates in two ways. It uses the kind of average called a mean instead of the smaller and more informative median ... something we worked over in an earlier chapter. And then it goes on to assume that the income of a family is in direct proportion to its size. Now I have four children, and I wish things were disposed in that way, but they are not. Families of four are by no means commonly twice as wealthy as families of two.
In fairness to the Russell Sage statisticians, who may be presumed innocent of desire to deceive, it should be said that they were primarily interested in making a picture of giving rather than of getting. The funny figure for family incomes was just a by-product. But it spread its deception no less effectively for that, and it remains a prime example of why little faith can be placed in an unqualified statement of average.
For a spurious air of precision that will lend all kinds of weight to the most disreputable statistic, consider the decimal. Ask a hundred citizens how many hours they slept last night. Come out with a total of, say, 783.1. Any such data are far from precise to begin with. Most people will miss their guess by fifteen minutes or more, and there is no assurance that the errors will balance out. We all know someone who will recall five sleepless minutes as half a night of tossing insomnia. But go ahead, do your arithmetic, and announce that people sleep an average of 7.831 hours a night. You will sound as if you knew precisely what you were talking about. If you had been so foolish as to declare only that people sleep 7.8 (or "almost 8") hours a night, there would have been nothing striking about it. It would have sounded like what it was, a poor approximation and no more instructive than almost anybody's guess.
