<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/e24fba5c99b75c2a8e2832c07697f00f.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=5f464cc27dcbc7501345295f327c315e4262fa80cecbc4b6783ae1abffd52e73)

卡尔·马克思同样也会故弄玄虚地营造出一种精确假象。在计算一家纺织厂的“剩余价值率”时，他首先列出了一堆假设、猜测和取整数字：“我们假设废料占比为6%……原材料成本约为342英镑。那1万根纺锭……我们假定每根成本为1英镑……设备损耗按10%计算……厂房租金则为300英镑……”他说：“上述数据可靠，是由曼彻斯特的一位纺织厂主提供给我的。”

<!--en-->
Karl Marx was not above achieving a spurious air of precision in the same fashion. In figuring the “rate of surplus-value” in a mill he began with a splendid collection of assumptions, guesses, and round numbers: “We assumethe waste to be 6% ... the raw material ... costs in round numbers £342. The 10,000 spindles ... cost, we will assume, £1 per spindle.... The wear and tear we put at 10%.
... The rent of the building we suppose to be £300...." He says, "The above data, which may be relied upon, were given me by a Manchester spinner."

基于这些近似值，马克思计算出：“因此剩余价值率为80/52 = 153¹¹/13\%。”按照每天十小时的工作时间，由此得出“必要劳动时间为$3^{21}/52$小时，剩余劳动时间为$6^{2}/52$小时。”

<!--en-->
From these approximations Marx calculates that: "The rate of surplus-value is therefore $80/52 = 153^{11}/13\%" For a ten-hour day this gives him "necessary labour —$3^{21}/52$ hours and surplus-labour = $6^{2}/52$."

那“三十三分之二小时”听起来确实精确得很，但全都是虚张声势罢了。

<!--en-->
There's a nice feeling of exactness to that two thirty-thirds of an hour. but it's all bluff.

百分比很容易造成混淆。就像那些看似精确的十进制数字一样，它们能为不精确的数据披上精确的外衣。美国劳工部的《月度劳工评论》曾称，在某个月份，华盛顿特区提供的提供车费补贴的兼职家务工作机会中，有4.9%的周薪为18美元。结果证明，这一百分比是基于仅仅两个案例得出的——当时总共只有41个此类工作机会。任何基于少量案例的百分比数字都很可能具有误导性。直接给出具体数值反而更有参考价值。而当百分比被精确到小数点后多位时，就愈发显得荒谬甚至具有欺骗性。

<!--en-->
Percentages offer a fertile field for confusion. And like the ever-impressive decimal they can lend an aura of precision to the inexact. The United States Department of Labor's *Monthly Labor Review* once stated that of the offers of part-time household employment with provisions for carfare, in Washington, D. C., during a specified month, 4.9 per cent were at $18 a week. This percentage, it turned out, was based on precisely two cases, there having been only forty-one offers altogether. Any percentage figure based on a small number of cases is likely to be misleading. It is more informative to give the figure itself. And when the percentage is carried out to decimal places you begin to run the scale from the silly to the fraudulent.

一则广告宣称：“现在购买圣诞礼物可节省100%！”这听起来像是圣诞老人才会给出的优惠，但实际上只是概念混淆而已。实际折扣仅为50%。诚然，所节省的金额确实相当于折后价的100%，但这并非广告所言。

<!--en-->
"Buy your Christmas presents now and save 100 per cent," advises an advertisement. This sounds like an offer worthy of old Santa himself, but it turns out to be merely a confusion of base. The reduction is only fifty per cent. The saving is one hundred per cent of the reduced or new price, it is true, but that isn't what the offer says.

同样，当某花卉种植协会主席在报纸采访中说“如今鲜花比四个月前便宜100%”时，他并非指花店现在免费送花。但他确实这么说了。

<!--en-->
Likewise when the president of a flower growers' association said, in a newspaper interview, that "flowers are 100 per cent cheaper than four months ago," he didn't mean that florists were now giving them away. But that's what he said.

艾达·M·塔贝尔在她的《标准石油公司史》中更是夸张：她称“西南部地区的降价幅度介于14%到220%之间”。照此推算，卖家反而得付给买家一笔可观的费用才能把石油运走。

<!--en-->
In her *History of the Standard Oil Company*, Ida M. Tarbell went even further. She said that "price cutting in the southwest ... ranged from 14 to 220 per cent." That would call for seller paying buyer a considerable sum to haul the oily stuff away.

《哥伦布快报》宣称某种制成品的利润高达3,800%，其依据是成本1.75美元、售价40美元。计算利润率时有多种方法（且必须注明所用方法）。若按成本计算，利润率为2,185%；若按售价计算，则为95.6%。《哥伦布快报》显然采用了自己的一套算法，结果如常地得出了夸大的数字。

<!--en-->
The Columbus *Dispatch* declared that a manufactured product was selling at a profit of 3,800 per cent, basing this on a cost of $1.75 and a selling price of $40. In calculating percentage of profits you have a choice of methods (and you are obligated to indicate which you are using). If figured on cost, this one comes to a profit of 2,185 per cent; on selling price, 95.6 per cent. The*Dispatch* apparently used a method of its own and, as so often seems to happen, got an exaggerated figure to report.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2a14932a2dd713ffa818127052bfa4f1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=3c94e351312114478f55ee6a9cb6dec5f780aa7bee73c14f97d457287145607b)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/2a14932a2dd713ffa818127052bfa4f1.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=3c94e351312114478f55ee6a9cb6dec5f780aa7bee73c14f97d457287145607b)

就连《纽约时报》也在刊登美联社从印第安纳波利斯发回的报道时，输掉了这场“基数误导之战”。

<!--en-->
Even *The New York Times* lost the Battle of the Shifting Base in publishing an Associated Press story from Indianapolis:

经济萧条今天在这里给了人们沉重一击。水管工、泥瓦匠、木匠、油漆工等隶属于印第安纳波利斯建筑工会的人获得了5%的加薪。这弥补了他们去年冬季被削减的20%工资中的四分之一。

<!--en-->
The depression took a stiff wallop on the chin here today. Plumbers, plasterers, carpenters, painters and others affiliated with the Indianapolis Building Trades Unions were given a 5 per cent increase in wages. That gave back to the men one-fourth of the 20 per cent cut they took last winter.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c4a25d2a57e59a5dde2a00067c3488c2.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=e3096193057f314fe2f664e3ee5ec86378768c6cfbe9e51912f3037809ffcf66)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c4a25d2a57e59a5dde2a00067c3488c2.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=e3096193057f314fe2f664e3ee5ec86378768c6cfbe9e51912f3037809ffcf66)

乍一听似乎合理——但削减幅度是以原先的工资为基数计算的，而加薪则是以削减后的工资水平为基数。

<!--en-->
Sounds reasonable on the face of it—but the decrease has been figured on one base—the pay the men were getting in the first place—while the increase usesa smaller base, the pay level after the cut.

为验证这种统计上的误导，我们不妨简单假设原工资为每小时1美元。削减20%后，工资降至80美分。在此基础上增加5%，即4美分，这并非削减额的四分之一，而是五分之一。像许多看似无意的错误一样，这一错误最终被夸大成了更吸引人的说法。

<!--en-->
You can check on this bit of statistical misfiguring by supposing, for simplicity, that the original wage was $1 an hour. Cut twenty per cent, it is down to 80 cents. A five per cent increase on that is 4 cents, which is not one-fourth but one-fifth of the cut. Like so many presumably honest mistakes, this one somehow managed to come out an exaggeration which made a better story.

这一切说明了一个道理：要抵消50%的减薪，就必须获得100%的加薪。

<!--en-->
All this illustrates why to offset a pay cut of fifty per cent you must get a raise of one hundred per cent.

还是《纽约时报》曾报道称，某个财政年度中因火灾损失的航空邮件重量为4,863磅，仅占总量的0.00063%。报道称当年飞机共运送了7,715,741磅邮件。如果保险公司据此制定费率，肯定会陷入麻烦。经计算可知，实际损失比例为0.063%，是报纸所报数字的100倍。

<!--en-->
It was the *Times* also that once reported that, for a fiscal year, air mail “lost through fire was 4,863 pounds, or a percentage of but 0.00063.” The story said that planes had carried 7,715,741 pounds of mail during the year. An insurance company basing its rates in that way could get into a pack of trouble. Figure the loss and you’ll find that it came to 0.063 per cent or one hundred times as great as the newspaper had it.

正是这种基数不断变化的错觉，导致了折扣计算的复杂性。当一家五金批发商打出“标价打五折后再打八折”的促销时，并不意味着总折扣率为70%。实际折扣率仅为60%，因为那20%的折扣是基于扣除50%后的较小基数来计算的。

<!--en-->
It is the illusion of the shifting base that accounts for the trickiness of adding discounts. When a hardware jobber offers “50% and 20% off list,” he doesn’t mean a seventy per cent discount. The cut is sixty per cent since the twenty per cent is figured on the smaller base left after taking off fifty per cent.

许多愚蠢的错误和诡计都源于把本不能相加的东西硬凑在一起，尽管它们看起来似乎可以相加。几代以来，孩子们一直用这种方式来为自己不上学找借口。

<!--en-->
A good deal of bumbling and chicanery have come from adding together things that don’t add up but merely seem to. Children for generations have been using a form of this device to prove that they don’t go to school.

你或许还记得吧：一年有365天，其中122天用于睡觉（占三分之一），另外45天用于吃饭（每天3小时）。从剩下的198天中再减去90天的暑假以及21天的圣诞节和复活节假期。最终剩下的天数甚至不够安排周末。

<!--en-->
You probably recall it. Starting with 365 days to the year you can subtract 122 for the one-third of the time you spend in bed and another 45 for the three hours a day used in eating. From the remaining 198 take away 90 for summer vacation and 21 for Christmas and Easter vacations. The days that remain are not even enough to provide for Saturdays and Sundays.

你可能会说，这实在是个过于古老且显而易见的伎俩，不适合用于正经的商业活动。但美国汽车工人联合会在其月刊《Ammunition》中坚称，这种手段仍被用来对付他们。

<!--en-->
Too ancient and obvious a trick to use in serious business, you might say. But the United Automobile Workers insist in their monthly magazine, *Ammunition*, that it is still being used against them.

![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/95e6b358d20306fc3b5d9528d324e004.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=51d299a5c6320d56c8c025e9e8a2c9b112cd6e98f694dbf1745aeb257a0910f2)

本书凝聚了187年*的出版经验！

<!--en-->
187 years* of publishing experience went into this book!

* 作者、编辑、插画师、印刷商和装订工的总年龄。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/3d0690e10dc18304f7cd6effb9483190.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dc1536202f02ed3bc22b919fa5934593b2225253445411f58d3a8c75342728bb) 那片广阔的蓝色天空也出现在每次罢工期间。每次罢工时，商会都会宣称罢工每天造成数百万美元的损失。他们通过计算如果罢工者全职工作的话会生产多少汽车得到这个数字；同样，他们也会计入对供应商造成的损失。所有可能的因素都被纳入其中，包括街道汽车票价和商家销售损失。那种认为百分比可以像苹果一样自由相加的类似奇怪观念曾被用来攻击作者。看看《纽约时报书评》中的这篇评论有多有说服力。书籍价格上涨与作者收入之间的差距，似乎是由于生产和材料成本大幅上升造成的。仅工厂和制造费用在过去十年中就上涨了10%至12%，材料成本上涨了6%至9%，销售和广告费用则上升了10%以上。综合来看，某家公司的总涨幅至少为33%，一些规模较小的出版社则接近40%。实际上，如果构成这本书出版成本的每一项都上涨了约10%，总成本也必然相应上涨了大约相同的比例。允许将这些百分比涨幅相加的逻辑可能导致各种荒谬结论。今天买二十样东西，发现每样都比去年上涨了5%。这样“加起来”就是100%，生活成本翻了一番。这是胡说八道。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/677d5a24a0d86ebe2c4d9e7224c6af3a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=57bd77a3d87c95b6a8bbf2ee6227f3d46461dfb80a1d4c5a344b02bcc7498dd3) 这有点像那个被问及如何以如此低价出售兔肉三明治的路边商人故事。“嗯，”他说，“我得加入一些马肉。但我把两者混合成五五开：一马一份，一只兔子一份。”一份工会出版物用漫画反对另一种无端相加的做法。漫画中展示了老板将正常一小时工资1.50美元、加班一小时工资2.25美元、双班一小时工资3美元相加，得出平均每小时工资为2.25美元。很难找到平均值意义较小的例子。另一个容易受骗的领域是百分比与百分点之间的混淆。如果你的利润从第一年的3%投资增长到第二年的6%，你可以称其为增长了3个百分点，从而显得相当温和。同样，你也可以将其描述为100%的增长。对于这种令人困惑的组合，尤其要注意民意调查者。百分位数也是具有欺骗性的。当你被告知约翰在代数或某些能力方面与同学相比处于什么位置时，那个数字可能是百分位数。它意味着他在每百名学生中的排名。例如，在一个三百人的班级中，前三位将在99百分位，接下来三位在98百分位，依此类推。百分位数的奇怪之处在于，百分数为99的学生可能比百分数为90的学生优秀得多，而百分数为40和60的学生可能成绩几乎相同。这源于许多特征倾向于围绕其自身平均值聚集，形成我们在前一章提到的“正常”钟形曲线。偶尔会出现统计学家之间的争论，即使是最不精明的观察者也无法忽视其中的问题。当统计学家产生分歧时，诚实的人就能得到好处。钢铁工业委员会指出了钢铁公司和工会都参与的某些不正当行为。为了证明1948年的经营状况良好（作为公司能够负担得起涨薪的证据），工会将那年的生产率与1939年进行了比较——那一年产量特别低。 为了不在欺骗竞赛中落后，这些公司坚持以员工实际获得的收入而非平均时薪作为比较依据。关键在于，前一年有太多工人从事兼职工作，因此即使工资水平完全没有上涨，他们的收入也必然有所增长。《时代》杂志以其一贯出色的图形设计而闻名，发表了一张图表，生动展示了统计数据如何几乎可以随意得出任何想要的结果。面对两种同样有效的研究方法——一种支持管理方观点，另一种支持劳工方观点，《时代》选择了两者都采用。实际上，这张图表由两张图表叠加而成，它们使用相同的数据。一张显示工资和利润以十亿美元为单位；显然，两者都在上升，且上升幅度大致相同。而且工资总额可能是利润的六倍。看来，巨大的通货膨胀压力来自工资。双图的另一部分以百分比形式表示变化情况：工资线相对平稳，而利润线则急剧上升。可以推断，利润是通货膨胀的主要原因。你可以选择自己认为的结论。或者，更好的是，你可以清楚地看到，无法将其中任何一个单独视为罪魁祸首。有时，指出有争议的话题并不像看起来那么简单明了，本身就是一项重要的服务。《时代》杂志经其许可重新绘制此图，作为非虚假图表的一个例子。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/db238b67f584b9dfa72a5789613bf13a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=8bb7987625f230bea655c423a0db5f4f688ccb4d859bd4cb03b53a0aeb177e7d) 对于数百万人来说，指数数字现在非常重要，因为工资水平往往与它们紧密相关。或许值得注意一下，可以做些什么让这些数字按照任何人的意愿变化。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/05818bd49ee1e4540c603ffb739fddb4.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4521aff9974fcf0c282eeec068f203400a643a3482caa3c89f8258e3ce85587b) 以最简单的例子来说，假设去年牛奶每夸脱售价20美分，面包每条售价5美分。今年牛奶价格降到了10美分，面包价格上升到了10美分。你现在想证明什么？生活成本上升了吗？下降了吗？还是没有变化？![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/ed6b92c154f8512a1894107d7b69bc3b.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=864ac41eb316dfabd73c401b958240ab65ea1e9cb71a659ce912da28f894b94e) 以去年为基期，使当时的价格达到100%。由于牛奶价格降至一半（50%），面包价格翻了一番（200%），50和200的平均值为125，因此价格上升了25%。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b9dc75399aaea5389bf53844d8f82b6d.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=49431f9110736c120309506d80084f0324cb847475f5ea20eb54dc4e4057bd12) 再试一次，以今年为基期。牛奶过去的价格是现在的200%，面包价格是过去的50%。平均值：125%。过去的价格比现在高25%。要证明成本水平根本没有变化，我们只需使用几何平均数，并以任一时期作为基期。这与我们一直使用的算术平均数略有不同，但这是一种完全合理的数值，在某些情况下是最有用、最能揭示真相的。要得到三个数的几何平均数，将它们相乘后再取立方根。四个数则取四次方根；两个数则取平方根。就是这样。以去年为基期，将其价格水平定为100。实际上，你需要将每个项目的100%相乘，再取立方根，即100。对于今年，牛奶是去年的50%，面包是200%，将50乘以200得到10,000。平方根，即几何平均数，为100。价格既没有上升也没有下降。事实上，尽管有数学基础，统计学既是一种艺术，也是一种科学。在合理范围内，可以进行许多操作甚至扭曲。通常，统计学家必须在方法之间做出选择，这是一个主观过程，然后找到他将用来反映事实的方法。 在商业实践中，他选择不利的方法的可能性与文案人员说赞助商的产品质量差、价格低几乎相同——其实他完全可以说它便宜且经济实惠。![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f9fb584eb81d9bb9a613ecfefe76b2a4.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=055d47b9fef9399cd33fafcdbcb4e0e8b0a43cd8c3a470828700d9dd54b547ab)甚至学术工作者也可能存在某种偏见（可能是无意识的），倾向于支持某个观点或达到某种目的。这提示我们在接受任何统计数据、报纸和书籍中的事实与数据、杂志和广告内容之前，需要仔细重新审视。有时，仔细审视会让问题更清晰。但随意拒绝统计方法也没有意义。这就像因为作者有时用词语隐藏事实与关系而非揭示它们而拒绝阅读。毕竟，不久前，佛罗里达的一位政治候选人通过指责对手“实行独身主义”获得了大量资金。纽约放映电影《Quo Vadis》的放映商用大字体引用《纽约时报》的话称其具有“历史上的虚张声势”。而一种专有药物Crazy Water Crystals的制造者，一直宣传他们的产品能带来“快速、短暂的缓解效果”。如何撒谎 如何用统计数据撒谎 如何不用统计数据撒谎

<!--en-->
* Combined ages of author, editor, illustrator, printer and binder.
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/3d0690e10dc18304f7cd6effb9483190.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=dc1536202f02ed3bc22b919fa5934593b2225253445411f58d3a8c75342728bb)
The wide, blue yonder lie also turns up during every strike. Every time there is a strike, the Chamber of Commerce advertises that the strike is costing so many millions of dollars a day.
They get the figure by adding up all the cars that would have been made if the strikers had worked full time. They add in losses to suppliers in the same way. Everything possible is added in, including street car fares and the loss to merchants in sales.
The similar and equally odd notion that percentages can be added together as freely as apples has been used against authors. See how convincing this one, from *The New York Times Book Review*, sounds.
The gap between advancing book prices and authors' earnings, it appears, is due to substantially higher production and material costs. Item: plant and manufacturing expenses alone have risen as much as 10 to 12 per cent over the last decade, materials are up 6 to 9 per cent, selling and advertising expenses have climbed upwards of 10 per cent. Combined boosts add up to a minimum of 33 per cent (for one company) and to nearly 40 per cent for some of the smaller houses.
Actually, if each item making up the cost of publishing this book has risen around ten per cent, the total cost must have climbed by about that proportion also. The logic that permits adding those percentage rises together could lead to all sorts of flights of fancy. Buy twenty things today and find that each has gone up five per cent over last year. That “adds up” to one hundred per cent, and the cost of living has doubled. Nonsense.
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/677d5a24a0d86ebe2c4d9e7224c6af3a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=57bd77a3d87c95b6a8bbf2ee6227f3d46461dfb80a1d4c5a344b02bcc7498dd3)
It's all a little like the tale of the roadside merchant who was asked to explain how he could sell rabbit sandwiches so cheap. "Well," he said, "I have to put in some horse meat too. But I mix 'em fifty-fifty: one horse, one rabbit."
A union publication used a cartoon to object to another variety of unwarranted adding-up. It showed the boss adding one regular hour at $1.50 to one overtime hour at $2.25 to one double-time hour at $3 for an average hourly wage of $2.25. It would be hard to find an instance of an average with less meaning.
Another fertile field for being fooled lies in the confusion between percentage and percentage points. If your profits should climb from three per cent on investment one year to six per cent the next, you can make it sound quite modest by calling it a rise of three percentage points. With equal validity you can describe it as a one hundred per cent increase. For loose handling of this confusing pair watch particularly the public-opinion pollers.
Percentiles are deceptive too. When you are told how Johnny stands compared to his classmates in algebra or some aptitude, the figure may be a percentile. It means his rank in each one hundred students. In a class of three hundred, for instance, the top three will be at the 99 percentile, the next three at the 98, and so on. The odd thing about percentiles is that a student with a 99-percentile rating is probably quite a bit superior to one standing at 90, while those at the 40 and 60 percentiles may be of almost equal achievement. This comes from the habit that so many characteristics have of clustering about their own average, forming the "normal" bell curve we mentioned in an early chapter.
Occasionally a battle of the statisticians develops, and even the most unsophisticated observer cannot fail to smell a rat. Honest men get a break when statisticulators fall out. The Steel Industry Board has pointed out some of the monkey business in which both steel companies and unions have indulged. To show how good business had been in 1948 (as evidence that the companies could well afford a raise), the union compared that year's productivity with that of 1939—a year of especially low volume. The companies, not to be outdone in the deception derby, insisted on making their comparisons on a basis of money received by the employees rather than average hourly earnings. The point to this was that so many workers had been on part time in the earlier year that their incomes were bound to have grown even if wage rates had not risen at all.
*Time* magazine, notable for the consistent excellence of its graphics, published a chart that is an amusing example of how statistics can pull out ofthe bag almost anything that may be wanted. Faced with a choice of methods, equally valid, one favoring the management viewpoint and the other favoring labor, *Time* simply used both. The chart was really two charts, one superimposed upon the other. They used the same data.
One showed wages and profits in billions of dollars. It was evident that both were rising and by more or less the same amount. And that wages involved perhaps six times as many dollars as profits did. The great inflationary pressure, it appeared, came from wages.
The other part of the dual chart expressed the changes as percentages of increase. The wage line was relatively flat. The profit line shot sharply upward. Profits, it might be inferred, were principally responsible for inflation.
You could take your choice of conclusions. Or, perhaps better, you could easily see that neither element could properly be singled out as the guilty one. It is sometimes a substantial service simply to point out that a subject in controversy is not as open-and-shut as it has been made to seem.
*Redrawn with the kind permission of TIME magazine as an example of a non-lying chart.*
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/db238b67f584b9dfa72a5789613bf13a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=8bb7987625f230bea655c423a0db5f4f688ccb4d859bd4cb03b53a0aeb177e7d)
Index numbers are vital matters to millions of people now that wage rates are often tied to them. It is perhaps worth noting what can be done to make them dance to any man's music.
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/05818bd49ee1e4540c603ffb739fddb4.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=4521aff9974fcf0c282eeec068f203400a643a3482caa3c89f8258e3ce85587b)
To take the simplest possible example, let's say that milk cost twenty cents a quart last year and bread was a nickel a loaf. This year milk is down to a dime and bread has gone up to a dime. Now what would you like to prove? Cost of living up? Cost of living down? Or no change?
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/ed6b92c154f8512a1894107d7b69bc3b.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=864ac41eb316dfabd73c401b958240ab65ea1e9cb71a659ce912da28f894b94e)
Consider last year as the base period, making the prices of that time 100 per cent. Since the price of milk has since dropped to half (50 per cent) and the price of bread has doubled (200 per cent) and the average of 50 and 200 is 125, prices have gone up 25 per cent.
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b9dc75399aaea5389bf53844d8f82b6d.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=49431f9110736c120309506d80084f0324cb847475f5ea20eb54dc4e4057bd12)
Try it again, taking this year as base period. Milk used to cost 200 per cent as much as it does now and bread was selling for 50 per cent as much. Average: 125 per cent. Prices used to be 25 per cent higher than they are now.
To prove that the cost level hasn't changed at all we simply switch to the geometric average and use either period as the base. This is a little different from the arithmetic average, or mean, that we have been using but it is a perfectly legitimate kind of figure and in some cases the most useful and revealing. To get the geometric average of three numbers you multiply them together and derive the cube root. For four items, the fourth root; for two, the square root. Like that.
Take last year as the base and call its price level 100. Actually you multiply the 100 per cent for each item together and take the root, which is 100. For this year, milk being at 50 per cent of last year and bread at 200 per cent,multiply 50 by 200 to get 10,000. The square root, which is the geometric average, is 100. Prices have not gone up *or* down.
The fact is that, despite its mathematical base, statistics is as much an art as it is a science. A great many manipulations and even distortions are possible within the bounds of propriety. Often the statistician must choose among methods, a subjective process, and find the one that he will use to represent the facts. In commercial practice he is about as unlikely to select an unfavorable method as a copywriter is to call his sponsor's product flimsy and cheap when he might as well say light and economical.
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/f9fb584eb81d9bb9a613ecfefe76b2a4.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=055d47b9fef9399cd33fafcdbcb4e0e8b0a43cd8c3a470828700d9dd54b547ab)
Even the man in academic work may have a bias (possibly unconscious) to favor, a point to prove, an axe to grind.
This suggests giving statistical material, the facts and figures in newspapers and books, magazines and advertising, a very sharp second look before accepting any of them. Sometimes a careful squint will sharpen the focus. But arbitrarily rejecting statistical methods makes no sense either. That is like refusing to read because writers sometimes use words to hide facts and relationships rather than to reveal them. After all, a political candidate in Florida not long ago made considerable capital by accusing his opponent of “practicing celibacy.” A New York exhibitor of the motion picture *Quo Vadis* used huge type to quote *The New York Times* as calling it “historical pretentiousness.” And the makers of Crazy Water Crystals, a proprietary medicine, have been advertising their product as providing “quick, ephemeral relief.”
How to LIE
How to LIE with Statistics
How to LIE without Statistics

# 第十章

<!--en-->
*CHAPTER 10*

## 如何反驳统计数据？

<!--en-->
*How to Talk Back to a Statistic*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/14b1a28c25ec4b1a6e3204e0b4c90641.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=0986a73809fde99c76c2bea3cadb39b16f1f745a45be888dc24fd92b7d8ccc85)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/14b1a28c25ec4b1a6e3204e0b4c90641.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=0986a73809fde99c76c2bea3cadb39b16f1f745a45be888dc24fd92b7d8ccc85)

到目前为止，我一直是把你当作渴望学习精良剑术的海盗来对待的。在这一章的结尾部分，我将不再使用这种文学手法。我将直面我自认为隐藏在本书背后的严肃目的：教你如何正视虚假的统计数据并予以驳斥；同样重要的是，教会你如何在充斥着欺诈的数据迷雾中识别出可靠且可用的信息——前几章主要讨论的正是这类问题。

<!--en-->
SO FAR, I have been addressing you rather as if you were a pirate with a yen for instruction in the finer points of cutlass work. In this concluding chapter I'll drop that literary device. I'll face up to the serious purpose that I like to think lurks just beneath the surface of this book: explaining how to look a phony statistic in the eye and face it down; and no less important, how to recognize sound and usable data in that wilderness of fraud to which the previous chapters have been largely devoted.

并非所有你遇到的统计信息都能像化学分析或化验室检测那样被准确验证。但你可以用五个简单的问题来检验它们，通过找到答案来避免被大量不实之词所误导。

<!--en-->
Not all the statistical information that you may come upon can be tested with the sureness of chemical analysis or of what goes on in an assayer's laboratory. But you can prod the stuff with five simple questions, and by finding the answers avoid learning a remarkable lot that isn't so.

## 谁说的？

<!--en-->
*Who Says So?*

首先要注意的是偏差——那些为了证明某种理论、维护声誉或谋取利益而有所偏见的实验室；那些追求轰动效应的报纸；以及涉及工资水平争议的劳资双方。

<!--en-->
About the first thing to look for is bias—the laboratory with something to prove for the sake of a theory, a reputation, or a fee; the newspaper whose aim is a good story; labor or management with a wage level at stake.

要留意有意识的偏差。其表现形式可能是直接歪曲事实，也可能是含糊其辞、难以定罪的表述；也可能是挑选有利数据而隐瞒不利数据。计量单位也可能被篡改，比如一次比较中使用某一年份，另一次则换成更有利的一年。还可能采用不恰当的衡量标准：本该用中位数时却用了平均值（也许这反而暴露了更多真相），并用“平均”这一模糊词汇来掩盖其中的诡计。

<!--en-->
Look for conscious bias. The method may be direct misstatement or it may be ambiguous statement that serves as well and cannot be convicted. It may be selection of favorable data and suppression of unfavorable. Units of measurement may be shifted, as with the practice of using one year for one comparison and sliding over to a more favorable year for another. An improper measure may be used: a mean where a median would be more informative (perhaps all too informative), with the trickery covered by the unqualified word “average.”

更要警惕无意识的偏差，它往往更加危险。1928年，许多统计学家和经济学家的图表与预测中就存在这种偏差，他们欣然忽视了经济结构中的裂痕，还引用各种统计数据来证明我们刚刚步入繁荣期。

<!--en-->
Look sharply for unconscious bias. It is often more dangerous. In the charts and predictions of many statisticians and economists in 1928 it operated to produce remarkable things. The cracks in the economic structure were joyously overlooked, and all sorts of evidence was adduced and statistically supported to show that we had no more than entered the stream of prosperity.

要弄清“谁说的”往往需要再仔细看看。说话者可能被斯蒂芬·波特在《处世之道》中所称的“靠谱名称”所掩盖。任何带有医学背景的名称都是“靠谱名称”；科学实验室也是“靠谱名称”；大学尤其是以技术研究著称的院校同样如此。前面几章中那位声称高等教育会危及女孩婚姻机会的作者，就巧妙地利用了康奈尔大学的“靠谱名称”。请注意：虽然数据来自康奈尔大学，但结论完全是作者自己的观点。不过这个“靠谱名称”确实容易让人误以为“康奈尔大学说……”。

<!--en-->
It may take at least a second look to find out who-says-so. The who may be hidden by what Stephen Potter, the *Lifemanship* man, would probably call the “O.K. name.” Anything smacking of the medical profession is an O.K. name. Scientific laboratories have O.K. names. So do colleges, especially universities, more especially ones eminent in technical work. The writer who proved a few chapters back that higher education jeopardizes a girl’s chance to marry made good use of the O.K. name of Cornell. Please note that while the data came from Cornell, the conclusions were entirely the writer’s own. But the O.K. name helps you carry away a misimpression of “Cornell University says ...”

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/66027599bc3ca0efb10e931303f2402a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=79e7501c75ce18a7bac8c0324aea6089788ffd439fbd68a58f68cb43e0115379)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/66027599bc3ca0efb10e931303f2402a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=79e7501c75ce18a7bac8c0324aea6089788ffd439fbd68a58f68cb43e0115379)

当引用某个“靠谱名称”时，务必确认该机构确实为信息提供了权威支撑，而不仅仅是与之相关而已。

<!--en-->
When an O.K. name is cited, make sure that the authority stands behind the information, not merely somewhere alongside it.

你可能读过《芝加哥商业日报》引以为傲的报道。该报进行了一项调查：在回复关于哄抬物价和囤积居奇问题的169家公司中，三分之二声称自己承担了朝鲜战争导致的价格上涨。“调查显示，”《商业日报》说道（遇到这类措辞时要格外留心！），“这些公司的做法与美国商业体制的敌人所指责的完全相反。”显然，这里就该问一句：“谁说的？”因为《商业日报》本身可能被视为利益相关方。这也是提出第二个检验问题的绝佳时机：

<!--en-->
You may have read a proud announcement by the Chicago *Journal of Commerce*. That publication had made a survey. Of 169 corporations that replied to a poll on price gouging and hoarding, two-thirds declared that they were absorbing price increases produced by the Korean war. “The survey shows,” said the *Journal* (look sharp whenever you meet those words!), “that corporations have done exactly the opposite of what the enemies of the American business system have charged.” This is an obvious place to ask, “Who says so?” since the *Journal of Commerce* might be regarded as an interested party. It is also a splendid place to ask our second test question:

## 他怎么知道的？

<!--en-->
*How Does He Know?*

原来，《商业日报》最初向1200家大公司发送了问卷，只有14%的公司予以回复。86%的公司根本不愿公开表态是否参与囤积或哄抬物价。

<!--en-->
It turns out that the *Journal* had begun by sending its questionnaires to 1,200 large companies. Only fourteen per cent had replied. Eighty-six per cent had not cared to say anything in public on whether they were hoarding or price gouging.

《商业日报》把情况美化得很好，但事实是没什么可炫耀的。实际情况是：在受调查的1200家公司中，9%称自己没有涨价，5%承认涨了价，而86%则保持沉默。那些回复的公司构成的样本很可能存在偏差。

<!--en-->
The *Journal* had put a remarkably good face on things, but the fact remains that there was little to brag about. It came down to this: Of 1,200 companies polled, nine per cent said they had not raised prices, five per cent said they had, and eighty-six per cent wouldn't say. Those that had replied constituted a sample in which bias might be suspected.

要警惕样本偏差的证据——即样本选取不当，或者像本例一样是自我选择的。请回想我们在前面章节中讨论过的问题：样本规模是否足够大，从而能得出可靠的结论？

<!--en-->
Watch out for evidence of a biased sample, one that has been selected improperly or—as with this one—has selected itself. Ask the question we dealt with in an early chapter: Is the sample large enough to permit any reliable conclusion?

同样，对于所报告的相关性而言：其程度是否足以说明问题？是否有足够的案例来支撑其重要性？作为普通读者，你无法运用显著性检验或得出关于样本充分性的确切结论。不过，对于你看到的许多报道，你或许能一眼看出——也许需要仔细观察一下——其中的案例数量根本不足以让任何有理智的人信服。

<!--en-->
Similarly with a reported correlation: Is it big enough to mean anything? Are there enough cases to add up to any significance? You cannot, as a casual reader, apply tests of significance or come to exact conclusions as to the adequacy of a sample. On a good many of the things you see reported, however, you will be able to tell at a glance —a good long glance, perhaps— that there just weren't enough cases to convince any reasoning person of anything.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/ff9f25237c70a671a73dd5f39ad8c97a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=18a2a492f003b15753270ad3ab596a56ab04f7c845cec01af70f2869382c088b)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/ff9f25237c70a671a73dd5f39ad8c97a.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=18a2a492f003b15753270ad3ab596a56ab04f7c845cec01af70f2869382c088b)

## 缺少了什么？

<!--en-->
*What's Missing?*

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/fe22872c4e2c9704661ecf0e89f70ec5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2ab7b9dd9d1c0102b6af13a728f2361ffee648ea81a8b11f3815590a362f3004)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/fe22872c4e2c9704661ecf0e89f70ec5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=2ab7b9dd9d1c0102b6af13a728f2361ffee648ea81a8b11f3815590a362f3004)

人们并不总会告诉你具体的案例数量。尤其当信息来源带有主观倾向时，缺少这类数据就足以让人对整则报道产生怀疑。同样，若给出的相关性数据没有附带可靠性指标（如可能误差、标准误差），也不应被过分看重。

<!--en-->
You won't always be told how many cases. The absence of such a figure, particularly when the source is an interested one, is enough to throw suspicion on the whole thing. Similarly a correlation given without a measure of reliability (probable error, standard error) is not to be taken very seriously.

在任何均值和中位数可能存在显著差异的情况下，要警惕那些未说明具体类型的平均值。

<!--en-->
Watch out for an average, variety unspecified, in any matter where mean and median might be expected to differ substantially.

许多数字之所以失去意义，是因为缺乏对比数据。《Look》杂志在一篇关于唐氏综合征的文章中写道：“一项研究显示，在2,800个案例中，超过一半的母亲年龄达到35岁或以上。”要从这些数据中得出有意义的信息，前提是你要了解女性生育的一般年龄情况。而我们当中很少有人掌握这类知识。

<!--en-->
Many figures lose meaning because a comparison is missing. An article in *Look* magazine says, in connection with Mongolism, that “one study shows that in 2,800 cases, over half of the mothers were 35 or over.” Getting any meaning from this depends upon your knowing something about the ages at which women in general produce babies. Few of us know things like that.

以下是1953年1月31日《纽约客》杂志“伦敦来信”栏目中的摘录。

<!--en-->
Here is an extract from the *New Yorker* magazine's “Letter from London” of January 31, 1953.

卫生部最近公布的数据显示，在大雾天气期间，大伦敦地区的死亡率骤增了2,800人。这一数字令公众感到震惊，因为人们通常将英国的恶劣气候视为麻烦而非致命因素……这个冬季的极端天气竟有如此致命的威力……

<!--en-->
The Ministry of Health's recently published figures showing that in the week of the great fog the death rate for Greater London jumped by twenty-eight hundred were a shock to the public, which is used to regarding Britain's unpleasant climatic effects as nuisances rather than as killers.... Theextraordinary lethal properties of this winter's prize visitation ...

但这次天气究竟有多致命呢？一周内死亡率比平时高出那么多是否属于异常情况？这类数据本来就会有所波动。那么随后几周的情况又如何呢？死亡率是否低于平均水平，从而暗示那些因雾气丧生的人本就濒临死亡？这个数字听起来令人震惊，但缺乏其他相关数据使其意义大打折扣。

<!--en-->
But how lethal was the visitation? Was it exceptional for the death rate to be that much higher than usual in a week? All such things do vary. And what about ensuing weeks? Did the death rate drop below average, indicating that if the fog killed people they were largely those who would have died shortly anyway? The figure sounds impressive, but the absence of other figures takes away most of its meaning.

有时公布的是百分比而缺少原始数据，这同样具有误导性。很久以前，约翰斯·霍普金斯大学刚开始招收女学生时，某位不赞成男女同校教育的人宣称了一个惊人的数字：霍普金斯大学的女生中有三分之一以上嫁给了教职员工！原始数据则揭示了更真实的情况：当时只有三名女学生，其中一人嫁给了教员。

<!--en-->
Sometimes it is percentages that are given and raw figures that are missing, and this can be deceptive too. Long ago, when Johns Hopkins University had just begun to admit women students, someone not particularly enamored of coeducation reported a real shocker: Thirty-three and one-third per cent of the women at Hopkins had married faculty members! The raw figures gave a clearer picture. There were three women enrolled at the time, and one of them had married a faculty man.

几年前，波士顿商会评选了“美国杰出女性”。在入选的16人中，有6人同时被列入《名人录》，据说她们共拥有“60个学位和18个孩子”。乍看之下，这似乎能让人对该群体有清晰的认识，但后来发现这六人中包括弗吉尼亚·吉尔德斯利夫院长和莉莲·M·吉尔布雷斯夫人。两人就占了全部学位的三分之一；而吉尔布雷斯夫人更是贡献了其中三分之二的孩子。

<!--en-->
A couple of years ago the Boston Chamber of Commerce chose its American Women of Achievement. Of the sixteen among them who were also in *Who's Who*, it was announced that they had "sixty academic degrees and eighteen children." That sounds like an informative picture of the group until you discover that among the women were Dean Virginia Gildersleeve and Mrs. Lillian M. Gilbreth. Those two had a full third of the degrees between them. And Mrs. Gilbreth, of course, supplied two-thirds of the children.

一家公司宣布其股票由3,003名股东持有，每人平均持有660股。这话没错。同样真实的是：在该公司200万股股票中，有三名男子持有了四分之三，其余四分之一则由三千名股东共享。

<!--en-->
A corporation was able to announce that its stock was held by 3,003 persons, who had an average of 660 shares each. This was true. It was also true that of the two million shares of stock in the corporation three men held three-quarters and three thousand persons held the other one-fourth among them.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/0f737a880f105734b61e7e8d50055574.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=41338cd4d2cbd072f99f2442fa6aa86279b3f3f35ee3604767e3b1f0772f3600)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/0f737a880f105734b61e7e8d50055574.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=41338cd4d2cbd072f99f2442fa6aa86279b3f3f35ee3604767e3b1f0772f3600)

如果你看到某个指数，不妨问问其中缺少了什么。也许缺失的是基数，而这个基数可能被刻意挑选以呈现扭曲的画面。某全国性劳工组织曾指出，经济萧条后利润和生产指数的上升速度远快于工资指数。但一旦有人找出缺失的数据，这一论点便站不住脚了：由于利润基数较低，其百分比增幅自然更容易显得更大。

<!--en-->
If you are handed an index, you may ask what's missing there. It may be the base, a base chosen to give a distorted picture. A national labor organization once showed that indexes of profits and production had risen much more rapidly after the depression than an index of wages had. As an argument for wage increases this demonstration lost its potency whensomeone dug out the missing figures. It could be seen then that profits had been almost bound to rise more rapidly in percentage than wages simply because profits had reached a lower point, giving a smaller base.

有时缺失的是导致变化的因素。这种遗漏会让人误以为另有其他原因导致了结果。某年公布的数据试图通过指出4月份的零售额高于上年来证明商业正在复苏，却忽略了前一年的复活节在3月，而后一年的复活节在4月这一事实。

<!--en-->
Sometimes what is missing is the factor that caused a change to occur. This omission leaves the implication that some other, more desired, factor is responsible. Figures published one year attempted to show that business was on the upgrade by pointing out that April retail sales were greater than in the year before. What was missing was the fact that Easter had come in March in the earlier year and in April in the later year.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/bef145d68ccc2649220bdc4dd9cd5f58.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=3582628db5542c5c3a469a168094fb44318f285936c2f808d52508aa9bedf39e)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/bef145d68ccc2649220bdc4dd9cd5f58.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=3582628db5542c5c3a469a168094fb44318f285936c2f808d52508aa9bedf39e)

如果不知道以下这些外部因素的影响程度，那么关于过去25年间癌症死亡人数大幅增加的报告就会具有误导性：如今，原本被归类为“病因不明”的病例现在常被列为癌症；尸检更为频繁，从而能做出更确切的诊断；医疗统计的报告与汇总也更为完整；而且现在达到癌症易发年龄的人口比例更高。此外，如果你关注的是总死亡人数而非死亡率，也别忘了如今的人口总数比过去要多得多。

<!--en-->
A report of a great increase in deaths from cancer in the last quarter-century is misleading unless you know how much of it is a product of such extraneous factors as these: Cancer is often listed now where “causes unknown” was formerly used; autopsies are more frequent, giving surer diagnoses; reporting and compiling of medical statistics are more complete; and people more frequently reach the most susceptible ages now. And if you are looking at total deaths rather than the death rate, don’t neglect the fact that there are more people now than there used to be.

## *有人偷换了话题吗？*

<!--en-->
*Did Somebody Change the Subject?*

在分析统计数据时，要留意原始数字与结论之间是否存在偷换概念的情况。一种事物常常被错误地表述为另一种事物。

<!--en-->
When assaying a statistic, watch out for a switch somewhere between the raw figure and the conclusion. One thing is all too often reported as another.

正如前文所述，某种疾病报告病例数的增加并不等同于实际患病案例的增加。候选人在民意测验中的领先优势并不一定能转化为投票时的胜利。杂志读者中“有代表性的一部分人”对国际事务类文章表现出的偏好，并不能作为他们真的会阅读这类文章的铁证。

<!--en-->
As just indicated, more reported cases of a disease are not always the same thing as more cases of the disease. A straw-vote victory for a candidate is not always negotiable at the polls. An expressed preference by a “cross section” of a magazine’s readers for articles on world affairs is no final proof that they would read the articles if they were published.

1952年，加利福尼亚中央谷地报告的脑炎病例数是此前最严重年份的三倍。许多惊慌失措的居民赶紧将孩子送走。但最终统计结果显示，昏睡病导致的死亡人数并未显著增加。实际情况是：州和联邦卫生部门派出了大量人员来处理这一长期存在的问题；由于他们的努力，许多往年会被忽视、甚至可能无法被识别的轻度病例被记录了下来。

<!--en-->
Encephalitis cases reported in the central valley of California in 1952 were triple the figure for the worst previous year. Many alarmed residents shipped their children away. But when the reckoning was in, there had been no great increase in deaths from sleeping sickness. What had happened was that state and federal health people had come in in great numbers to tackle a long-time problem; as a result of their efforts a great many low-grade cases were recorded that in other years would have been overlooked, possibly not even recognized.

这让人想起林肯·斯蒂芬斯和雅各布·A·里斯这两位纽约记者曾经制造的一场“犯罪潮”。报纸上报道的犯罪案件数量之多、篇幅之长、字体之大，足以让公众要求采取行动。时任改革警察委员会主席的西奥多·罗斯福为此十分尴尬。他只是要求斯蒂芬斯和里斯停止报道，便平息了这场“犯罪潮”。这一切仅仅是因为这两位记者为了竞争谁能在报道中揭露更多的入室盗窃等案件。官方警方记录中根本没有任何增长迹象。

<!--en-->
It is all reminiscent of the way that Lincoln Steffens and Jacob A. Riis, as New York newspapermen, once created a crime wave. Crime cases in the papers reached such proportions, both in numbers and in space and big type given to them, that the public demanded action. Theodore Roosevelt, as president of the reform Police Board, was seriously embarrassed. He put an end to the crime wave simply by asking Steffens and Riis to lay off. It had all come about simply because the reporters, led by those two, had got into competition as to who could dig up the most burglaries and whatnot. The official police record showed no increase at all.

一家报纸报道称：“5岁以上的英国男性冬季平均每周泡澡1.7次，夏季则为2.1次。”“英国女性冬季平均每周泡澡1.5次，夏季为2.0次。”该数据来源于工程部对“6,000户具有代表性的英国家庭”进行的热水使用调查。报告称样本具有代表性，其规模似乎也足以支持《旧金山纪事报》那句有趣标题的结论：英国男人比女人更爱泡澡。

<!--en-->
"The British male over 5 years of age soaks himself in a hot tub on an average of 1.7 times a week in the winter and 2.1 times in the summer," says a newspaper story. "British women average 1.5 baths a week in the winter and 2.0 in the summer." The source is a Ministry of Works hot-water survey of "6,000 representative British homes." The sample was representative, it says, and seems quite adequate in size to justify the conclusion in the San Francisco *Chronicle*'s amusing headline: BRITISH HE'S BATHE MORE THAN SHE'S.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/8006d16b345b0be1b2ef67579a798d54.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=0e57caf0d22922c6c2703efb68d87d2f27456ace1c111e92a6856ab36856b646)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/8006d16b345b0be1b2ef67579a798d54.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=0e57caf0d22922c6c2703efb68d87d2f27456ace1c111e92a6856ab36856b646)

如果能说明这些数字是平均值还是中位数，它们会更具参考价值。不过，主要的缺陷在于话题被偷换了。工程部真正了解的是这些人声称自己泡澡的频率，而非他们实际泡澡的频率。涉及如此私密的话题，再加上英国人特有的沐浴传统，声称与实际行为很可能并不一致。英国男人是否真的比女人更常泡澡无从确定；唯一可以肯定的是，他们声称自己如此。

<!--en-->
The figures would be more informative if there were some indication of whether they are means or medians. However, the major weakness is that the subject has been changed. What the Ministry really found out is how often these people said they bathed, not how often they did so. When a subject is as intimate as this one is, with the British bath-taking tradition involved, saying and doing may not be the same thing at all. British he's may or may not bathe oftener than she's; all that can safely be concluded is that they say they do.

以下是几种需要留意的偷换话题现象。

<!--en-->
Here are some more varieties of change-of-subject to watch out for.

1935年的人口普查显示农场数量比五年前增加了五十万个，于是人们认为出现了“回归田园”的运动。但两次统计所定义的对象并不相同。人口普查局更改了农场的定义；根据新定义，至少有30万个在1930年定义下不会被列为农场的单位被纳入统计。

<!--en-->
A back-to-the-farm movement was discerned when a census showed half a million more farms in 1935 than five years earlier. But the two counts were not talking about the same thing. The definition of farm used by the Bureau of the Census had been changed; it took in at least 300,000 farms that would not have been so listed under the 1930 definition.

当数据基于人们的陈述时，即便涉及看似客观的事实，也会出现奇怪的结果。例如，人口普查显示35岁的人口比34岁或36岁的人口更多。这种错误源于家庭成员在报告他人年龄时，由于不确定确切数字，往往将其四舍五入为常见的5的倍数。避免这种情况的一种方法是询问出生日期。

<!--en-->
Strange things crop out when figures are based on what people say—even about things that seem to be objective facts. Census reports have shown more people at thirty-five years of age, for instance, than at either thirty-four or thirty-six. The false picture comes from one family member's reporting the ages of the others and, not being sure of the exact ages, tending to round them off to a familiar multiple of five. One way to get around this: ask birth dates instead.

中国某大片地区的“人口”从2800万增至1.05亿。其中真正的人口增长微乎其微；这种巨大差异只能通过对两次普查的目的以及人们在接受统计时的心理进行分析才能解释。第一次普查是为了征税和军事目的，第二次则是为了饥荒救济。

<!--en-->
The "population" of a large area in China was 28 million. Five years later it was 105 million. Very little of that increase was real; the great difference could be explained only by taking into account the purposes of the two enumerations and the way people would be inclined to feel about being counted in each instance. The first census was for tax and military purposes, the second for famine relief.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c9caa0bc398af80c54a9517d9b1db5d5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=9a32adac0619a6d84ccd6fd05d4392c396a44a4b5f109ebd81cc3559a407fe65)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/c9caa0bc398af80c54a9517d9b1db5d5.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=9a32adac0619a6d84ccd6fd05d4392c396a44a4b5f109ebd81cc3559a407fe65)

类似的情况在美国也曾发生。1950年的人口普查显示，65至70岁年龄段的人数比十年前55至60岁年龄段的人数还要多。这种差异无法用移民来解释。其中大部分可能是由于人们为了领取社会保障金而大规模虚报年龄所致；也有可能是早期记录中出于虚荣心而故意低报了年龄。

<!--en-->
Something of the same sort has happened in the United States. The 1950 census found more people in the sixty-five-to-seventy age group than there were in the fifty-five-to-sixty group ten years before. The difference could not be accounted for by immigration. Most of it could be a product of large-scale falsifying of ages by people eager to collect social security. Also possible is that some of the earlier ages were understated out of vanity.

另一种转移话题的方式体现在参议员威廉·兰格的言论中：“我们甚至可以从阿尔卡特拉斯岛带走一名囚犯，让他住在华尔道夫酒店，费用反而更低……”这位北达科他州参议员指的是此前关于关押囚犯费用的报道——在阿尔卡特拉斯岛关押一名囚犯每天需花费8美元，这一数字“相当于旧金山一家高档酒店的房间费”。话题从总体维护成本被偷换成了单纯的酒店房间租金。

<!--en-->
Another kind of change-of-subject is represented by Senator William Langer's cry that "we could take a prisoner from Alcatraz and board him at the Waldorf-Astoria cheaper...." The North Dakotan was referring to earlier statements that it cost eight dollars a day to maintain a prisoner at Alcatraz, "the cost of a room at a good San Francisco hotel." The subject has been changed from total maintenance cost (Alcatraz) to hotel-room rent alone.

所谓“事后归因式”的牵强附会也是一种看似不经意实则刻意转移话题的手段。它将两件相关之事的关联歪曲为因果关系。《电气世界》杂志曾在题为《电力对美国的意义》的社论中展示了一张综合图表。从图中可以看出，随着“工厂中的电力马力”上升，“每小时平均工资”也随之提高；与此同时，“每周平均工时”却减少了。当然，这些都是长期趋势，根本没有证据表明它们之间存在因果关系。

<!--en-->
The *post hoc* variety of pretentious nonsense is another way of changing the subject without seeming to. The change of something *with* something else is presented as *because of*. The magazine *Electrical World* once offered a composite chart in an editorial on "What Electricity Means to America." You could see from it that as "electrical horsepower in factories" climbed, so did "average wages per hour." At the same time "average hours per week" dropped. All these things are long-time trends, of course, and there is no evidence at all that any one of them has produced any other.

还有那些喜欢自称“第一”的人。只要不挑剔具体领域，几乎任何人都能宣称自己在某些方面是“第一”。1952年底，两家纽约报纸都坚称自己在食品杂货广告领域排名第一。从某种意义上说，它们确实都对。其中，《世界电讯报》解释说它在全版广告方面排名第一——因为这种广告形式会出现在所有报纸副本中，也是该报唯一采用的广告形式。《美国日报》则强调总版面字数才是关键，并声称自己在这方面排名第一。这种追求绝对化的做法，甚至让电台气象员将普通的一天称为“自1949年以来最热的6月2日”。

<!--en-->
And then there are the firsters. Almost anybody can claim to be first in *something* if he is not too particular what it is. At the end of 1952 two New York newspapers were each insisting on first rank in grocery advertising.Both were right too, in a way. The *World-Telegram* went on to explain that it was first in full-run advertising, the kind that appears in all copies, which is the only kind it runs. The *Journal-American* insisted that total linage was what counted and that it was first in that. This is the kind of reaching for a superlative that leads the weather reporter on the radio to label a quite normal day “the hottest June second since 1949.”

当你考虑直接借款或分期付款时，转移话题的现象会让成本比较变得困难。6%听起来就是6%，但实际情况可能并非如此。

<!--en-->
Change-of-subject makes it difficult to compare cost when you contemplate borrowing money either directly or in the form of installment buying. Six per cent sounds like six per cent—but it may not be at all.

如果你从银行借100美元，年利率为6%，并在一年内按月等额还款，那么你为使用这笔资金所付出的代价约为3美元。但另一种被称为“100美元中收取6美元”的6%贷款利率，其实际成本却是前者的两倍。大多数汽车贷款正是按这种方式计算的。这非常复杂难懂。

<!--en-->
If you borrow $100 from a bank at six per cent interest and pay it back in equal monthly installments for a year, the price you pay for the use of the money is about $3. But another six per cent loan, on the basis sometimes called $6 on the $100, will cost you twice as much. That’s the way most automobile loans are figured. It is very tricky.

关键在于你并不能整整一年都拥有那100美元。六个月后你就已偿还了一半。如果按“100美元中收取6美元”即6%来计算利息，实际上你支付的利率接近12%。

<!--en-->
The point is that you don’t have the $100 for a year. By the end of six months you have paid back half of it. If you are charged at $6 on the $100, or six per cent of the amount, you really pay interest at nearly twelve per cent.

更糟糕的是1952年和1953年一些粗心大意购买冷冻食品计划的消费者所遭遇的情况。他们听到的利率标注为6%到12%不等。这听起来像利息，其实并非如此。这实际上是按本金直接计算的费用，最糟糕的是还款期往往只有六个月而非一年。这样一来，100美元在半年内分期偿还所产生的实际利率竟高达约48%。难怪会有那么多客户违约，那么多食品计划最终崩溃。

<!--en-->
Even worse was what happened to some careless purchasers of freezer-food plans in 1952 and 1953. They were quoted a figure of anywhere from six to twelve per cent. It sounded like interest, but it was not. It was an on-the-dollar figure and, worst of all, the time was often six months rather than a year. Now $12 on the $100 for money to be paid back regularly over half a year works out to something like forty-eight per cent real interest. It is no wonder that so many customers defaulted and so many food plans blew up.

有时人们会利用语义手段来转移话题。以下摘自《商业周刊》的一篇文章。

<!--en-->
Sometimes the semantic approach will be used to change the subject. Here is an item from *Business Week* magazine.

会计师们认为“盈余”是个不好的词。他们建议从公司资产负债表中删除这个词。美国会计师协会会计程序委员会指出：……应使用“留存收益”或“固定资产增值”等描述性术语。

<!--en-->
Accountants have decided that “surplus” is a nasty word. They propose eliminating it from corporate balance sheets. The Committee on Accounting Procedure of the American Institute of accountants says: ... Use such descriptive terms as “retained earnings” or “appreciation of fixed assets.”

这条来自一篇新闻报道，内容涉及标准石油公司创纪录的营收和每日百万美元的净利润。

<!--en-->
This one is from a newspaper story reporting Standard Oil’s record-breaking revenue and net profit of a million dollars a day.

或许董事会将来会考虑拆分股票，因为这样或许能带来某种优势……尤其是当每股利润看起来不那么可观时……

<!--en-->
Possibly the directors may be thinking some time of splitting the stock for there may be an advantage ... if the profits per share do not look so large....

## 这说得通吗？

<!--en-->
*Does It Make Sense?*

“这说得通吗？”当整个论述建立在未经证实的假设之上时，这句话往往能戳破统计数据的虚假本质。你或许熟悉鲁道夫·弗莱什的可读性公式——它试图通过单词和句子的长度等简单而客观的指标来衡量一篇散文的阅读难易程度。像所有试图将难以捉摸的事物量化为数字、用算术取代判断的工具一样，这个想法颇具吸引力。至少它吸引了那些雇佣作家的机构，比如报纸出版商，尽管许多作家本人并不买账。该公式的假设是：单词长度等因素决定了可读性。但说句难听的，这一点仍有待证明。

<!--en-->
"Does it make sense?" will often cut a statistic down to size when the whole rigmarole is based on an unproved assumption. You may be familiar with the Rudolf Flesch readability formula. It purports to measure how easy a piece of prose is to read, by such simple and objective items as length of words and sentences. Like all devices for reducing the imponderable to a number and substituting arithmetic for judgment, it is an appealing idea. At least it has appealed to people who employ writers, such as newspaper publishers, even if not to many writers themselves. The assumption in the formula is that such things as word length determine readability. This, to be ornery about it, remains to be proved.

一位名叫罗伯特·A·杜富尔的人用他手头的一些文学作品测试了弗莱什公式。结果显示，《睡谷传说》的阅读难度竟比《理想国》高出一半之多；辛克莱·刘易斯的小说《卡斯·廷伯莱恩》甚至被评定为比雅克·马里坦的文章《艺术的精神价值》更难读懂。真是荒谬至极。

<!--en-->
A man named Robert A. Dufour put the Flesch formula to trial on some literature that he found handy. It showed "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" to be half again as hard to read as Plato's Republic. The Sinclair Lewis novel *Cass Timberlane* was rated more difficult than an essay by Jacques Maritain, "The Spiritual Value of Art." A likely story.

许多统计数据从表面上看就是错误的。它们之所以能蒙混过关，只是因为数字的魔力让人暂时丧失了常识判断力。伦纳德·恩格尔在《哈珀斯杂志》的一篇文章中列举了几例医学领域的此类数据。

<!--en-->
Many a statistic is false on its face. It gets by only because the magic of numbers brings about a suspension of common sense. Leonard Engel, in a *Harper's* article, has listed a few of the medical variety.

例如，一位知名泌尿科医生计算出美国有八百万前列腺癌病例——这意味着每个处于易感年龄段的男性平均拥有1.1个癌变的前列腺！另一位著名神经科医生则估计每十二个美国人中就有一人患偏头痛；由于偏头痛占慢性头痛病例的三分之一，这意味着四分之一的美国人都会遭受严重头痛之苦。还有人常提到多发性硬化症病例数为25万；但死亡数据显示，这种致残性疾病的患者实际上不会超过三四万人。

<!--en-->
An example is the calculation of a well-known urologist that there are eight million cases of cancer of the prostate gland in the United States—which would be enough to provide 1.1 carcinomatous prostate glands for every male in the susceptible age group! Another is a prominent neurologist's estimate that one American in twelve suffers from migraine; since migraine is responsible for a third of chronic headache cases, this would mean that a quarter of us must suffer from disabling headaches. Still another is the figure of 250,000 often given for the number of multiple sclerosis cases; death data indicate that there can be, happily, no more than thirty to forty thousand cases of this paralytic disease in the country.

关于《社会保障法》修正案的听证会上，总会出现各种经不起细究的论调。其中一种说法是：由于人的预期寿命只有约六十三岁，因此设定六十五岁为退休年龄的社会保障计划纯属骗局——因为几乎所有人都在那之前就去世了。

<!--en-->
Hearings on amendments to the Social Security Act have been haunted byvarious forms of a statement that makes sense only when not looked at closely. It is an argument that goes like this: Since life expectancy is only about sixty-three years, it is a sham and a fraud to set up a social-security plan with a retirement age of sixty-five, because virtually everybody dies before that.

你只需看看周围认识的人就能反驳这种观点。不过其根本谬误在于：该数字指的是出生时的预期寿命，因此大约有一半的新生儿预计能活得更久。顺便提一下，这个数字来自最新的官方完整生命表，适用于1939年至1941年期间；最新的估算已将其修正为六十五岁以上。也许这会引出另一种同样荒谬的论点：现在几乎人人都能活到六十五岁。

<!--en-->
You can rebut that one by looking around at people you know. The basic fallacy, however, is that the figure refers to expectancy at birth, and so about half the babies born can expect to live longer than that. The figure, incidentally, is from the latest official complete life table and is correct for the 1939-1941 period. An up-to-date estimate corrects it to sixty-five-plus. Maybe that will produce a new and equally silly argument to the effect that practically everybody now lives to be sixty-five.

几年前，一家大型电器公司基于长期被视为理所当然的出生率下降趋势，展开了战后规划。计划重点开发小容量家电，比如适合公寓使用的冰箱。后来，其中一位规划人员突然恢复了常识：他暂时放下图表，发现他自己、同事、朋友、邻居以及前同学中，除少数例外，几乎都有三四个孩子或正打算要孩子。这一发现促使公司重新评估并调整策略——不久之后，公司便将重点转向更受多子女家庭青睐的大容量型号，并获得了丰厚利润。

<!--en-->
Postwar planning at a big electrical-appliance company was going great guns a few years ago on the basis of a declining birth rate, something that had been taken for granted for a long time. Plans called for emphasis on small-capacity appliances, apartment-size refrigerators. Then one of the planners had an attack of common sense: He came out of his graphs and charts long enough to notice that he and his co-workers and his friends and his neighbors and his former classmates with few exceptions either had three or four children or planned to. This led to some open-minded investigating and charting—and the company shortly turned its emphasis most profitably to big-family models.

那些看似精确得惊人的数字同样是违背常识的例证。纽约市报纸报道的一项研究称，与家人同住的职业女性每周需要40.13美元的收入才能维持生计。任何没有在阅读时完全丧失逻辑思维能力的人都会明白：维持基本生活的成本根本无法精确到分毫。但“40.13美元”听起来比“约40美元”显得更专业，因而具有极大的诱惑力。

<!--en-->
The impressively precise figure is something else that contradicts common sense. A study reported in New York City newspapers announced that a working woman living with her family needed a weekly pay check of $40.13 for adequate support. Anyone who has not suspended all logical processes while reading his paper will realize that the cost of keeping body and soul together cannot be calculated to the last cent. But there is a dreadful temptation; "$40.13" sounds so much more knowing than "about $40."

你同样有权对几年前美国石油工业委员会发布的报告持怀疑态度——该报告称汽车年均税费为51.13美元。

<!--en-->
You are entitled to look with the same suspicion on the report, some years ago, by the American Petroleum Industries Committee that the average yearly tax bill for automobiles is $51.13.

外推法很有用处，尤其是在被称为趋势预测的占卜形式中。但在查看这些数字或据此绘制的图表时，必须时刻牢记一点：当前的趋势可能是事实，但未来的趋势不过是经过推算的猜测而已。其隐含的前提是“其他条件不变”以及“现有趋势将持续下去”。然而事实上，其他条件从来都不会保持不变——否则生活将会索然无味。

<!--en-->
Extrapolations are useful, particularly in that form of soothsaying called forecasting trends. But in looking at the figures or the charts made from them, it is necessary to remember one thing constantly: The trend-to-now may be a fact, but the future trend represents no more than an educated guess. Implicit in it is "everything else being equal" and "present trends continuing." And somehow everything else refuses to remain equal, else life would be dull indeed.

若要见识一下无节制外推所带来的荒谬之处，不妨看看电视的发展趋势。从1947年到1952年，美国家庭中电视机的数量增加了约10,000%。若按此趋势推算未来五年，很快就会出现几十亿台电视机——天哪，或者每个家庭拥有四十台之多。如果你想更夸张些，可以选取比1947年更早的年份作为基准，这样就能“证明”每个家庭很快会拥有四万台而非四十台电视机。

<!--en-->
For a sample of the nonsense inherent in uncontrolled extrapolation, consider the trend of television. The number of sets in American homes increased around 10,000% from 1947 to 1952. Project this for the next five years and you find that there'll soon be a couple billion of the things, Heaven forbid, or forty sets per family. If you want to be even sillier, begin with a base year that is earlier in the television scheme of things than 1947 and you can just as well "prove" that each family will soon have not forty but forty thousand sets.

政府研究人员莫里斯·汉森称盖洛普在1948年的选举预测为“人类历史上最广为宣传的统计错误”。不过，与我们一些最常用的未来人口估算相比，这一预测反而堪称精准之典范；那些估算曾引发全国范围的嘲笑。早在1938年，一个由专家组成的总统委员会就认为美国人口永远无法达到1.4亿；而仅仅十二年后，实际人口便已超过这一数字。有些教科书出版时间尚近，至今仍在大学中使用，它们预测美国人口峰值不会超过1.5亿，且要到1980年左右才能达到该数值。这些严重的低估源于假设某种趋势会持续不变。一个世纪前类似的假设则走向了另一个极端：它假定1790年至1860年间的人口增长率会一直延续下去。亚伯拉罕·林肯在第二次致国会的咨文中预测，到1930年美国人口将达到251,689,914人。

<!--en-->
A Government research man, Morris Hansen, called Gallup's 1948 election forecasting "the most publicized statistical error in human history." It was a paragon of accuracy, however, compared with some of our most widely used estimates of future population, which have earned a nationwide horselaugh. As late as 1938 a presidential commission loaded with experts doubted that the U. S. population would ever reach 140 million; it was 12 million more than that just twelve years later. There are textbooks published so recently that they are still in college use that predict a peak population of not more than 150 million and figure it will take until about 1980 to reach it. These fearful underestimates came from assuming that a trend would continue without change. A similar assumption a century ago did as badly in the opposite direction because it assumed continuation of the population-increase rate of 1790 to 1860. In his second message to Congress, Abraham Lincoln predicted the U. S. population would reach 251,689,914 in 1930.

![图片](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b337d176424c6ea037acb5026325fc75.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=82a6665fbc5dcf20a2974bb3c0e17daacc6fcf5754888baf85a62d4757f6b469)

<!--en-->
![Image](https://easylink-easydoc-task.s3.oss-cn-shanghai.aliyuncs.com/public/b337d176424c6ea037acb5026325fc75.png?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=LTAI5t9E8h6okbJxhoCnJXq1%2F20261014%2Fcn-shanghai%2Fs3%2Faws4_request&X-Amz-Date=20261014T063901Z&X-Amz-Expires=3600&X-Amz-SignedHeaders=host&X-Amz-Signature=82a6665fbc5dcf20a2974bb3c0e17daacc6fcf5754888baf85a62d4757f6b469)

此后不久，即1874年，马克·吐温在《密西西比河上的生活》中总结了外推法带来的荒谬之处：

<!--en-->
Not long after that, in 1874, Mark Twain summed up the nonsense side of extrapolation in *Life on the Mississippi*:

在一百七十六年间，下密西西比河的长度缩短了242英里。平均下来，每年缩短略多于一又三分之一英里。因此，任何心智健全、既不瞎也不傻的人都能看出：就在明年11月满一百万年前的古奥陶纪时期，下密西西比河的长度竟然超过了130万英里，像一根钓竿一样伸进墨西哥湾。同理，任何人都能预见：七百四十二年后，下密西西比河的长度将只剩一又四分之三英里，开罗和新奥尔良的城市街道将会连为一体，在一位市长和一套共同议会的管辖下和谐共处。科学真是令人着迷——只需投入微不足道的事实，却能换来如此丰厚的猜测回报。

<!--en-->
In the space of one hundred and seventy-six years the Lower Mississippi has shortened itself two hundred and forty-two miles. That is an average of a trifle over one mile and a third per year. Therefore, any calm person, who is not blind or idiotic, can see that in the Old Oolitic Silurian Period, just a million years ago next November, the Lower Mississippi River was upward of one million three hundred thousand miles long, and stuck out over the Gulf of Mexico like a fishing-rod. And by the same token any person can see that seven hundred and forty-two years from now the Lower Mississippi will be only a mile and three-quarters long, and Cairo and New Orleans will have joined their streets together, and be plodding comfortably along under a single mayor and a mutual board of aldermen. There is something fascinating about science. One gets such wholesale returns of conjecture out of such a trifling investment of fact.

# 1

据说作家路易斯·布罗姆菲尔德在收到过多批评信而无法逐一回复时，总会用一句固定的话来应付。他既不承认任何观点，也不鼓励对方继续通信，但这句话几乎能让所有人满意。关键句子是：“你说的话或许有道理。”

<!--en-->
Author Louis Bromfield is said to have a stock reply to critical correspondents when his mail becomes too heavy for individual attention. Without conceding anything and without encouraging further correspondence, it still satisfies almost everyone. The key sentence: "There may be something in what you say."

这让我想起一位牧师，他因对受洗婴儿的美言而深受教区母亲们的欢迎。但当母亲们相互交流时，竟没人能记起他说了什么，只记得那是“动听的话”。后来才发现，他千篇一律的回应竟只是：“哇！这真是个可爱的宝宝啊！”（满脸笑容）

<!--en-->
It reminds me of the minister who achieved great popularity among mothers in his congregation by his flattering comments on babies brought in for christening. But when the mothers compared notes not one could remember what the man had said, only that it had been "something nice." Turned out his invariable remark was, "My!" (beaming) "This *is* a baby, isn't it!"
